concepts.title: Knapsack · 物品使用次数与一维状态更新

introduction.definition: 0/1 背包中每件物品最多选一次，完全背包允许同类物品重复使用。两者都可把容量作为状态，但一维压缩时必须防止错误复用当前物品。最少硬币数、最大价值、方案计数是不同目标，不能照搬同一递推的初始化。
introduction.example: 若递增更新却得到 6，说明同一件被用了两次；完全背包允许重复时 6 才合法。若目标改成“最少硬币数”，就应使用最小化递推和相应不可达值。

blocks.text: 最大价值状态 dp[c] 配合重量 w、价值 v，可尝试 \(dp[c]=\max(dp[c],dp[c-w]+v)\)。0/1 情形按容量递减，读取的仍是本轮物品加入之前的状态；完全背包按容量递增，允许读取本轮已更新的状态。精确装满问题要把不可达状态设为不可达，容量零再按目标初始化。
只有一件重量 2、价值 3 的物品，容量为 4。0/1 背包的价值最多为 3，若递增更新却得到 6，说明同一件被用了两次；完全背包允许重复时 6 才合法。若目标改成“最少硬币数”，就应使用最小化递推和相应不可达值。

worked.title: 0/1 Knapsack: Descending Capacity Prevents Reuse
worked.scenario: Item weights are [1,2,5], each usable once, and capacity is 4. Determine whether it can be filled exactly. Boolean dp[c] records whether processed items can sum to c.
steps: Initialize only dp[0] to true. For weight 1, scan capacities from 4 down to 1. Only 0 and 1 become reachable.
Process weight 2 in descending order. Capacities 0,1,2,3 are reachable. Capacity 4 reads dp[2] from before this item, so remains false.
Weight 5 exceeds capacity. An ascending scan would reuse weight 1 within one pass and incorrectly make every capacity reachable.
worked.result: Capacity 4 is unreachable. Time O(number of items × capacity), auxiliary space O(capacity). This is exact-fill reachability.
worked.pitfall: Unbounded knapsack permits repeated use of an item type and can use an ascending update order that allows reuse. Loop order expresses the usage constraint.
worked.question: What if the weights become [1,2,3]?
worked.answer: Yes: 1+3 fills capacity 4, still using each item only once.

depth.boundary: With items in the outer loop, 0/1 capacities are usually traversed backward and unbounded capacities forward. Also distinguish counting from optimization.

introduction.definition: Activation checkpointing avoids saving every intermediate activation and recomputes some during backpropagation, trading extra computation for GPU memory. A model checkpoint instead saves model or training state for recovery or deployment. Both use the word checkpoint, but solve different problems. Gradient accumulation, parameter sharding and freezing some parameters can also reduce GPU memory use, each with computational or capability tradeoffs.
introduction.example:
A network has four segments, each needing about 100 MB of saved intermediate activations. Training may face interruption or insufficient GPU memory.
Disk snapshots support recovery. Activation recomputation reduces part of training memory use. Both can be used together.

exercise.question: If optimizer state is large, does activation checkpointing remove it?
exercise.answer: No. It targets intermediate activations; optimizer state needs a separate storage or sharding strategy.

blocks.text: Activation checkpointing avoids saving every intermediate activation and recomputes some during backpropagation, trading extra computation for GPU memory. A model checkpoint instead saves model or training state for recovery or deployment. Both use the word checkpoint, but solve different problems. Gradient accumulation, parameter sharding and freezing some parameters can also reduce GPU memory use, each with computational or capability tradeoffs.

worked.title: Two Checkpoints: Saving State and Recomputing Activations
worked.scenario: A network has four segments, each needing about 100 MB of saved intermediate activations. Training may face interruption or insufficient GPU memory.
steps: A recovery checkpoint saves model, optimizer, scheduler and training step count, plus random state and data progress when needed. It writes mainly to persistent storage.
Activation checkpointing retains selected boundary activations and recomputes some forward operations during backpropagation, trading time for activation memory.
Retaining two segment boundaries may reduce intermediate storage, but boundary tensors, inputs, temporary tensors and other states still count. An exact 50% memory reduction cannot be assumed.
worked.result: Disk snapshots support recovery. Activation recomputation reduces part of training memory use. Both can be used together.
worked.pitfall: Model weights alone usually do not support an exact training resume. Activation checkpointing does not automatically save a resumable run.
worked.question: If optimizer state is large, does activation checkpointing remove it?
worked.answer: No. It targets intermediate activations; optimizer state needs a separate storage or sharding strategy.

depth.boundary: This differs from saving a model checkpoint for recovery.

introduction.definition: AdaGrad scales each parameter’s update using its past gradients. This is useful for sparse features, but cumulative statistics can make effective step sizes increasingly small. RMSProp uses moving averages of recent squared gradients to limit that continual decay. These are adaptive step-size methods: parameters can receive different effective update scales. Adaptive does not mean that the learning rate needs no tuning or that validation is unnecessary.
introduction.example: 例子：当前梯度为 2，AdaGrad 既有平方梯度和为 5，学习率 0.1，忽略 ε 时本次更新幅度为 0.2/√9≈0.0667。若 RMSProp 的衰减为 0.9、旧均方为 1，则新均方为 0.9×1+0.1×4=1.3。两种方法保存历史的方式不同。

exercise.question: 用自己的话解释：上面的情景为什么是“Adagrad / RMSProp”的例子？请指出定义中的关键条件在情景里如何体现，而不是只复述最后的数值。

introduction.definition: Adam combines a moving average of gradients with statistics of squared gradients, giving both momentum and per-parameter scaling. Its beta parameters control how long past information is retained. Epsilon is a small numerical stabilizer, not an exploration probability. Check the context when the same parameter name appears in different algorithms. Adam is convenient for many deep learning tasks but is not universally the best optimizer in theory or practice.
introduction.example:
Use the simplified decoupled update θ_next=(1-ηλ)θ-ηg for shrinkage and gradient updates, with θ=2, η=0.1, λ=0.01 and g=0.4.
Weight decay shrinks parameters during an update; learning-rate decay describes how η changes over time. Their numerical effects interact because shrinkage contains ηλ.

exercise.question: If g=0, can weight decay still update the parameter?
exercise.answer: Yes. If ηλ is nonzero and decay applies to that parameter, the equation still performs θ←(1-ηλ)θ.

worked.title: Weight Decay and Learning-Rate Decay: Different Controls
worked.scenario: Use the simplified decoupled update θ_next=(1-ηλ)θ-ηg for shrinkage and gradient updates, with θ=2, η=0.1, λ=0.01 and g=0.4.
steps: The shrinkage factor is 0.999, giving the shrunk parameter 1.998.
The gradient term is 0.04, giving 1.958 after the update. With λ=0, the same step gives 1.96.
Reducing the next step’s learning rate to 0.01 changes the schedule for η. λ still sets parameter shrinkage strength.
worked.result: Weight decay shrinks parameters during an update; learning-rate decay describes how η changes over time. Their numerical effects interact because shrinkage contains ηλ.
worked.pitfall: Here g denotes the update direction. Actual AdamW adjusts gradients using momentum and second-moment statistics, so this direction is not simply the raw gradient.
worked.question: If g=0, can weight decay still update the parameter?
worked.answer: Yes. If ηλ is nonzero and decay applies to that parameter, the equation still performs θ←(1-ηλ)θ.

depth.boundary: AdamW changes how weight decay is applied; it is not simply a faster version of Adam.

introduction.definition: A fixed workflow arranges major steps such as retrieval, generation and review in advance. An agent loop chooses the next tool or action from current results. ReAct alternates reasoning, action and observation. More autonomous decisions do not necessarily improve reliability. Repeated tasks often suit fixed processes, while open-ended tasks require more dynamic choices. Both can be combined without turning the whole system into an unconstrained loop.
introduction.example: 例子：固定工作流总是先检索、再写答案；一个受限智能体先检索，发现缺少日期后选择再次查原文，证据齐全才生成答案。允许的工具、最大调用数和停止条件必须事先明确；它不能把网页中的指令当成用户授权。

introduction.definition: An API, or application programming interface, defines the capabilities that a system exposes. Think of it as a restaurant menu: callers know what they can order without knowing how the kitchen works. An SDK supplies development tools and wrappers for a platform. A framework often controls the overall application flow; a library supplies functionality that the application actively calls, though the distinction is not always strict.
introduction.example: 例子：GET /orders/42 返回订单 42 的状态。调用者只需知道路径、字段和错误约定，不必知道服务器用哪种数据库。若状态查询失败，API 应区分“订单不存在”和“服务暂不可用”，不能都返回一段看似成功的空数据。

introduction.definition: Intuitively, a query represents what the current position seeks, keys provide matching clues at other positions, and values contain the information to aggregate. Attention scores determine aggregation weights after normalization. This is an analogy: queries, keys and values are learned vectors, not human-written questions, catalogs and answers. A high attention weight does not automatically establish interpretable causal importance to the final output.
introduction.example:
Query q=[1,0], keys [1,0], [0,1], [1,1], and values [2,0], [0,2], [1,1]. Key dimension is 2.
Attention outputs a weighted combination of values; query–key matching determines the weights. Lower temperature concentrates these unequal-score weights more strongly.

exercise.question: If two keys have equal scores, must they have equal weights?
exercise.answer: Under the same query and mask conditions, their softmax weights are equal. Their value vectors may still differ.

worked.title: Attention: Scores, Normalization and Weighted Sums
worked.scenario: Query q=[1,0], keys [1,0], [0,1], [1,1], and values [2,0], [0,2], [1,1]. Key dimension is 2.
steps: Dot products are [1,0,1]. Dividing by √2 gives approximately [.707,0,.707]. The demo temperature defaults to 1.
Softmax subtracts the maximum score before exponentiation, giving weights approximately [.4011,.1978,.4011], summing to 1.
The weighted value sum is approximately [1.2033,.7967]. Masking the third key gives it weight 0 and renormalizes the other weights.
worked.result: Attention outputs a weighted combination of values; query–key matching determines the weights. Lower temperature concentrates these unequal-score weights more strongly.
worked.pitfall: This is scaled dot-product attention for one query, one head and no dropout. The extra temperature control is a teaching device. Masking all keys requires separately defined behavior.
worked.question: If two keys have equal scores, must they have equal weights?
worked.answer: Under the same query and mask conditions, their softmax weights are equal. Their value vectors may still differ.

worked.title: KV Cache: Which Computations Are Reused?
worked.scenario: During causal autoregressive decoding, four tokens have already been processed. Now process the fifth token to predict the sixth. Keys and values for the first four tokens are cached separately at each layer.
steps: Reuse the first four tokens’ cached K and V instead of recomputing their projections. Compute Q, K and V for the fifth token and append its K and V to the cache.
The fifth token’s query attends to the visible keys for tokens 1…5 and weights their values. Its final representation predicts the sixth token. This attention work still grows with prefix length.
Suppose each token stores 2 groups of d values, each b bytes. For L layers, T tokens and batch size B, simplified memory use is 2BLTdb.
worked.result: Before processing the fifth token, B=1, L=2, T=4, d=8 and b=2 give 256 bytes of cached values. Here d is the total cached key width per layer, with the same width assumed for values. After appending the fifth token, the same formula gives 320 bytes.
worked.pitfall: GQA/MQA, quantization, paging and framework metadata change real memory use. KV caching and FlashAttention optimize different aspects of inference.
worked.question: What happens when length doubles under this simplified cache formula?
worked.answer: Cache size doubles. This does not establish that total inference time exactly doubles.

depth.boundary: Attention weights do not automatically provide a causal explanation.

introduction.definition: Backtracking expands choices into a search tree: choose, explore recursively, then undo the choice on return. Permutations use a used marker so each element is chosen once. Subsets use an increasing start index so different selection orders do not enumerate the same set repeatedly. Define the state first, then choose used markers, a starting index, or a remaining target.
introduction.example: If you only save a reference to the same mutable list, undoing it later will change all answers together. Backtracking is not an antonym of dynamic programming; memoization is also possible when different search paths have the same subsequent state.

blocks.text: Copying the current path is usually required when adding it to an answer. If you only save a reference to the same mutable list, undoing it later will change all answers together. Backtracking is not an antonym of dynamic programming; memoization is also possible when different search paths have the same subsequent state.

worked.title: Backtracking: Choose, Recurse and Undo
worked.scenario: Enumerate permutations of [1,2,3]. path stores the current sequence; used marks selected positions.
steps: Choose 1, then 2 and 3, obtaining [1,2,3]. Save a copy of the path.
Undo 3 and then 2; choose 3 followed by 2 to obtain [1,3,2]. Undo these choices and continue with other starting elements.
At depth 3, save the result and return. Every choice needs a matching undo so sibling branches start from the same state.
worked.result: There are 6 permutations. The output itself requires Θ(n×n!) time and space. Recursion and marks use O(n) auxiliary space, excluding output.
worked.pitfall: Saving the mutable path reference can make every final result identical. With duplicate input values, marking positions still produces repeated value permutations, requiring deduplication.
worked.question: Does an empty array have 0 permutations or 1?
worked.answer: By combinatorial convention it has 1: the empty permutation, represented by [[]]. This is also the natural recursion base case.

depth.boundary: Pruning depends on the problem constraints, and enumeration cost is also bounded below by the output size.

introduction.definition: Batch size is the number of samples processed together in a forward pass. Microbatch size can differ from the total number contributing to one parameter update.
introduction.example: A microbatch of 8, accumulated over 4 passes on 2 workers, contributes 64 sample presentations to an update. Memory use for one forward pass is still tied mainly to the microbatch, not to storing all 64 activations at once.

exercise.question: 用自己的话解释：上面的情景为什么是“Batch Size”的例子？请指出定义中的关键条件在情景里如何体现，而不是只复述最后的数值。

exercise.evidence: A microbatch of 8, accumulated over 4 passes on 2 workers, contributes 64 sample presentations to an update. Memory use for one forward pass is still tied mainly to the microbatch, not to storing all 64 activations at once.

blocks.text: With equal-sized microbatches of size B, accumulation over A steps and D data-parallel workers gives effective batch size BAD when gradients are combined consistently and workers see the intended samples. This identity does not make all optimization dynamics equivalent.

depth.boundary: Distinguish between per-device micro-batches and global effective batches.

introduction.definition: Batch normalization uses minibatch statistics to normalize intermediate activations, then applies learnable parameters to preserve expressive capacity. It is common in convolutional networks. Very small training batches or large differences between devices’ batches can make the statistics unstable. Inference usually uses running statistics accumulated during training, rather than statistics from the current individual sample. Incorrect training or evaluation modes can therefore change outputs unexpectedly.
introduction.example: 例子：一条记录的特征为 (1,3)，按这两个特征计算的均值是 2、方差是 1，忽略 ε 和仿射变换时 LayerNorm 输出 (−1,1)；RMSNorm 用均方根 √5 缩放，输出 (1/√5,3/√5)。BatchNorm 则沿批次等规定轴取统计量，不能直接沿同一轴替换。

introduction.definition: BCE is commonly used for binary classification and for each label in multilabel learning. It compares predicted probabilities with target labels, rather than merely counting correct class decisions. Think of it as scoring probability predictions: the less probability assigned to the true answer, the greater the penalty.
introduction.example: Consider an email that is actually spam. Model A assigns a 49% probability of spam; model B assigns only 1%. With a 50% classification threshold, both are wrong, so accuracy cannot distinguish these errors. But model B almost rules out the true answer and is more confidently wrong, so BCE penalizes it more. Probability prediction quality and the final hard classification are different things.

exercise.question: 用自己的话解释：上面的情景为什么是“BCE — Binary Cross-Entropy”的例子？请指出定义中的关键条件在情景里如何体现，而不是只复述最后的数值。

blocks.text: In multilabel image recognition, the model can separately predict whether an image contains a cat, a dog or a car, then combine the BCE losses for those labels. Separate loss terms do not imply that the labels are independent in the real world; a shared network can still use their correlations. If exactly one of cat, dog or bird must be chosen, model the classes as mutually exclusive instead.

worked.title: BCE: Same Classification Error, Different Loss
worked.scenario: The true label is y=1 and the model assigns positive-class probability p. At a fixed threshold of 0.5, compare p=0.49 with p=0.01.
steps: For y=1, BCE=-ln(p). p=0.49 gives about 0.71335; p=0.01 gives about 4.60517.
Both hard predictions are negative, but the latter assigns less probability to the true class and incurs about 6.46 times the loss.
For y=0, loss becomes -ln(1-p). The same probability 0.01 is now a correct, confident prediction.
worked.result: Loss scores probability predictions, not the number of 0/1 errors. The demo restricts probabilities to (0,1); logarithmic divergence at the endpoints is separate.
worked.pitfall: BCEWithLogitsLoss accepts raw logits: do not apply Sigmoid first. The demo displays probability and its corresponding logit, and computes the equivalent single-sample BCE.
worked.question: At p=0.5, do both labels give the same loss?
worked.answer: Yes: both give ln(2)≈0.69315.

depth.boundary: Used for binary classification and per-label multilabel tasks; it measures more than thresholded correctness.

introduction.definition: BCELoss expects probabilities as input. BCEWithLogitsLoss accepts raw logits and combines sigmoid with BCE internally. This fused computation improves numerical stability by avoiding problems caused by first forming extreme probabilities. Do not apply sigmoid separately before BCEWithLogitsLoss. You need not memorize the API for an interview, but should understand that WithLogits means scores before the probability transformation.

introduction.definition: Breadth-first search uses a queue to explore nodes one step away before those two steps away. When every edge has the same cost, it therefore finds a path with the fewest steps. Depth-first search uses recursion or an explicit stack to follow a path deeply and backtrack when needed. It suits dependency analysis, connectivity structure, and backtracking. Finding a path with DFS does not mean finding a shortest path. Both searches must track visited states to avoid looping indefinitely around cycles.
introduction.example:
A directed graph has equal-cost edges A→B, A→C, B→D, C→D and D→E. F is isolated. Find the fewest edges from A.
One shortest path from A to E is A-B-D-E, of length 3. F is unreachable. With adjacency lists, time is O(V+E) and space is O(V).

exercise.question: If A→C has cost 10, does BFS still guarantee minimum total cost?
exercise.answer: No. Minimizing edge count and total cost are different objectives. Dijkstra is an option for nonnegative weights.

worked.title: BFS: Mark on Enqueue to Find Shortest Paths
worked.scenario: A directed graph has equal-cost edges A→B, A→C, B→D, C→D and D→E. F is isolated. Find the fewest edges from A.
steps: Set A’s distance to 0. When it is dequeued, mark and enqueue B and C, both at distance 1.
B discovers D at distance 2 with parent B. When C encounters D, its existing mark prevents a duplicate enqueue.
D discovers E at distance 3. The queue eventually empties; F never receives a distance. Reverse the parent chain E→D→B→A to recover a path.
worked.result: One shortest path from A to E is A-B-D-E, of length 3. F is unreachable. With adjacency lists, time is O(V+E) and space is O(V).
worked.pitfall: The conclusion requires equal edge costs. General weighted paths cannot be compared by layer count alone. Marking only on dequeue allows duplicate enqueues.
worked.question: If A→C has cost 10, does BFS still guarantee minimum total cost?
worked.answer: No. Minimizing edge count and total cost are different objectives. Dijkstra is an option for nonnegative weights.

worked.title: 0–1 BFS: First Discovery Need Not Be Shortest
worked.scenario: Directed edges are A→B=1, A→C=0 and C→B=0. Find the minimum cost from A to B.
steps: Processing A tentatively sets B=1 and pushes it to the back, then sets C=0 and pushes it to the front.
Process C first. Edge C→B gives cost 0, improving on 1. Update B and push it to the front.
B’s final distance is 0 along A-C-B. Its two edges cost less than the direct one-edge route.
worked.result: 0–1 BFS relaxes edges whenever distance improves. Ordinary equal-weight BFS marking rules cannot be copied unchanged.
worked.pitfall: Treating “already enqueued” as “never update” incorrectly leaves B=1. The deque rule also does not extend unchanged to weight 2.
worked.question: If all three edges have weight 1, what is the minimum cost?
worked.answer: 1. Direct A→B is shortest, and ordinary BFS is sufficient.

depth.boundary: BFS finds paths with the fewest edges. These need not have minimum total cost when edge weights differ.

applications.title: Multi-source BFS · 等时传播与最近源距离
applications.reason: BFS 的队列和分层原理只保留基础入口；这里补充多起点初始化和传播时间。

introduction.definition: Binary classification answers a yes/no question, such as whether an email is spam. Multiclass single-label classification chooses one of several mutually exclusive answers, such as cat, dog, or bird as the main species. Multilabel classification allows several answers simultaneously, such as both cats and dogs in an image. It usually assigns each label a separate probability without requiring them to sum to one. This distinction directly affects the output layer and loss; class count alone cannot determine whether BCE or mutually exclusive categorical cross-entropy is appropriate.
introduction.example: 例子：邮件是否垃圾是二分类；把一张图只归为猫、狗、鸟之一是多类单标签；同一图片同时标注“猫”和“室内”是多标签。最后一种允许多个真标签，不能直接强制所有类别概率像单标签 softmax 那样总和为 1。

concepts.title: BM25 / HNSW · 文本与向量检索的索引应用

introduction.definition: BM25 是按词项统计给文档打分的检索方法，通常由倒排索引找候选；HNSW 是组织近似最近邻搜索的分层图索引，可用于向量检索。一个定义打分口径，一个组织搜索过程，不能因为都用于检索就视为同一种算法。
introduction.example: 检索产品编号 ZX-17 时，词项精确匹配往往很有用；检索“忘记密码怎么办”与“账户登录恢复”时，可另外利用向量相似性召回。无论采用哪种索引，最终都应在同一已标注查询集上比较召回与延迟，再决定是否合并候选，不能只凭方法名称判断优劣。

exercise.question: 用自己的话解释：上面的情景为什么是“BM25 / HNSW · 文本与向量检索的索引应用”的例子？请指出定义中的关键条件在情景里如何体现，而不是只复述最后的数值。

blocks.text: BM25 的一类常见写法对查询词累加 \(\operatorname{IDF}(w)f_w(k_1+1)/(f_w+k_1(1-b+b|D|/\operatorname{avgdl}))\)，f_w 为文档内词频，|D| 为文档长度，k₁ 控制词频饱和，b 控制长度调整；IDF 版本须固定。HNSW 另需规定距离、图连接数和搜索宽度，扩大搜索通常增加成本，不能保证每次返回精确最近邻。

worked.title: RRF: Fuse Ranks Instead of Adding Raw Scores
worked.scenario: Keyword retrieval ranks A,B,C; vector retrieval ranks C,B,D. A document contributes 1/(k+rank) from each list, with ranks starting at 1.
steps: At k=60, A receives 1/61 and D receives 1/63. B receives 2/62.
C receives 1/63+1/61≈0.032266, slightly above B≈0.032258.
Merge all documents that appear and sort by the fused score. A document absent from a list contributes 0 from that list.
worked.result: The final order is C,B,A,D. Rank fusion avoids directly adding BM25 raw scores and similarity scores on different scales.
worked.pitfall: RRF scores are not probabilities. Deduplicate each retrieval list first. The parameter k is not the number of results returned.
worked.question: What happens if only one retrieval list remains?
worked.answer: The fused order matches that list, because 1/(k+rank) decreases as rank increases.

depth.boundary: An index cannot compensate for an unsuitable vector representation.

introduction.definition: Boosting 把多个较简单的模型逐步组合起来。后续模型针对当前组合尚未处理好的部分作修正，而不是每个模型都独立完成全部任务。
introduction.example: 真实数值是 10，当前模型预测 7。平方误差情形下，新模型可以学习剩余差值 3；若只加入一半修正，组合预测变成 8.5。

exercise.question: 每增加一棵树都能降低训练误差，是否就一定改善新数据上的预测？
exercise.answer: 不一定。模型也可能开始拟合训练噪声，应查看独立验证表现；训练目标改善和泛化改善是两个问题。

blocks.text: Gradient boosting adds models sequentially to improve the current ensemble. With squared error, a new tree can be understood as predicting unexplained residuals; with other losses, fitting negative loss gradients is more accurate. GBDT uses decision trees as gradient-boosting base learners. Each round adds a correction rather than training a wholly independent complete model.

The learning rate controls each new tree's contribution; tree count controls the number of rounds. Smaller contributions often require more rounds to reach a given training error, so consider both together. Maximum depth and leaf count constrain each correction's complexity. Training corrections do not guarantee improvement on validation every round, so early stopping is common.

depth.boundary: Boosting methods cannot all be described as fitting the same type of residual.

applications.title: Gradient Boosted Trees · 梯度提升树的金融应用
applications.reason: 将提升法连接到金融标签的逐轮拟合，强调损失、学习率、时间验证和交易映射。

introduction.definition: 统计自举（bootstrap）从已有样本中有放回地重抽样，用重抽样结果估计统计量的抽样变化。随机森林还用自举训练不同树；某棵树未抽到的原样本称为该树的袋外样本（OOB）。它与逐段解利率曲线的“自举”是不同方法。
introduction.example: 原样本为 A、B、C、D，一次自举可能抽到 A、A、D、B，C 是这次的 OOB。用多个重抽样均值的标准差估计均值的不确定性；OOB 预测则只汇总未训练过该观测的树，不能把训练过它的树也加进来。

exercise.question: 用自己的话解释：上面的情景为什么是“Bootstrap / OOB”的例子？请指出定义中的关键条件在情景里如何体现，而不是只复述最后的数值。

blocks.text: 从 n 个独立同分布观测中抽 n 次，一个指定观测未被抽中的概率为 $(1-1/n)^n\to e^{-1}$。每次重抽样得到统计量 $\hat\theta^{*(b)}$，用 B 次结果的分布近似其抽样不确定性。金融时间序列有依赖时，通常需要区块等保留依赖的重抽样，不能直接打散日期。

depth.boundary: Out-of-bag evaluation does not replace appropriate temporal or group-based validation.

distinctions.title: Yield Curve Bootstrapping · 收益率曲线自举
distinctions.reason: 统计自举通过有放回重抽样估计不确定性；曲线自举按工具现金流逐段解折现因子。“自举”同名，算法与输出不同。

introduction.definition: Broadcasting aligns tensor dimensions so an elementwise operation can apply to compatible shapes without explicitly copying a smaller input along every dimension.
introduction.example: Adding shapes [3,1] and [1,4] produces [3,4]. Adding [3] and [4] fails because the trailing dimensions are unequal and neither is 1. An unintended but valid broadcast can silently produce the wrong computation.

exercise.question: 用自己的话解释：上面的情景为什么是“Broadcasting”的例子？请指出定义中的关键条件在情景里如何体现，而不是只复述最后的数值。
exercise.definition: Broadcasting aligns tensor dimensions so an elementwise operation can apply to compatible shapes without explicitly copying a smaller input along every dimension.
exercise.evidence: Adding shapes [3,1] and [1,4] produces [3,4]. Adding [3] and [4] fails because the trailing dimensions are unequal and neither is 1. An unintended but valid broadcast can silently produce the wrong computation.

blocks.text: Compare dimensions from the trailing axis: they must be equal or one must be 1; missing leading dimensions act as 1. The output uses the larger size on each aligned dimension. Broadcasting is a shape rule, independent of arithmetic precision.

depth.boundary: A valid broadcast can still compute the wrong quantity.

introduction.definition: 概率校准检查预测概率与长期实际频率是否一致：一批被预测为 0.8 的事件，应约有 80% 发生。校准改善的是概率含义；它与为了匹配期权报价而反求定价模型参数的校准不同。
introduction.example: 若在独立校准数据支持下调整为 0.6，同样这组标签的得分为 0.24；仍须用新测试样本评价。

exercise.question: 用自己的话解释：上面的情景为什么是“Calibration”的例子？请指出定义中的关键条件在情景里如何体现，而不是只复述最后的数值。
exercise.definition: 概率校准检查预测概率与长期实际频率是否一致：一批被预测为 0.8 的事件，应约有 80% 发生。校准改善的是概率含义；它与为了匹配期权报价而反求定价模型参数的校准不同。

blocks.text: 二元标签 $y_i\in\{0,1\}$、预测概率 pᵢ 时，$\mathrm{Brier}=n^{-1}\sum_i(p_i-y_i)^2$，越小越好，但它同时受区分能力等因素影响，不是纯校准误差。可靠性图比较各概率组的平均预测与实际频率。校准器要在适当留出集拟合，测试标签不能参与调整。
100 个样本都预测 0.8，实际发生 60 次，说明该组过度自信；其 Brier 为 (60×0.2²+40×0.8²)/100=0.28。若在独立校准数据支持下调整为 0.6，同样这组标签的得分为 0.24；仍须用新测试样本评价。

depth.boundary: A high AUC does not guarantee well-calibrated probabilities.

applications.reason: 在通用概率校准基础上，连接金融方向标签、非对称支付、成本与独立的时间校准段。

distinctions.reason: 概率校准比较预测概率与实际频率；定价模型校准选择匹配市场价格的参数。它们的目标和评价数据不同。

introduction.definition: The difficulty with anagram grouping is not how to append the list, but constructing the same keys for the same class of objects. The sorted character sequence can be used as the key; when the question is limited to lowercase English letters, the twenty-six character count can also be used as the key. For example, the character order of eat and tea is different, but the frequency array is the same. This idea is called normalized representation: eliminating unimportant order differences.
introduction.example: For example, the character order of eat and tea is different, but the frequency array is the same. This idea is called normalized representation: eliminating unimportant order differences.

blocks.text: Keys must be unambiguous. Do not concatenate multiple counts into a number string without separation, otherwise different counts may result in the same string. Sorting keys incur additional character sorting costs; counting keys for a fixed alphabet can be constructed linearly based on the total number of characters, but the twenty-six position premise cannot be directly generalized to all character sets.

depth.boundary: Character counts can identify anagrams. Composite keys must encode those counts unambiguously.

introduction.definition: A checkpoint saves training state. Model weights alone are usually sufficient for inference. Resuming training faithfully may also require optimizer state, scheduler progress, random-number-generator state and the data-loading position. A random seed helps control initialization and data shuffling, but hardware differences and nondeterministic operations can still change results. Reproducibility concerns the whole process, not just recording a seed.
introduction.example:
A network has four segments, each needing about 100 MB of saved intermediate activations. Training may face interruption or insufficient GPU memory.
Disk snapshots support recovery. Activation recomputation reduces part of training memory use. Both can be used together.

exercise.question: If optimizer state is large, does activation checkpointing remove it?
exercise.answer: No. It targets intermediate activations; optimizer state needs a separate storage or sharding strategy.

Resuming training faithfully may also require optimizer state, scheduler progress, random-number-generator state and the data-loading position. A random seed helps control initialization and data shuffling, but hardware differences and nondeterministic operations can still change results. Reproducibility concerns the whole process, not just recording a seed.

worked.title: Two Checkpoints: Saving State and Recomputing Activations
worked.scenario: A network has four segments, each needing about 100 MB of saved intermediate activations. Training may face interruption or insufficient GPU memory.
steps: A recovery checkpoint saves model, optimizer, scheduler and training step count, plus random state and data progress when needed. It writes mainly to persistent storage.
Activation checkpointing retains selected boundary activations and recomputes some forward operations during backpropagation, trading time for activation memory.
Retaining two segment boundaries may reduce intermediate storage, but boundary tensors, inputs, temporary tensors and other states still count. An exact 50% memory reduction cannot be assumed.
worked.result: Disk snapshots support recovery. Activation recomputation reduces part of training memory use. Both can be used together.
worked.pitfall: Model weights alone usually do not support an exact training resume. Activation checkpointing does not automatically save a resumable run.
worked.question: If optimizer state is large, does activation checkpointing remove it?
worked.answer: No. It targets intermediate activations; optimizer state needs a separate storage or sharding strategy.

depth.boundary: Weights alone usually do not support exact continuation, and seeds do not guarantee identical results across environments.

introduction.definition: 并发表示多个任务在重叠的时间段内推进；并行表示多个任务在同一时刻实际执行。
introduction.example: 一个厨师轮流照看两口锅，是并发；两个厨师各自同时炒菜，可以是并行。轮流推进并不要求真正同时执行。

exercise.question: 单核处理器在两个程序之间快速切换，属于并发还是一定属于并行？
exercise.answer: 属于并发，不能仅凭快速切换认定并行。是否同时执行还要看执行资源与具体任务。

blocks.text: The basic execution unit of a computer is the CPU, or central processing unit. CPUs are good at logical decisions, sequential execution, and complex control flow. GPUs, or graphics processing units, are good at performing many similar computations at once. Matrix operations in deep learning are highly parallel, making GPUs a major platform for training and inference. A GPU is not faster than a CPU at everything; its advantage depends on suitable workloads and enough data parallelism.

Concurrency means organizing tasks so they can make progress over overlapping periods. Their execution may be interleaved on one core or run in parallel on multiple cores. Parallelism means that computations actually execute simultaneously. Asynchronous execution means that, after starting an operation that may require waiting, the program can do other work and handle the result later. Multithreading and asynchronous execution are not equivalent; an asynchronous program can run on a single thread.

worked.title: CPU and GPU: Account for Work That Cannot Speed Up
worked.scenario: A program takes 100 seconds. A GPU can accelerate 80 seconds of work by 10×; the other 20 seconds remain unchanged. Initially ignore transfer overhead.
steps: The accelerated portion falls from 80 seconds to 8, giving 28 seconds in total.
Overall speedup is 100/28≈3.57, not 10.
Even eliminating all 80 seconds leaves 20 seconds, limiting speedup to 5×. Real transfers and scheduling also affect the result.
worked.result: Amdahl’s law shows why an individual kernel’s speedup must be assessed in the context of end-to-end runtime.
worked.pitfall: The analysis assumes fixed workload and accelerated fraction. Larger batches or another algorithm can change that fraction and require fresh measurement.
worked.question: If only 10% of time can be accelerated, what is the limit even at infinite speed?

depth.boundary: Asynchrony describes waiting and control flow and is not equivalent to parallelism.

introduction.definition: Metric learning studies similarity in a representation space. Contrastive loss brings related representations closer while separating unrelated ones. Triplet loss uses an anchor, a positive sample and a negative sample, aiming to place the positive closer to the anchor than the negative. InfoNCE often frames learning as finding the correct match among a batch of candidates. These ideas support image–text alignment, semantic retrieval and face verification. Negative samples may actually be related to the anchor; such false negatives create misleading training pressure.
introduction.example: 例子：同一图片的两种增强是正对，另一图片为负对。若使用 triplet 形式 max(0,d(a,p)−d(a,n)+m)，距离分别为 0.2、0.5，间隔 m=0.4，则损失为 0.1。这里 d 是规定的距离，减小正对距离或增加负对距离都可能降低损失。

introduction.example: 把计算想成厨房：主厨处理点单、调整步骤；很多帮厨同时切同样大小的土豆。这个比喻对应不同的分工，不表示 GPU 可以自动把任何程序变快。

exercise.answer: 不一定。可以同时进行的工作不足时，额外的人需要等待，协调也有成本。GPU 的优势依赖足够多、适合并行的工作。

introduction.definition: Cross-entropy is not an alternative to BCE: BCE is cross-entropy for the binary case. In training code, CrossEntropyLoss commonly accepts raw scores for multiple classes and performs the appropriate normalization internally. A typical task has one correct class per sample. Next-token prediction uses the same kind of classification objective over the vocabulary. Negative log-likelihood, or NLL, penalizes a model for assigning low likelihood to observed data. Cross-entropy for discrete classification is closely related to NLL, but likelihood-based objectives are not limited to classification.
introduction.example:
Logits are [1000,1001,999], with the second class correct. Calculate probabilities and multiclass cross-entropy.
Stable computation uses an algebraically equivalent transformation rather than arbitrary logit clipping. Training code commonly uses a cross-entropy interface accepting raw scores.

exercise.question: What if 500 is added to every logit?
exercise.answer: Mathematically, nothing changes. A stable implementation still subtracts the maximum first to avoid unnecessarily large intermediate values.

worked.title: Softmax: Shift Before Exponentiating
worked.scenario: Logits are [1000,1001,999], with the second class correct. Calculate probabilities and multiclass cross-entropy.
steps: Direct exponentiation can overflow. Subtract the maximum 1001 to obtain [-1,0,-2], without changing Softmax.
Exponentials are approximately [.367879,1,.135335]. Normalization gives probabilities [.244728,.665241,.090031].
Cross-entropy for the true class is -ln(.665241)≈.407606. Adding a constant to all logits preserves relative scores and these probabilities.
worked.result: Stable computation uses an algebraically equivalent transformation rather than arbitrary logit clipping. Training code commonly uses a cross-entropy interface accepting raw scores.
worked.pitfall: Do not apply Softmax before passing inputs to CrossEntropyLoss as logits. Do not mix an inference threshold into the loss formula.
worked.question: What if 500 is added to every logit?
worked.answer: Mathematically, nothing changes. A stable implementation still subtracts the maximum first to avoid unnecessarily large intermediate values.

depth.boundary: PyTorch CrossEntropyLoss expects raw scores, while NLLLoss expects log probabilities.

introduction.definition: 交叉验证按规定的切分方式，轮流用部分数据训练、用另一部分评估，帮助比较方法和参数。验证数据不参与对应轮的拟合。
introduction.example: 把资料分成几份，每轮留一份作模拟考试，其余用于学习。若在考试前已经用全部资料计算了预处理参数，考试就不再完全独立。

exercise.question: 做交叉验证前，先用全部数据挑选特征，会有什么问题？
exercise.answer: 留出的验证数据已经影响了特征选择，评估会泄漏。需要在每轮训练部分内完成选择和拟合；时间序列还要尊重时间顺序。

blocks.text: Cross-validation evaluates stability across repeated data splits. Out-of-fold predictions, or OOF predictions, come from a fold model that did not see the corresponding sample during training; stacking commonly uses them. Nested cross-validation performs model selection in an inner loop and evaluates the whole selection procedure in an outer loop, reducing optimism from repeated tuning. It costs more computation and does not eliminate distribution shift. The time-based or group-based splitting rules must still be appropriate.

worked.title: Data Leakage: Fitting a Mean Using Future Data
worked.scenario: Train on the first two months and validate on the third. A feature has training values [0,2] and future validation values [100,102].
steps: Using the full-data mean gives 51. Transforming training data with it exposes fitting to the future distribution.
Split chronologically first. The training mean is 1; use that fitted value for both training and validation. Large transformed validation values are possible.
Fit transformations only on the training portion of each cross-validation fold too. Evaluate an independent test set after model selection.
worked.result: Preventing leakage requires controlling which data each fitting operation sees, including imputation, scaling, feature selection and target encoding.
worked.pitfall: The large values make leakage visible; mean leakage does not necessarily improve every model’s score. Do not arbitrarily shuffle time-dependent tasks.
worked.question: If validation and training means differ greatly, should the scaler be refitted on validation data?
worked.answer: Do not do so during evaluation to improve the score. Investigate distribution shift, and retrain under a clearly defined data-update protocol.

depth.boundary: Time-dependent or grouped data cannot be split randomly without considering its structure.

applications.title: Nested Time Validation · 金融时序的嵌套验证
applications.reason: 在一般交叉验证上增加时间顺序、标签完成与内外层职责，评价完整的选参流程。

introduction.definition: CTC 是处理输入序列与输出标签没有逐帧对齐信息的一种训练方法。例如知道一句话的文字，但不知道每个字对应哪几帧声音。
introduction.example: 同一个字可以在多个音频帧上重复出现，帧间也可出现空白。CTC 按规则折叠帧级路径，得到最终文字，再汇总能产生该文字的多条路径。

exercise.question: 路径 A、空白、A 折叠后，是否与连续的 A、A 一样？
exercise.answer: 不一样。CTC 先合并连续重复标签，再移除空白。A、空白、A 得到 AA；连续 A、A 得到 A。次序很关键。

blocks.text: CTC, connectionist temporal classification, handles tasks where input frames and output labels lack a known alignment. In speech recognition, for example, the transcript may be known without knowing which frames correspond to each sound. CTC sums over possible alignments using a collapse rule that merges consecutive repeated labels before removing a dedicated blank symbol. Label smoothing softens the target distribution to discourage overconfidence. Auxiliary losses add training signals for intermediate representations, load balancing or other goals. Adding a loss does not automatically help; objectives and their weights can conflict.

depth.boundary: CTC assumes monotonic alignments and compatible sequence lengths; it does not align arbitrary sequence pairs.

introduction.definition: 数据泄漏是训练、特征处理或模型选择使用了实际预测时不可得的信息，使评价偏乐观。泄漏不仅是直接看到测试答案，也可能来自全样本预处理、相关样本跨折和事后筛选。
introduction.example: 若先用三者求均值 4，再切训练测试，未来输入已经改变了训练参数。正确做法是冻结训练均值 2；即使没有读取未来标签，这仍是一种泄漏。

introduction.definition: IoU, intersection over union, measures overlap between predicted and ground-truth regions. Dice is another common overlap measure and can be used to construct a training loss. In medical imaging, a model may miss a small lesion entirely yet achieve high pixel accuracy by correctly predicting the background. Region-overlap metrics make this failure easier to see. Segmentation often combines BCE or cross-entropy with Dice-based objectives to assess both individual pixels and overall overlap. Distinguish differentiable training approximations from the metrics used in formal evaluation.
introduction.example: 例子：预测区域有 4 个像素，真实区域有 6 个，交集为 3，则 Dice=2×3/(4+6)=0.6，损失 1−Dice=0.4；IoU=3/(4+6−3)=3/7。空预测与空真值同时出现时分母为零，需事先约定平滑和评分规则。

introduction.definition: Dijkstra's algorithm maintains the best distances discovered so far, repeatedly selects the nearest unfinalized node, and uses it to improve its neighbors' distances. With nonnegative edge weights, this nearest node can be finalized safely: extending a path cannot suddenly make it cheaper through a negative edge. Navigation and nonnegative-cost networks are typical uses. A priority queue accelerates selecting the next node. Dijkstra is not a universal shortest-path algorithm for arbitrary weighted graphs.
introduction.example:
Directed edges are A→B=5, A→C=1, C→B=1, B→D=2 and C→D=7. Start from A.
Distances are A=0, C=1, B=2, D=4. The shortest route to D is A-C-B-D.

exercise.question: If C→B=-4 is allowed, does the same nonnegative-weight proof apply?
exercise.answer: No. Negative edges may lower a finalized distance. Choose another method according to the constraints.

worked.title: Dijkstra: Why Old Distances Remain in the Queue
worked.scenario: Directed edges are A→B=5, A→C=1, C→B=1, B→D=2 and C→D=7. Start from A.
steps: After A, candidates are B=5 and C=1. Processing C first improves B to 2 and D to 8.
Processing the new B=2 improves D to 4. Old entries B=5 and D=8 may still be queued.
Next process D=4. When B=5 is popped, skip it because it differs from current dist[B]=2. Likewise skip D=8.
worked.result: Distances are A=0, C=1, B=2, D=4. The shortest route to D is A-C-B-D.
worked.pitfall: The demo sorts a small list to display candidates; it is not an efficient heap implementation. Heap complexity bounds do not describe that display container.
worked.question: If C→B=-4 is allowed, does the same nonnegative-weight proof apply?
worked.answer: No. Negative edges may lower a finalized distance. Choose another method according to the constraints.

depth.boundary: The standard algorithm is not generally valid when edges may have negative weights.

introduction.definition: DPO directly optimizes relative response preferences from preference data. Its classic form uses a reference model, without first fitting a separate reward network and then running online policy optimization. IPO, KTO and ORPO are other preference optimization approaches, differing in objectives, feedback formats or dependence on reference models. You need not memorize every objective here. These are methods for training existing models from preferences, rather than new Transformer architectures. Choose according to the available data.
introduction.example: 例子：同一提示有一个偏好回答和一个被拒绝回答，DPO 使用两者相对参考模型的对数概率差。若该差为 2、β=0.1，则损失 −log(sigmoid(0.2))≈0.598。GRPO 则可对同一提示采样一组回答并按组内奖励构造优势，不是同一个训练目标。

introduction.definition: Dreamer learns a latent world model from real interaction experience, then rolls out imagined trajectories inside that model to train an actor and a critic. It aims to turn each real experience into many internal learning opportunities, improving sample efficiency. The key distinction is training an action policy inside the model; this need not involve a large new search before every real action. Model prediction errors affect the policy, so real data must continually correct the model.
introduction.example: 例子：机器人已有一次真实动作转移记录，Dreamer 在学得的潜状态模型中展开若干虚拟动作以训练策略；MuZero 在表示、动力学和奖励模型上做搜索。虚拟搜索得到高奖励仍依赖模型准确，必须回到真实环境验证。

Model prediction errors affect the policy, so real data must continually correct the model.
例子：机器人已有一次真实动作转移记录，Dreamer 在学得的潜状态模型中展开若干虚拟动作以训练策略；MuZero 在表示、动力学和奖励模型上做搜索。虚拟搜索得到高奖励仍依赖模型准确，必须回到真实环境验证。

depth.boundary: Compare control objectives, prediction targets, and planning mechanisms.

introduction.definition: Dropout randomly masks activations during training to reduce reliance on particular information pathways. Inference normally disables this masking, with scaling handled according to the implementation. Dropout does not permanently delete neurons after training. Drop path and stochastic depth randomly skip paths or residual branches in suitable architectures, providing more structured stochastic regularization. Their benefit depends on the architecture and data; adding more does not always help.
introduction.example: 例子：训练时保留概率为 0.5，输入激活为 4，采用 inverted dropout 后输出以各半概率为 0 或 8，期望仍为 4。推理时通常直接使用 4。一次被保留的输出翻倍，不代表模型在推理时还应再乘一次 0.5。

introduction.definition: A tensor dtype specifies how values are represented, such as a floating-point format or integer type. Its device specifies where the tensor is stored and computed, such as CPU memory or a particular accelerator.
introduction.example: One million float32 values occupy about four million raw bytes, versus two million for float16. Moving a tensor to a GPU changes its location, not automatically its dtype or mathematical shape.

introduction.definition: Linked list questions need to distinguish between node identity and node value. Two nodes with the same value do not mean that the linked lists intersect. The sentinel or dummy node is placed before the real head, so that operations such as deleting the head node and inserting the head can also be written as "modify the next of the predecessor". When deleting the nth node from the last, the fast and slow pointers maintain a fixed distance, so that the slow pointer finally falls on the predecessor of the node to be deleted. The bounds should be derived from loop invariants, not just by reciting how many times the fast pointer has been moved.
introduction.example: 例子：从链表 1→2 中删除头节点 1。添加哨兵 D→1→2 后，把 D.next 改为 2，最后返回 D.next。这样删除头与删除中间节点都可通过“前驱的 next”处理；哨兵是额外节点，不是具有特殊数值的业务节点。

introduction.definition: 动态规划把问题表达成状态和状态之间的递推关系，保存重复子问题的结果，避免反复求解。求最优值时，状态还必须包含后续决策所需的信息。
introduction.example: 每次爬一级或两级台阶。到第 n 级的走法，可按最后一步来自 n−1 级还是 n−2 级分成两类，所以 f(n)=f(n−1)+f(n−2)。设 f(0)=1、f(1)=1，就有 f(2)=2、f(3)=3。
introduction.story: 几位同学分别询问“到第三层有多少种走法”。值班同学把每层算好的结果写在白板上，后来的同学直接查表。白板省去了重复计算，但前提是问题规则相同；若有人增加“不能连续走两级”的限制，只记录层数就不足以回答，白板还得区分上一步怎么走。

exercise.question: 给递归加一个缓存，是否就能保证动态规划的状态设计正确？
exercise.answer: 不能。缓存只保存已有状态的答案。若把影响未来的条件遗漏，例如遗漏上一步是否走了两级，不同子问题会被误当成同一个问题，保存得再快也会算错。

blocks.text: The central question in dynamic programming is not how to fill a table, but how to define the state. A state should retain information needed for future decisions without carrying irrelevant history. In a knapsack problem, for example, the current item and remaining capacity define the state; given these, the order in which earlier items were considered usually no longer matters.

If different choice sequences reach the same state, its best result can be computed once and reused: this is an overlapping subproblem. Optimization also requires that the current optimum can be constructed from suitable subproblem optima, usually called optimal substructure. Top-down memoization solves and caches states when encountered; bottom-up computation evaluates them in dependency order.

Examples include knapsack, longest common subsequence, edit distance, and certain path problems. The number of states can be enormous; adding several dimensions can cause state explosion. Dynamic programming does not make every combinatorial problem cheap. In an interview, explain that a suitable state definition merges subproblems that recur along different paths, using stored intermediate results to avoid repeated search.

depth.boundary: Memoization alone is insufficient; state meanings and boundaries must also be clear.

introduction.definition: 提前停止根据独立验证数据的表现，决定何时停止训练。Patience 表示允许连续多少次检查没有达到规定改善标准，再触发停止。
introduction.example: 像练习同一套题：练得越久，旧题分数可能越高，但新题未必更好。训练时定期做验证，连续几轮没有进步，就停止并按规则恢复最佳权重。

exercise.question: 训练损失还在下降，是否一定不能停止？
exercise.answer: 不是。训练损失下降可能是在继续拟合训练细节。提前停止关注规定的验证指标，还要明确改善阈值、检查频率和是否恢复最佳权重。

blocks.text: During training, periodically evaluate on validation data that was not used to fit the model. Falling training error alongside persistently worsening validation error is a common sign of overfitting. Early stopping ends training based on validation performance and usually retains a better checkpoint. Patience is the allowed number of consecutive checks without improvement, not necessarily seconds or epochs. Repeatedly using the test set to decide when to stop destroys its value as an independent evaluation.
例子：越小越好的验证损失依次为 0.50、0.40、0.41、0.42，patience=2 且改善阈值为零，则最后连续两轮未改善时停止，并恢复损失 0.40 的权重。不能恢复到最后一轮后仍称其为最佳验证模型。

depth.boundary: Patience usually counts validation checks, so state its unit.

introduction.definition: Latent variables are unobserved internal variables used to explain data—for example, a customer's unknown group given observed spending. EM alternates estimating hidden-variable probabilities under current parameters and updating parameters using those estimates. In a GMM, it repeatedly estimates component memberships and updates the components. Under suitable conditions the objective does not worsen, but a global optimum is not guaranteed.

introduction.definition: F1 is the harmonic mean of precision and recall. It summarizes their balance at a chosen threshold, but does not encode every application cost and does not include true negatives.
introduction.example: If TP=8, FP=2 and FN=12, precision is 0.8, recall is 0.4, and F1 is 16/30, about 0.533. Its value is below the arithmetic mean 0.6 because the harmonic mean penalizes imbalance.

blocks.text: F1=2PR/(P+R)=2TP/(2TP+FP+FN), when the denominators are defined. P denotes precision and R recall. Reporting across classes also requires a macro, micro or other aggregation rule.

depth.boundary: Specify averaging conventions such as macro or micro when comparing multiclass results.

introduction.definition: A fast pointer taking two steps and a slow pointer taking one can find a midpoint or detect a cycle. Without a cycle, the fast pointer reaches null first; with a cycle, the pointers must meet inside it. To find the cycle entry, reset one pointer to the head, then advance both at the same speed. Their next meeting point is the entry. This follows from the relationship between the head-to-entry distance and distances around the cycle.
introduction.example: 例子：链 A→B→C→B 形成环。快指针每次两步、慢指针一步；从 A 出发，第一次到 C 与 B，第二次都到 C，因而相遇。相遇是环存在的证据，找环入口还需按算法重新设置指针，不能直接认定 C 是入口。

blocks.text: To test whether a linked list is a palindrome, find a midpoint, reverse the second half, and compare corresponding values using constant auxiliary space. depth.boundary: The first meeting point is usually not the cycle entry, and null checks remain necessary.

introduction.definition: Focal loss reduces the relative loss contribution of easy, correctly classified samples so that training focuses more on difficult ones. This is useful in object detection, where easy background locations can greatly outnumber objects. Rather than assigning a fixed minority-class weight, it adjusts a sample’s contribution according to the model’s current prediction. Difficult samples may also be mislabeled, so focal loss is not a universal remedy for class imbalance. Assess it alongside label quality, sampling and evaluation metrics.
introduction.example: 例子：二元正标签的预测正确类概率为 p_t=0.9，γ=2，忽略 α 时 focal loss=−(1−0.9)²log(0.9)≈0.00105；普通交叉熵约为 0.105。调制项降低容易样本权重，γ 是聚焦强度，不能保证提高所有任务的准确率。

introduction.definition: The forward pass computes outputs and a loss from inputs and current parameters. The backward pass propagates loss derivatives through the computation graph. An optimizer step then uses derivatives to update parameters.
introduction.example: For w=2, x=3 and y=5, prediction is 6 and loss is 1. The parameter derivative is 6. With learning rate 0.1, an ordinary gradient-descent step would change w to 1.4; that final action belongs to the optimizer.

exercise.question: 用自己的话解释：上面的情景为什么是“Forward / Backward”的例子？请指出定义中的关键条件在情景里如何体现，而不是只复述最后的数值。

introduction.definition: A gradient is the vector of partial derivatives of a scalar function with respect to its inputs or parameters. It describes local change, not the value of the function itself.
introduction.example: For L(w)=w^2, the gradient at w=3 is 6. A step w_new=w-0.1×6 gives 2.4. The local approximation helps choose a direction, but a large step can still increase a nonlinear objective.

introduction.definition: Gradient clipping limits the magnitude of gradients in an update. Norm-based clipping commonly rescales the whole gradient when its norm is too large, preserving its overall direction; value-based clipping bounds individual components. This differs from reducing the learning rate: clipping targets unusually large gradients, whereas the learning rate sets the overall scale of updates. Excessive clipping can slow learning. It cannot compensate for incorrect labels or a faulty loss implementation.
introduction.example: 例子：梯度向量为 (3,4)，范数为 5，最大范数阈值为 2，则统一缩放为 (1.2,1.6)。这是保留方向的范数裁剪；把每个坐标分别截到 2 得到 (2,2)，属于另一种规则，方向已经改变。

introduction.definition: 哈希表用哈希函数把键映射到存储位置，支持按键查找、插入和删除。不同键可能映射到同一位置，这叫冲突，需要另外处理。
introduction.example: 把编号按除以 10 的余数分到十个桶，编号 23 和 43 都进入 3 号桶。查找 43 时先去 3 号桶，再比较完整编号，不能把余数相同当作键相同。
introduction.story: 图书管理员用书号决定把借书卡放进哪个抽屉。知道书号后，就能直奔一个抽屉。抽屉里可能有多张卡，所以仍要核对书号；如果规则让大多数卡都挤进同一个抽屉，查找就会变慢。抽屉定位像哈希函数，核对卡片像冲突处理。

exercise.question: 两个键的哈希值相同，是否说明它们是同一个键？
exercise.answer: 不能。哈希映射允许冲突，必须继续比较键。查找的平均效率还依赖哈希分布、负载和冲突处理，不能由“按键定位”直接推出每次都只做一步。

blocks.text: A hash table is a key concept to understand. A hash function maps a key to a storage location for fast lookup. Python dictionaries and sets use hash-based ideas. Average lookup is usually fast, but collisions, memory costs, and worst cases still exist. A hash map stores keys and values; a hash set primarily tests whether an element is present.

worked.title: Two Sum: Look Up Before Inserting
worked.scenario: Array [4,1,5,3], target sum 8. Return two distinct positions. The hash table stores previously read values and their indices.
steps: At index 0, the value is 4 and its complement is another 4. It is absent, so insert 4→0. At index 1, the value is 1 and the required 7 is also absent.
At index 2, the value is 5 and the required complement is 3. After the failed lookup, insert 5→2.
At index 3, the value is 3 and the required 5 is found at index 2, giving positions (2,3). Each lookup considers only elements before the current position.
worked.result: 5+3=8, so return zero-based indices [2,3]. With expected constant-time hash lookup, total expected time is O(n) and auxiliary space is O(n).
worked.pitfall: Inserting the current position before looking up its complement can use one element twice. With duplicate values, distinguish values from positions.
worked.question: For [3,3] with target 6, why may both equal numbers be used?
worked.answer: The first lookup finds no 3, then saves position 0. The second lookup finds position 0. The two positions are distinct.

worked.title: Prefix Sums: Counting Still Works with Negative Numbers
worked.scenario: For [1,-1,1], count contiguous subarrays whose sum is 1. Let s be the prefix sum and initialize its frequency table to {0:1}.
steps: After the first element, s=1. Look up s-1=0 and find one prior prefix. Add 1 to the count, then record prefix sum 1.
After the second element, s=0. Looking up -1 finds no prefix. Increase the frequency of prefix sum 0 to 2.
After the third element, s=1. Looking up 0 finds two prior prefixes, raising the total count to 3. Then record the current prefix.
worked.result: The three index intervals are [0,0], [0,2] and [2,2]. Expected time O(n), auxiliary space O(n).
worked.pitfall: Query before recording the current prefix; otherwise a target of 0 counts an empty interval. With negative values, window sums need not change monotonically as the window grows.
worked.question: How many nonempty zero-sum intervals does [0,0,0] contain?
worked.answer: 6: three of length 1, two of length 2 and one of length 3. Prefix frequencies contribute 1+2+3.

worked.title: LRU: One Access Changes the Eviction Choice
worked.scenario: Cache capacity is 2. Display most recently used entries on the left. Execute put(1), put(2), get(1), put(3), get(2).
steps: The first two writes give [2,1]. get(1) hits and moves 1 to the front, giving [1,2].
put(3) exceeds capacity, evicts least recently used 2, and leaves [3,1].
get(2) misses, leaving [3,1]. A hash table locates nodes; a doubly linked list moves them to the front and removes the tail.
worked.result: Accessing 1 changes the later eviction choice. A hash table plus doubly linked list gives typical operations expected O(1) time and uses O(capacity) space.
worked.pitfall: The demo displays order with a short array; that array implementation is not O(1). LRU does not evict by insertion time or guarantee the optimal hit rate.
worked.question: At capacity 3, would get(2) still miss?
worked.answer: No. Inserting 3 would not exceed capacity, so 2 would remain cached.

depth.boundary: Expected constant-time lookup is not an unconditional worst-case guarantee.

introduction.definition: Huber loss behaves like squared error for small errors and more like absolute error for large errors, balancing smoothness and robustness to outliers. Quantile loss, also called pinball loss, assigns different costs to overestimation and underestimation to learn a conditional quantile. Inventory planning, for example, may require a conservative high-demand quantile as well as average demand. Choose a loss based on what should be predicted and the costs of different errors, rather than the popularity of an abbreviation.

blocks.text: Interview answer: BCE is used for binary probability predictions and strongly penalizes confidently wrong predictions. Mutually exclusive multiclass tasks commonly use multiclass cross-entropy. For continuous-value prediction, consider MSE, MAE or Huber loss. Model architecture and loss function are separate choices; the same network can be trained with different objectives.

introduction.definition: When setting zero in a matrix, you cannot immediately change the rows and columns as soon as you see zero, otherwise the newly created zeros will continue to propagate. First record which rows and columns need to be changed to zero, and then execute them uniformly. To compress the mark space, you can use the first row and first column as marks, but you should save whether the first row and first column originally contain zeros. Process the first row and column last to avoid overwriting the mark before it is used up.
introduction.example: 例子：矩阵 [[1,0],[3,4]] 的原始零位于第 1 行第 2 列，最终应为 [[0,0],[3,0]]。若扫描时直接把新写出的零也当原始标记，可能错误地把 3 清零；需先记录哪些行列原本含零。

introduction.definition: An inverted index maps a word or feature back to documents containing it, supporting keyword search. A bitmap index represents records with a particular value as bits, turning multiple-condition filtering into fast bitwise operations for certain analytical workloads. These are not more advanced B+ trees; they target different query structures. A database may maintain several indexes and let its planner choose among them. Ask about query conditions before choosing an index.
introduction.example: 例子：倒排索引记录“风险”出现在文档 2、5，“对冲”出现在文档 5、8，两词交集只需得到文档 5。普通数据库的树索引则按键排序支持范围查询。不同索引解决不同访问模式，不能把建索引理解成所有操作都会加速。

introduction.definition: Initialization determines the starting point of training. Using the same weights for all neurons may not break the symmetry; the scale may be too large or too small, making it difficult to propagate information and gradients. Xavier and He initialization are common methods for selecting initial scales based on layer structure and activation properties. They help get started with training and do not directly impart knowledge to the model. The weights of the pre-trained model have come from learning, which is not the same thing as random initialization.
introduction.example: 例子：残差层输出 y=x+F(x)，若某次 F(x)=0，输入 x=3 会直接传为 3。其导数包含恒等路径的 1，有助于梯度传播；这不意味着任意深度、初始化和学习率组合都稳定。对称初始化仍可能让不同单元学到相同东西。

blocks.text: With N samples and batch size B, keeping the final partial batch gives ceil(N/B) batches per epoch. Updating every A batches reduces the update count, with the final incomplete accumulation handled by an explicit rule.
For 1,000 samples and batches of 100, one epoch has 10 iterations if one iteration is one batch. With accumulation over 2 batches, that epoch has 5 optimizer steps. Ten iterations are not ten epochs.

depth.boundary: Gradient accumulation or skipped updates means these counts are not interchangeable.

introduction.definition: Maximum subarray sum can define the state as "the largest non-empty consecutive sum that must end at the current position". The new element is either connected to the previous interval or starts over; choose the larger value between the two, and then use the global answer to record the maximum value among all end points. The state only needs the previous value, so it can be squeezed into constant extra space.
introduction.example: 例子：数组 (−2,3,−1,4,−5)，记录“必须在当前位置结束”的最大和，依次为 −2、3、2、6、1，全局最大为 6，对应 (3,−1,4)。递推为 end=max(x,end+x)；若要求非空子数组，全负输入也不能返回空集的 0。

introduction.definition: KL divergence measures a discrepancy between probability distributions. It can train a student model to match a teacher’s distribution or constrain a new policy from moving too far from a reference policy. KL divergence is generally asymmetric, so the direction of comparison matters. It is not a geometric distance or a direct measure of semantic similarity between answers. Cross-entropy, KL divergence and entropy are related, but explain which distributions are being compared rather than treating them as interchangeable losses.
introduction.example: 例子：P=(0.5,0.5)，Q=(0.25,0.75)，KL(P∥Q)=0.5log(2)+0.5log(2/3)≈0.1438。交换 P、Q 得约 0.1308，因此 KL 不对称。若 P 在某处有正概率而 Q 为零，该方向的 KL 可以无穷大。

concepts.title: K-nearest Neighbors · K 近邻预测

introduction.definition: K 近邻预测（KNN）为新样本寻找训练数据中距离最近的 K 个已标注样本，再用这些邻居的标签投票或数值平均作预测。
introduction.example: 新住户想估计房价，先找位置和面积相近的几套已成交房，再参考它们的价格。如何衡量“相近”和选几套，都会影响结果。

exercise.question: KNN 与把无标签对象分成 K 堆的 K-means，是同一件事吗？
exercise.answer: 不是。KNN 用已知标签的邻居作预测；K-means 按中心和距离组织分组。两者都用距离，但目标和 K 的含义不同。

blocks.text: K 近邻预测（KNN）利用距离最近的已标注训练样本进行分类或回归。K-means 是无监督聚类，定义统一放在聚类页；两者都用距离，但不应在两个基础入口重复解释 K-means。
对查询 x 找到 K 个邻居集合 N_K(x)。分类按标签票数或距离权重投票；回归可用 $\hat y=K^{-1}\sum_{i\in N_K(x)}y_i$。K 为邻居数，距离、尺度、并列与权重规则都须预先规定，不能用测试标签选择 K。
查询 x=2.1，训练点为 (1,A)、(2,A)、(3,B)、(9,B)，取欧氏距离与 K=3，最近三点标签 A、B、A，预测为 A。这使用了训练标签；把同一批未标注点分成簇的 K-means 则是另一个任务。

depth.boundary: KNN is covered in Chapter 29. Similar names do not imply the same task.

distinctions.title: Clustering
distinctions.reason: KNN 使用邻居的已知标签预测新样本；K-means 根据距离组织无标签数据，定义集中在聚类页。相似名称不代表同一任务。

concepts.title: KV Cache / FlashAttention · 注意力推理的缓存与访存

introduction.definition: KV cache 保存自回归推理中已处理 token 的键和值，供后续 token 复用。FlashAttention 则通过分块等方式减少注意力计算的中间存储和数据搬运；它不是另一种 KV cache，两者可以配合使用。注意力的数学机制见基础链接。
introduction.example: L=2、T=100、H=2、d=4、b=2 时，示意 KV 存储为 6400 字节。T 翻倍，这部分存储也翻倍。更换模型权重后，旧状态不能仅因输入文字相同就继续使用；跨请求的共享还要满足各自数据和访问边界。

blocks.text: 简化地，L 层、缓存 T 个 token、每层 H 个 KV 头、每头维度 d、每个数 b 字节时，键和值共占 \(M=2LTHdb\) 字节，不计分配器和额外元数据。复用需要模型版本、位置、前缀及其他影响状态的配置兼容。缓存避免重复投影，并没有免除新 token 读取历史键值的工作。

worked.title: KV Cache: Which Computations Are Reused?
worked.scenario: During causal autoregressive decoding, four tokens have already been processed. Now process the fifth token to predict the sixth. Keys and values for the first four tokens are cached separately at each layer.
steps: Reuse the first four tokens’ cached K and V instead of recomputing their projections. Compute Q, K and V for the fifth token and append its K and V to the cache.
The fifth token’s query attends to the visible keys for tokens 1…5 and weights their values. Its final representation predicts the sixth token. This attention work still grows with prefix length.
Suppose each token stores 2 groups of d values, each b bytes. For L layers, T tokens and batch size B, simplified memory use is 2BLTdb.
worked.result: Before processing the fifth token, B=1, L=2, T=4, d=8 and b=2 give 256 bytes of cached values. Here d is the total cached key width per layer, with the same width assumed for values. After appending the fifth token, the same formula gives 320 bytes.
worked.pitfall: GQA/MQA, quantization, paging and framework metadata change real memory use. KV caching and FlashAttention optimize different aspects of inference.
worked.question: What happens when length doubles under this simplified cache formula?
worked.answer: Cache size doubles. This does not establish that total inference time exactly doubles.

depth.boundary: Cache management, numerical quantization, and kernel optimization are different techniques.

introduction.definition: The learning rate controls the overall step size of optimizer updates. It measures neither how much knowledge has been learned nor how many epochs training has run. Imagine searching for low ground: the update direction tells you where to move, and the learning rate influences how far to move. Optimizers can also use historical gradients to scale individual parameter updates, so the learning rate is not the absolute change applied to every parameter.
introduction.example: If the stride length is too large, it may cross the favorable area at once, oscillate back and forth, and even cause numerical instability in training. Steps that are too small may result in slow improvement within a given budget. There is no single value that is best for all models, batch sizes, and optimizers. A smaller learning rate does not guarantee that the final generalization will be better, because the training budget, data, and other settings jointly affect the results.

blocks.text: Suppose two runs each train for ten epochs. With a learning rate that is too small, one may learn little in that time, while a suitable learning rate gives the other good validation performance. Equal epoch counts do not imply equal optimization progress. Conversely, unstable loss is not always caused by the learning rate: labels, the loss implementation or numerical precision may also be responsible.

worked.title: Learning Rate: Convergence, Oscillation and Divergence
worked.scenario: Use the simplified objective L(θ)=θ²/2, with gradient θ, initial θ=4 and fixed learning rate η.
steps: The update is θ_next=(1-η)θ. At η=0.1, 4→3.6→3.24 approaches 0 slowly.
At η=1.8, 4→-3.2→2.56 alternates sign but shrinks in magnitude, so still converges.
At η=2.2, 4→-4.8→5.76 alternates sign and grows in magnitude, so diverges.
worked.result: For this quadratic with curvature exactly 1, 0<η<2 converges; η=2 gives constant-amplitude oscillation; η=1 reaches 0 in one step.
worked.pitfall: (0,2) is not a universally safe learning-rate range for neural networks. Curvature, noise and the optimizer change stability conditions.
worked.question: For L=5θ²/2, what is the stable range of fixed learning rates?
worked.answer: The gradient is 5θ and the update factor is 1-5η. Requiring its absolute value to be below 1 gives 0<η<0.4.

worked.title: Weight Decay and Learning-Rate Decay: Different Controls
worked.scenario: Use the simplified decoupled update θ_next=(1-ηλ)θ-ηg for shrinkage and gradient updates, with θ=2, η=0.1, λ=0.01 and g=0.4.
steps: The shrinkage factor is 0.999, giving the shrunk parameter 1.998.
The gradient term is 0.04, giving 1.958 after the update. With λ=0, the same step gives 1.96.
Reducing the next step’s learning rate to 0.01 changes the schedule for η. λ still sets parameter shrinkage strength.
worked.result: Weight decay shrinks parameters during an update; learning-rate decay describes how η changes over time. Their numerical effects interact because shrinkage contains ηλ.
worked.pitfall: Here g denotes the update direction. Actual AdamW adjusts gradients using momentum and second-moment statistics, so this direction is not simply the raw gradient.
worked.question: If g=0, can weight decay still update the parameter?
worked.answer: Yes. If ηλ is nonzero and decay applies to that parameter, the equation still performs θ←(1-ηλ)θ.

depth.boundary: The learning rate is neither the epoch count nor a fixed change to every weight.

introduction.definition: In neural classification, a logit usually means an unnormalized real-valued output score before conversion to probabilities. In binary statistical terminology, the logit of a probability is its log odds.
introduction.example: Probability p=0.8 has odds 4 and log odds about 1.386. A raw score z=2 is valid even though probability 2 would be invalid. Calibration still needs checking after score conversion.

depth.boundary: Scores may be negative or exceed one; they are not probabilities.

introduction.definition: A loop invariant is a statement true at a particular point of every iteration. Correctness reasoning checks initialization, preservation and the consequence when the loop terminates.
introduction.example: For [2,4,1], the accumulator before indices 0,1,2,3 is 0,2,6,7. The invariant explains what the partial result means, rather than only checking that this example happened to finish with 7.

introduction.definition: A loss scores model errors and is what training aims to improve. An objective function may also include requirements such as regularization. An evaluation metric indicates whether performance meets the task’s needs. The training objective and reported metric can differ: for example, train a purchase-probability predictor with BCE but assess precision or actual conversion outcomes after deployment. An optimizable loss gives training a direction, without guaranteeing complete alignment with the final business objective.

introduction.definition: Binary search relies on a monotonic true/false condition, rather than merely a sorted array. To find an insertion position, search for the first value greater than or equal to the target. With a half-open interval [left,right), initialize right to the array length. If the midpoint satisfies the condition, keep the left part including that midpoint; otherwise move left just past it. The search ends when left equals right, giving the boundary.
introduction.example: If the midpoint satisfies the condition, keep the left part including that midpoint; otherwise move left just past it. The search ends when left equals right, giving the boundary.

blocks.text: The invariant must preserve the desired boundary, which may equal the array length. Keep the termination and update rules consistent with either a half-open or a closed search interval. For fixed-width integers, computing the midpoint as left plus half of right-left can avoid the overflow of left+right.

worked.title: Binary Search: Half-Open Intervals and Lower Bound
worked.scenario: In sorted [1,2,2,4,7], find the first position not less than 2. Use [left,right), initially [0,5).
steps: Midpoint 2 contains 2 and satisfies the condition. Move right to 2, retaining possible earlier answers.
Midpoint 1 also contains 2, so move right to 1. Midpoint 0 contains 1 and fails the condition, so move left to 1.
Stop at left=right=1. A boundary may equal the array length. It is an insertion position, not a guarantee that the target exists.
worked.result: The lower bound of 2 is 1; of 3 it is 3; of 8 it is 5. Time O(log n).
worked.pitfall: right is excluded, so it can start at n. Do not index the array directly when the returned boundary equals n.
worked.question: Which other boundary gives the number of occurrences of 2?
worked.answer: The upper bound, the first position greater than 2, is 3. The count is 3-1=2.

worked.title: LIS: Equal Values Replace Rather Than Extend
worked.scenario: For [3,1,2,2,5,4], find the longest strictly increasing subsequence length.
steps: After 3, tails=[3]. Value 1 replaces the first entry not less than 1, giving [1].
The first 2 extends tails to [1,2]. The second 2 replaces the same position without increasing length, preserving strict increase.
Value 5 gives [1,2,5]; 4 then gives [1,2,4]. Length is 3.
worked.result: The answer is 3. Here tails happens to form an actual subsequence, but this is not guaranteed for every input.
worked.pitfall: For [2,3,1], final tails=[1,3] violates the input order and is not a reconstructed subsequence.
worked.question: For a longest nondecreasing subsequence, how should the repeated 2 be handled?
worked.answer: Update the first entry strictly greater than the value, allowing equality to extend the sequence. This input’s nondecreasing length is 4.

depth.boundary: Interval conventions and updates must agree. A boundary position does not itself prove the target exists.

introduction.definition: For multiclass or multilabel tasks, metrics can be calculated separately for each class and then averaged. Macro averaging gives every class equal weight, making problems in small classes easier to see. Weighted averaging uses weights such as class sample counts, so large classes can dominate. Micro averaging pools the counts first, then calculates the metric, emphasizing overall sample-level performance. All three scores may be called F1 but differ, so comparisons must specify the averaging method.
introduction.example: 例子：两类 F1 分别为 0.9、0.5，macro F1 为 0.7。若汇总计数 TP=8、FP=2、FN=4，则 micro F1=2TP/(2TP+FP+FN)=16/22≈0.7273。宏平均先算各类指标，微平均先汇总计数，不能只改变显示名称。

introduction.definition: 梯度累积把一批数据拆成几小批，分别计算梯度并积累，到约定的边界再更新一次参数，以减少单次前向、反向的显存需求。
introduction.example: GPU 一次只能放两条记录，但希望每八条更新一次，就分四小批处理，在这四次反向计算后才进行一次优化器更新。

exercise.question: 四小批累积，是不是四次参数更新？
exercise.answer: 不是。按这个约定，四小批对应一次更新。损失归一化与批统计等细节，还会影响它与真正大批次是否等价。

blocks.text: When GPU memory cannot fit many samples at once, split them into microbatches, run forward and backward passes separately, accumulate their gradients and then update. For example, compute gradients after each microbatch but update parameters only after four microbatches: four iterations correspond to one optimizer step. This gives a larger effective batch, but is not always exactly equivalent to one large batch. BatchNorm statistics, for example, can differ. Gradient accumulation does not mean parameters change after every microbatch.

depth.boundary: Partial final batches, loss normalization, and BatchNorm can affect equivalence to a large batch.

introduction.definition: These names denote floating-point formats. Lower precision generally saves memory and can accelerate computation on supported hardware, but the numerical range and resolution differ. BF16 has an exponent range similar to FP32 but lower precision; FP16 has a narrower representable range. Mixed precision uses different formats for different operations, often retaining higher precision for sensitive calculations. It does not simply make all numbers smaller, and does not guarantee equal speedups on every device.
introduction.example: 例子：一个梯度为 10⁻⁸，在常见 FP16 范围内可能下溢。若损失先乘 1024，梯度也乘同一倍数；反传后再除 1024，才恢复原更新尺度。缩放不能修复中间激活溢出，溢出时还需跳过更新并调整策略。

introduction.definition: For a sliding-window maximum, a deque stores indices in nonincreasing order of their values. When a new value arrives, remove indices from the back while their values are no greater: the new value is at least as large and expires later. Remove the front index when it leaves the window. The remaining front gives the current maximum.
introduction.example: For example, the window sweeps through one, three, and two. When three enters, one can be eliminated, but two cannot eliminate three. Each index can enter and exit the queue once at most, so the amortized time is linear. Use a queue that supports constant-time operations on both ends; deleting the head of an ordinary array in some languages will move elements, and it cannot be claimed that the implementation is still linear.

introduction.definition: Daily Temperatures maintains a stack of indices with nonincreasing temperatures. When a warmer temperature arrives, repeatedly pop indices; the difference between the current index and the popped index is the waiting time. The stack contains positions whose answers are unresolved, and popped positions need no further work. Each index is pushed and popped once, giving linear total work by amortized analysis. Equal temperature is not warmer, so it must not resolve an earlier position.
introduction.example:
For temperatures [20,24,22,27,21], find how many days each position waits for a warmer day. The stack stores indices whose answers are unresolved.
Waiting times are [1,2,1,0,0]. Each index is pushed and popped at most once: time O(n), auxiliary space O(n).

exercise.question: What changes for [20,20,21]?
exercise.answer: The result is [2,1,0]. The second 20 does not pop the first 20.
