worked.title: Monotonic Stack: Resolve Waiting Time When Popping
worked.scenario: For temperatures [20,24,22,27,21], find how many days each position waits for a warmer day. The stack stores indices whose answers are unresolved.
steps: Day 1 has temperature 24, warmer than day 0 at 20. Pop index 0 and set its answer to 1.
Day 2 at 22 is not warmer than 24, so push it. Day 3 at 27 first pops index 2 and records 1, then pops index 1 and records 2.
Indices 3 and 4 have no later warmer day, so their answers remain 0.
worked.result: Waiting times are [1,2,1,0,0]. Each index is pushed and popped at most once: time O(n), auxiliary space O(n).
worked.pitfall: The task requires a strictly warmer day, so equal temperatures do not resolve an answer. Store indices, not only values, to calculate distances.
worked.question: What changes for [20,20,21]?
worked.answer: The result is [2,1,0]. The second 20 does not pop the first 20.

depth.boundary: Linear total work follows because each item enters and leaves at most once. Specify comparisons for equal values.

introduction.definition: MSE, mean squared error, is common in continuous-value prediction and penalizes large errors strongly. MAE, mean absolute error, measures the magnitude of deviations from the true value and is less sensitive to extreme errors. RMSE is the square root of MSE and has the same units as the target. For temperature predictions, an error in degrees is easier to interpret than one in squared degrees. These losses and metrics can be used with other suitable models, not only linear regression.
introduction.example: 例子：两笔预测误差为 1、−3，MSE=(1²+3²)/2=5，MAE=(1+3)/2=2，RMSE=√5≈2.236。RMSE 与目标同单位，MSE 的单位是目标单位的平方；不能跨不同目标尺度直接比较它们的数值。

concepts.title: Multi-source BFS · 等时传播与最近源距离

introduction.definition: 多源 BFS 把多个起点同时置为距离零，再按普通 BFS 扩展。它求等权图中每个可达节点到最近起点的最短距离，适合同时发生的传播或多个服务点的最近距离；不是从每个源分别重复整次搜索。
introduction.example: 若某格被障碍完全隔离，应保留不可达状态，不能把它当作零分钟到达。

exercise.question: 用自己的话解释：上面的情景为什么是“Multi-source BFS · 等时传播与最近源距离”的例子？请指出定义中的关键条件在情景里如何体现，而不是只复述最后的数值。

blocks.text: 对起点集合 S，\(d(v)=\min_{s\in S}\operatorname{dist}(s,v)\)。先把 S 中所有节点入队，并在首次入队时标记已发现，再向未发现邻居赋 d+1。邻接表实现的时间为 O(V+E)，辅助存储为 O(V)。若边耗时不同，层数不能直接当经过时间。
一条五格通道的两端同时开始传播，初始队列含位置 0 和 4，距离依次为 (0,1,2,1,0)。只先完成左端的 BFS 再处理右端，会破坏“所有源同时开始”的初始化含义。若某格被障碍完全隔离，应保留不可达状态，不能把它当作零分钟到达。

depth.boundary: With unequal edge travel times, layer count need not equal shortest travel time.

introduction.definition: Loss scaling amplifies the loss in some mixed-precision training so that small gradients remain representable, then compensates before updating. NaN denotes an invalid numeric value; Inf denotes infinity, for example after overflow. These can arise from division by zero, extreme scores or unstable operations. OOM means out of memory, not exploding gradients. For OOM, inspect batch size, sequence length, saved activations and model size. For NaN, inspect numerical values and data first.

depth.boundary: Separate numerical diagnosis from memory diagnosis first.

introduction.definition: Offline RL trains on a fixed collection of interactions without gathering new experience from the environment during training. It can overestimate actions poorly covered by the dataset. CQL addresses this with conservative value estimation; IQL fits values and extracts a policy while limiting dependence on evaluating actions outside the data. Neither creates missing coverage. Offline evaluation is also an imperfect substitute for safe, controlled real-world validation.
introduction.example: 例子：日志只记录在某状态选择“等待”，从未记录“大额买入”。离线算法即使给后者估出高价值，也缺少相应数据支持；在仿真里选择它不等于已验证真实成交。off-policy 指学习目标策略可不同于采样策略，offline 另强调训练期间不再收集新交互。

introduction.definition: Weights and biases are learnable model values; “parameter” is the general category. Learning rate, batch size, and maximum tree depth are usually hyperparameters controlling the model or training, rather than weights directly fitted by ordinary training. A bias term is not the statistical bias in the bias–variance tradeoff or social bias. The same word has different meanings: first determine whether the discussion concerns model structure, statistical error, or fairness.
introduction.example: 例子：回归模型 ŷ=wx+b，拟合得到 w=2、b=1，这是参数。学习率 0.01、正则强度 0.1 是选择训练程序的超参数，应在验证流程中选择；不能反复看最终测试误差调到最好，再把它当独立测试成绩。

introduction.definition: 主成分分析（PCA）把多个数值特征重新组合成彼此正交的方向，依次保留数据变化较大的方向，用较少维度表示数据。
introduction.example: 身高和臂展常一起增减。把它们想成平面上的点云，最长的延伸方向可以总结大部分变化；另一个方向记录偏离这个趋势的部分。

exercise.question: 保留变化最大的方向，就一定保留了最有用的预测信息吗？
exercise.answer: 不一定。PCA 优化的是特征方差的保留，不使用预测目标。较小方差的方向也可能与任务结果有关。

blocks.text: 主成分分析（PCA）把中心化后的多变量数据投影到彼此正交、按方差大小排序的方向。它是无监督降维：只看输入的变化，不保证保留的方向最能预测标签。
有 n 行样本、d 列特征的中心化矩阵 X，样本协方差为 $\Sigma=X^\top X/(n-1)$。求 $\Sigma v_j=\lambda_jv_j$，按特征值 λ 降序选择 k 个单位正交向量组成 V，投影为 $Z=XV$。第 j 个方向的解释方差比为 $\lambda_j/\sum_l\lambda_l$。中心和可选的尺度参数必须只在训练集拟合。
协方差矩阵 [[2,1],[1,2]] 的特征值为 3、1，第一方向为 (1,1)/√2，保留一个方向解释 75% 方差。中心化样本 (2,0) 在这一方向的坐标为 √2；标签若取决于另一方向，压缩仍可能丢失预测信息。

depth.boundary: High-variance directions need not be the most useful for classification.

applications.title: PCA Residual · 多资产收益的主成分残差
applications.reason: 把一般主成分分析连接到多资产共同收益剔除，并区分几何残差与最终持仓中性。

introduction.definition: PID adjusts control using current error, accumulated error and the rate of error change to track a desired state. The proportional term responds to deviation, the integral term handles persistent offset, and the derivative term can provide damping. Noise, delay and tuning affect stability. PID is not learned from large video datasets, but is useful in many stabilization tasks.
introduction.example:
One-dimensional position x starts at 0 and targets 5. The real system follows x_next=x+u+wind, while the predictor ignores wind. Actions are restricted to [-1,1].
Closed-loop feedback changes accumulated error, but a proportional policy without wind compensation cannot eliminate every offset. The demo shows predicted and actual next positions together.

exercise.question: With zero wind, what happens after the feedback policy reaches 5?
exercise.answer: Its action becomes 0 and position remains 5. The fixed-action policy keeps moving by 1 each step.

worked.title: World Models: Prediction Error and Feedback Correction
worked.scenario: One-dimensional position x starts at 0 and targets 5. The real system follows x_next=x+u+wind, while the predictor ignores wind. Actions are restricted to [-1,1].
steps: A fixed-action policy always uses u=1. With wind=-0.3, each real movement is only 0.7, so predictions and observations diverge.
A feedback policy observes again each step and uses u=clip(5-x,-1,1). Its action shrinks as it approaches the target.
With wind=-0.3, feedback settles near 4.7, retaining a steady-state offset. Fixed actions continue past the target.
worked.result: Closed-loop feedback changes accumulated error, but a proportional policy without wind compensation cannot eliminate every offset. The demo shows predicted and actual next positions together.
worked.pitfall: This is not full MPC: it neither optimizes a multistep action sequence nor trains a world model. The simplified dynamics illustrate prediction, observation and feedback.
worked.question: With zero wind, what happens after the feedback policy reaches 5?
worked.answer: Its action becomes 0 and position remains 5. The fixed-action policy keeps moving by 1 each step.

depth.boundary: The prediction horizon may differ from the executed horizon.

concepts.title: Postorder DP · 树上动态规划的返回值与全局答案

introduction.definition: 后序树形动态规划先求子树摘要，再合成当前节点的结果。它把动态规划用于树结构；递归只负责遍历顺序，状态的含义和能否向父节点延伸仍须单独定义。树高、直径、最大路径和可以采用相近遍历，却不能混用返回值。
introduction.example: 若计算最大路径和且整棵树只有值 −3 的节点，答案应是 −3；把全局答案初始化为 0 会错误地选择一条题目未允许的空路径。

exercise.question: 用自己的话解释：上面的情景为什么是“Postorder DP · 树上动态规划的返回值与全局答案”的例子？请指出定义中的关键条件在情景里如何体现，而不是只复述最后的数值。

blocks.text: 以节点数定义高度，空树 h=0，节点高度为 \(h(u)=1+\max(h_l,h_r)\)。若直径按边数计，经过当前节点的候选为 h_l+h_r。最大路径和中，返回父节点的增益只能选一侧；更新全局答案时才允许左右两侧同时接入。每个节点处理一次，时间为 O(n)，递归栈空间取决于树高。
根节点的左右孩子都为叶子，左右高度均为 1，根高度为 2，直径是 2 条边。若计算最大路径和且整棵树只有值 −3 的节点，答案应是 −3；把全局答案初始化为 0 会错误地选择一条题目未允许的空路径。

depth.boundary: A one-sided path passed upward differs from a candidate joining both sides at the current node.

introduction.definition: TRPO uses a trust-region approach to constrain policy changes and avoid destroying existing behavior in one update. PPO pursues similar stability through easier-to-implement objectives, such as clipping or penalties. It commonly performs several updates on a newly collected batch of interactions before gathering fresh data. PPO controls update incentives; it does not enforce the same maximum change on every parameter or guarantee that a policy never moves too far.
introduction.example: 例子：PPO 的一次样本优势为 +1，新旧动作概率比为 1.3，裁剪 ε=0.2，则该样本的裁剪目标取 min(1.3,1.2)=1.2。SAC 的熵奖励和 TD3 的双评论家、延迟更新解决的是不同机制，不能用同一裁剪式概括全部算法。

exercise.question: 用自己的话解释：上面的情景为什么是“PPO / SAC / TD3”的例子？请指出定义中的关键条件在情景里如何体现，而不是只复述最后的数值。

introduction.definition: Precision is the fraction of predicted positives that are actually positive. It answers whether positive predictions are trustworthy at a specified decision threshold.
introduction.example: A detector raises 10 alarms and 8 are true cases: precision is 80%. This does not tell how many true cases it missed; recall addresses that separate denominator.

exercise.question: 用自己的话解释：上面的情景为什么是“Precision”的例子？请指出定义中的关键条件在情景里如何体现，而不是只复述最后的数值。
exercise.definition: Precision is the fraction of predicted positives that are actually positive. It answers whether positive predictions are trustworthy at a specified decision threshold.
exercise.evidence: A detector raises 10 alarms and 8 are true cases: precision is 80%. This does not tell how many true cases it missed; recall addresses that separate denominator.

blocks.text: Precision=TP/(TP+FP), where TP counts correctly predicted positives and FP counts negative examples predicted positive. If no positive predictions exist, the denominator is zero and the evaluation convention must be stated.

depth.boundary: The denominator counts predicted positives, not actual positives. Precision is undefined when no examples are predicted positive unless a reporting convention is specified.

introduction.definition: 前缀和记录序列从起点到各个边界的累计总和。一个区间的总和可以由两个累计值相减得到。
introduction.example: 每天记累计存款：前两天累计 8 元，前五天累计 20 元，那么第三到第五天共存入 12 元。不必重新把那三天逐一相加。

exercise.question: 为什么求第三到第五天的存款要减去“前两天”，而不是“前三天”？
exercise.answer: 前三天已经包含第三天的存款，减掉它会少算一天。区间左端点之前的累计值才是要排除的部分。

blocks.text: Define the prefix sum P such that the sum of the first zero elements is zero. The sum of a segment is k, which is equivalent to the current prefix sum minus an earlier prefix sum equal to k. Therefore, when scanning the current prefix P, check how many times P minus k has appeared before, then accumulate the answer, and finally record the current P. The occurrence of the zero prefix must be recorded once at the beginning to count the interval starting from the beginning of the array.

For example, one, negative one, one, the target is one. The three legal intervals come from two single elements and the entire array; the prefix frequency can count the contribution of repeated prefixes. The hash table must save the number of times, not just whether it exists. Recording the current prefix first and then querying will incorrectly include empty intervals when k is zero.

worked.title: Prefix Sums: Counting Still Works with Negative Numbers
worked.scenario: For [1,-1,1], count contiguous subarrays whose sum is 1. Let s be the prefix sum and initialize its frequency table to {0:1}.
steps: After the first element, s=1. Look up s-1=0 and find one prior prefix. Add 1 to the count, then record prefix sum 1.
After the second element, s=0. Looking up -1 finds no prefix. Increase the frequency of prefix sum 0 to 2.
After the third element, s=1. Looking up 0 finds two prior prefixes, raising the total count to 3. Then record the current prefix.
worked.result: The three index intervals are [0,0], [0,2] and [2,2]. Expected time O(n), auxiliary space O(n).
worked.pitfall: Query before recording the current prefix; otherwise a target of 0 counts an empty interval. With negative values, window sums need not change monotonically as the window grows.
worked.question: How many nonempty zero-sum intervals does [0,0,0] contain?
worked.answer: 6: three of length 1, two of length 2 and one of length 3. Prefix frequencies contribute 1+2+3.

worked.title: Difference Arrays: Undo the Increment After the Range
worked.scenario: Start with a zero-based, length-5 array of zeros. Add 2 to inclusive [1,3], then add -1 to [2,4], reconstructing the array afterward.
steps: Allocate a length-6 difference array. The first update adds 2 to d[1] and subtracts 2 from d[4].
The second subtracts 1 from d[2] and adds 1 to d[5]. Position d[5] is a sentinel canceling the update after the array ends.
Prefix-sum the first five differences to obtain values 0,2,1,1,-1 at positions 0…4.
worked.result: The final array is [0,2,1,1,-1]. Each range update changes two endpoints; final reconstruction takes O(n).
worked.pitfall: For an inclusive range, cancel at r+1 rather than r. Allocate the sentinel but do not return it as a sixth array value.
worked.question: For a half-open range [l,r), where is the cancellation?
worked.answer: At d[r], because r is already outside the updated range.

depth.boundary: Counting often needs prefix frequencies and an initial zero prefix. Tree paths also need state undo on return.

introduction.definition: Classic Q-learning uses the estimated value of the best next-state action in its target, even when exploration actually selects another action. SARSA uses the value of the action actually selected next under the behavior policy. This illustrates off-policy versus on-policy learning: the relationship between the target policy and the policy collecting data. Off-policy does not mean offline; an off-policy algorithm can collect new data while learning.
introduction.example:
Current Q(s,a)=2, reward r=1, maximum next-state Q=4, discount γ=0.9 and learning rate α=0.5.
The same observed reward produces different learning targets depending on termination. One tabular Q-learning update does not establish a fully learned policy.

exercise.question: With α=1, what is the updated value for the nonterminal transition?
exercise.answer: It becomes the current target, 4.6. This does not mean the target estimate is noise-free.

worked.title: Q-Learning: No Bootstrapping at True Termination
worked.scenario: Current Q(s,a)=2, reward r=1, maximum next-state Q=4, discount γ=0.9 and learning rate α=0.5.
steps: For a nonterminal transition, the target is r+γ max Q=1+0.9×4=4.6.
The TD error is 4.6-2=2.6. Update Q=2+0.5×2.6=3.3.
At a true terminal state, the target is only r=1, giving 2+0.5×(1-2)=1.5.
worked.result: The same observed reward produces different learning targets depending on termination. One tabular Q-learning update does not establish a fully learned policy.
worked.pitfall: Distinguish true termination from time-limit truncation. Bootstrapping depends on the task and interface semantics. Q-learning uses the maximum next-state value; SARSA uses the actual next action’s value.
worked.question: With α=1, what is the updated value for the nonterminal transition?
worked.answer: It becomes the current target, 4.6. This does not mean the target estimate is noise-free.

depth.boundary: They relate the behavior policy and target policy differently.

introduction.definition: If you want to find the kth largest value, you don't have to sort the entire array. Maintain a min-heap with a size of at most k. The top of the heap is the minimum value among the current retainers, which is the elimination threshold. It is worth replacing only if the new value exceeds the threshold. After scanning, the top of the heap will be the kth largest. The frequencies of the top k high-frequency elements are first counted, and then the same selection is made according to the frequency. The ranking object changes from the numerical value to the frequency of the key.

blocks.text: The heap only guarantees the extreme value at the top of the heap, and does not guarantee the overall ordering of the internal array. Here, the kth largest number of elements is counted, and repeated values still account for multiple rankings; the top k high-frequency objects are different keys and must be distinguished.

worked.title: Top K: Let Requirements Determine the Algorithm
worked.scenario: Find the two largest values in [9,1,7,3,8]. First clarify whether output must be ordered, input may be modified, and data arrives continuously.
steps: Keep a min-heap of size 2, whose root is the current second-largest value. Reading 9 and 1 gives {1,9}; 7 replaces 1, 3 is ignored, and 8 replaces 7.
The retained values are {8,9}. Descending output still requires sorting those two results.
A static array can instead use quickselect to find the boundary in average O(n) time. It rearranges the array, leaves the selected region unsorted, and its worst case depends on pivot selection.
worked.result: A heap suits streaming updates: time O(n log k), auxiliary space O(k). Quickselect suits mutable static data. The constraints determine the choice.
worked.pitfall: “Quickselect is faster than sorting” is incomplete without average versus worst-case cost, output ordering and input mutation requirements.
worked.question: Data keeps arriving and Top K must be available at any time. What should be considered first?
worked.answer: A fixed-size heap is usually convenient for incremental maintenance. Also discuss costs when k is close to n and the overhead of returning sorted results.

depth.boundary: Quickselect usually modifies input. Randomized versions have expected linear but worst-case quadratic time.

introduction.definition: RAG, retrieval-augmented generation, retrieves relevant information from external documents or knowledge bases before answering, and supplies it to an LLM. It addresses stale parameter knowledge, private organizational knowledge absent from training, and answers that require clear evidence. RAG can reduce some knowledge hallucinations but cannot guarantee every answer is correct.
introduction.example:
Keyword retrieval ranks A,B,C; vector retrieval ranks C,B,D. A document contributes 1/(k+rank) from each list, with ranks starting at 1.
The final order is C,B,A,D. Rank fusion avoids directly adding BM25 raw scores and similarity scores on different scales.

exercise.question: What happens if only one retrieval list remains?
exercise.answer: The fused order matches that list, because 1/(k+rank) decreases as rank increases.

blocks.text: Keep three roles distinct. An LLM supplies language and reasoning capabilities. RAG supplies external knowledge. An agent system uses models, tools and workflows to perform tasks. These can work together, but describe different parts of a system.

worked.title: RRF: Fuse Ranks Instead of Adding Raw Scores
worked.scenario: Keyword retrieval ranks A,B,C; vector retrieval ranks C,B,D. A document contributes 1/(k+rank) from each list, with ranks starting at 1.
steps: At k=60, A receives 1/61 and D receives 1/63. B receives 2/62.
C receives 1/63+1/61≈0.032266, slightly above B≈0.032258.
Merge all documents that appear and sort by the fused score. A document absent from a list contributes 0 from that list.
worked.result: The final order is C,B,A,D. Rank fusion avoids directly adding BM25 raw scores and similarity scores on different scales.
worked.pitfall: RRF scores are not probabilities. Deduplicate each retrieval list first. The parameter k is not the number of results returned.
worked.question: What happens if only one retrieval list remains?
worked.answer: The fused order matches that list, because 1/(k+rank) decreases as rank increases.

depth.boundary: Retrieval does not guarantee a correct answer or sufficient evidence.

introduction.definition: Random forests predict with many trees. Classic training gives each tree a different bootstrap sample and limits each split to a random feature subset. This second randomness is crucial: if one strong feature always dominates the top split, trees become similar; limiting candidates lets them explore different rules.
introduction.example: if one strong feature always dominates the top split, trees become similar; limiting candidates lets them explore different rules.

blocks.text: Regression usually averages tree values; classification may vote or average class probabilities depending on implementation. Different perspectives reduce a single tree's high variance. They cannot recover information every tree lacks, nor guarantee freedom from overfitting.

worked.title: Random Forests: Error Correlation Limits Voting Gains
worked.scenario: Five classification trees vote [1,1,0,1,0] on one email. Positive means spam.
steps: Hard voting gives 3 to 2, producing class 1. Trees using identical data and features may make highly correlated errors.
For each tree, draw a bootstrap sample of training observations with replacement. Randomly selecting candidate features at each split introduces further variation among trees.
If all five trees make the same error on a type of email, adding votes does not automatically correct that systematic bias.
worked.result: An ensemble requires useful individual predictors and is also affected by error correlation. Real random forest classifiers may average leaf probabilities, unlike this hard-voting example.
worked.pitfall: 3/5 is not automatically a calibrated real-world probability. Out-of-bag evaluation does not replace independent testing for every task.
worked.question: Every tree predicts 0 when the truth is 1. Would adding 100 identical trees help?
worked.answer: No. Duplicating the same error adds no information.

depth.boundary: Random forests mainly reduce variance; they do not guarantee freedom from overfitting.

introduction.definition: Recall is the fraction of actual positive cases identified by a classifier. It measures coverage of positives at a specified decision threshold.
introduction.example: If a dataset contains 20 true cases and the detector finds 8, recall is 40%. The number of false alarms can change precision without changing this recall value.

blocks.text: Recall=TP/(TP+FN), where FN counts positive examples missed by the classifier. If there are no actual positives, this ratio is undefined without an explicit reporting convention.

introduction.definition: 正则化通过限制模型复杂度、约束参数或改变训练过程，减少模型对训练样本偶然细节的依赖。
introduction.example: 拟合几个测量点时，一条绕来绕去的曲线能穿过每个点；适当限制曲线复杂度，可能更接近新测量点的规律，但也可能限制过头。

exercise.question: 正则化越强，模型对新数据就一定越好吗？
exercise.answer: 不是。过强的限制会使模型连真实规律也学不到。强度需要通过独立验证来选择。

blocks.text: 正则化通过限制模型复杂度、约束参数或改变训练过程，降低对有限训练样本偶然特征的依赖。它通常引入偏差以换取更稳定的泛化，不保证在每个测试集上改善。Dropout 的机制与例子集中在独立方法页。
参数惩罚的一种形式为 $J(\theta)=L_{\mathrm{train}}(\theta)+\lambda R(\theta)$，L 为训练损失，R 为复杂度惩罚，λ≥0 为强度。L2 惩罚常取参数平方和，L1 常取绝对值和；惩罚是否含偏置、是否除样本数须注明。
若训练损失为 3，单个权重 w=2，R=w²、λ=0.1，则总目标为 3.4。把 w 缩小虽降低惩罚，也可能增加拟合误差；需要优化完整目标，并在独立验证数据上选择 λ，而不是只追求更小权重。

depth.boundary: Excessive regularization can suppress real signal.

introduction.definition: Replication stores copies of the same data on multiple nodes; sharding partitions different data across nodes. They solve different problems and can be used together. Replication supports availability and read capacity; sharding distributes storage and work.
introduction.example: A 900 GB dataset split into 3 shards has about 300 GB per shard. Keeping 2 copies of each shard uses about 1,800 GB in total. Adding replicas does not divide the logical dataset into smaller shards; adding shards does not by itself create failover copies.

blocks.text: With D bytes of logical data, S evenly sized shards and R copies of each shard, each shard contains about D/S logical bytes and total replicated storage is about RD, before indexes and overhead. A partition key decides which shard owns a record; replica consistency and failure recovery require separate rules.

depth.boundary: The number of copies and the way data is divided solve different problems.

introduction.definition: The ROC curve compares true positive and false positive rates across thresholds; its AUC summarizes ranking discrimination. The PR curve compares precision and recall, often revealing the burden of false positives more directly when positives are rare. A high ROC AUC does not guarantee adequate precision at a particular threshold. Average precision is a common PR summary measure, but may differ from trapezoidal integration of the curve. Confirm the exact definition when reporting results.
introduction.example:
There are 1000 samples, of which 10 are positive. A model gives TP=5, FP=5, FN=5, TN=985.
With class imbalance, accuracy can hide important differences. A single confusion matrix does not determine full ROC AUC or PR AUC.

exercise.question: Does raising the threshold always improve precision?
exercise.answer: No. The predicted-positive set shrinks, so recall cannot rise, but the positive proportion among remaining predictions can increase or decrease.

blocks.text: Result and explanation: With class imbalance, accuracy can hide important differences. A single confusion matrix does not determine full ROC AUC or PR AUC.
Pitfalls and limits: Do not substitute precision at one threshold for PR AUC, or infer a complete ranking absent from these counts.

worked.title: Imbalanced Evaluation: Two Very Different 99% Scores
worked.scenario: There are 1000 samples, of which 10 are positive. A model gives TP=5, FP=5, FN=5, TN=985.
steps: Predicting everything negative gives TN=990, FN=10 and the same 99% accuracy, but Recall=0.
The operating points share accuracy but differ in positive detections and false alarms requiring review. Choose using costs and thresholds.

introduction.definition: A sample is one example, such as an order. A feature is information available for prediction, such as price or a user's previous view count. A label is a supervised answer, such as whether the order was later canceled. Target is a broader term for the value or content the model is trained to predict or reconstruct: a class, number, next text segment, or image. Labels need not be manually annotated: next-word prediction gets its answers from the text itself. Distinguish answers available during training from information available at prediction time. If an answer unavailable at prediction time enters the input during training or evaluation, it causes data leakage.

introduction.definition: A learning-rate scheduler specifies how the learning rate changes. Step decay reduces it at specified points; exponential decay reduces it proportionally; cosine annealing follows a smooth cosine curve. ReduceLROnPlateau monitors a metric and lowers the rate when improvement stalls. These rules respond to either a fixed schedule or observed performance. Choose with the total training duration and the need for finer updates near the end in mind.
introduction.example: 例子：初始学习率 0.1，每完成两轮乘 0.5，则第 1–2 轮用 0.1、第 3–4 轮用 0.05。若调度器按优化器更新步数推进，梯度累积会改变每轮更新次数；需记录调用时点，不能把 epoch 与 step 混用。

introduction.definition: Full-batch gradient descent uses all training samples to compute an update direction. This gives a less noisy direction but is expensive for large datasets. Strictly, stochastic gradient descent can mean using one sample per update, although modern training commonly uses SGD to mean minibatch training. Minibatches give noisier directions but allow more frequent updates and hardware parallelism. Stochastic gradients are estimates from sampled data, not arbitrary changes to parameters.

introduction.definition: The sigmoid is a scalar function mapping any finite real score to a value strictly between zero and one. It is often used for binary labels or independently modeled multiple labels.
introduction.example: At z=0, the output is 0.5. At z=log(3), it is 0.75. Applying sigmoid separately to two scores does not require their outputs to sum to one.

introduction.definition: The sliding window maintains a contiguous interval, allowing the right end to incorporate new elements, the left end to remove old elements, and incrementally update status such as frequency. First define when the current range is legal, and then decide when to shrink. In the longest substring without repeated characters, once a new character causes repetition, the window will continue to be narrowed until there are no more repetitions, and then the maximum length will be updated.
introduction.example: For example, on the second b in abba, move left past both the leading a and the first b; removing just one character is insufficient. If using last-seen indices, set left to the maximum of its current value and the repeated character’s previous index plus one. This prevents left from moving backward at the final a.

worked.title: Sliding Window: Shrink Until a Duplicate Is Removed
worked.scenario: For the string abcaad, find the longest contiguous substring with no repeated character. Maintain a character set for [left,right].
steps: Read a, b and c to form abc of length 3. Before adding the next a, detect the duplicate, remove the leftmost a and advance left to 1.
The window becomes bca. The next a is another duplicate. Remove b, c and then a until the old a is gone, then insert the new a.
Finally read d. The current window ad has length 2; the best length remains 3. Each character is inserted and removed at most once.
worked.result: The answer is 3, achieved by abc or bca. Time O(n); set space O(min(n, alphabet size)).
worked.pitfall: Advancing left only once may leave an invalid window. A substring must be contiguous; it cannot skip characters in the middle.
worked.question: What is the answer for aaaa?
worked.answer: 1. Each new a requires removing the old a from the window.

depth.boundary: With negative values, interval sums are not monotonic under expansion; positive-array window rules do not apply unchanged.

introduction.definition: Softmax converts a vector of real class scores into nonnegative values summing to one. It is commonly used for a choice among mutually exclusive classes.
introduction.example: Scores [0,log(2)] produce probabilities [1/3,2/3]. Adding 100 to both scores gives the same probabilities. Increasing one class score changes the other probabilities through the shared denominator.

introduction.definition: For now, think of a tensor as a multidimensional array. Its shape gives its size along each direction; an axis identifies a direction of organization or computation. A color-image batch can have sample, channel, height, and width axes. “Dimension” may mean the number of axes or the size of one axis, so context matters. Embedding dimension usually means components per vector, not dataset sample count. Shape mismatches concern data alignment, not necessarily a flaw in the algorithm's principle.
introduction.example:
Predictions have shape [3,1] and labels have shape [3]. Use ordinary elementwise subtraction to calculate errors.
Wrong shapes can yield a valid computation with incorrect meaning. Check shapes, axis meanings and the expected output shape.

exercise.question: Why is this harder to detect at batch=1?
exercise.answer: Broadcasting [1,1] with [1] still produces one number, so small tests can hide the axis error.

introduction.definition: A classification threshold must still be chosen after predicting probabilities. Raising it usually produces fewer positive predictions but may miss more actual positives. The confusion matrix distinguishes true positives, false positives, true negatives and false negatives. Sensitivity usually means recall, or the true positive rate. Specificity measures the proportion of actual negatives correctly excluded. These measure different aspects of performance and should be discussed in terms of missed detections and false alarms.
introduction.example:
Scores [.95,.8,.7,.6,.4,.3,.2,.05] have true labels [1,0,1,0,1,0,0,0]. Predict positive when the score is at least the threshold.
Lowering the threshold expands the predicted-positive set. Recall cannot decrease, but precision need not be monotonic. The demo’s scores themselves do not change.

exercise.question: At threshold 1, what are the accuracy and recall?
exercise.answer: Every prediction is negative: accuracy is 5/8, recall is 0, and precision is undefined.

blocks.text: A classification threshold must still be chosen after predicting probabilities. Raising it usually produces fewer positive predictions but may miss more actual positives. The confusion matrix distinguishes true positives, false positives, true negatives and false negatives. Sensitivity usually means recall, or the true positive rate. Specificity measures the proportion of actual negatives correctly excluded. These measure different aspects of performance and should be discussed in terms of missed detections and false alarms.

worked.title: Thresholds: Recalculate the Confusion Matrix
worked.scenario: Scores [.95,.8,.7,.6,.4,.3,.2,.05] have true labels [1,0,1,0,1,0,0,0]. Predict positive when the score is at least the threshold.
steps: At threshold 0.5, the first four predictions are positive: two true positives and two false positives. The remainder contains one false negative and three true negatives.
Lowering the threshold to 0.4 finds the third actual positive: TP=3, FP=2, FN=0, TN=3.
worked.result: Lowering the threshold expands the predicted-positive set. Recall cannot decrease, but precision need not be monotonic. The demo’s scores themselves do not change.
worked.pitfall: With no predicted positives, the precision denominator is 0. The demo displays “undefined” rather than treating this as 100%. Applications must define their convention.
worked.question: At threshold 1, what are the accuracy and recall?
worked.answer: Every prediction is negative: accuracy is 5/8, recall is 0, and precision is undefined.

depth.boundary: Choose thresholds on validation data according to false-positive and false-negative costs.

introduction.definition: 词元（token）是分词器处理文本的离散单位，可以是一段字节、字符或子词。嵌入（embedding）把离散词元编号映射为可学习向量；编号本身的大小不代表语义距离。
introduction.example: 玩具词表中编号 7 的向量为 (0.2,−0.4)，编号 9 为 (0.1,0.6)，序列 [7,9,7] 得到三行二维向量。相同编号查到相同初始向量，但经上下文网络后，两个位置的表示可以不同。金融文本还需检查文本实际到达时间。

blocks.text: 词表大小为 V、向量维度为 d 时，嵌入矩阵 $E\in\mathbb R^{V\times d}$；编号 i 的向量为第 i 行 Eᵢ。长度 L 的序列查表后形状为 L×d。分词器版本决定文本怎样转成编号，后续注意力处理上下文，这两步不能混成一个定义。

depth.boundary: A token need not correspond to one character or one word.

introduction.definition: For Course Schedule, encode prerequisites as directed edges. Enqueue every zero-in-degree vertex, process it, and decrement its successors’ in-degrees. Enqueue a successor when its in-degree reaches zero. All courses are feasible exactly when all vertices are processed; otherwise the remaining graph contains a directed cycle. Include isolated courses in the total.
introduction.example:
Dependencies are A→C, B→C, C→D and D→E; F has none. An edge means its source must finish before its destination.
Without the cycle, one topological order contains all 6 nodes. With it, only 3 nodes are processed, proving no topological order covers the whole graph. Time O(V+E).

exercise.question: Is checking only the subgraph reachable from one starting node enough?
exercise.answer: No. Another component may contain a cycle. Count processed nodes across all V nodes.

blocks.text: A DFS alternative uses visitation colors. Encountering a vertex that is still on the active recursion path reveals a directed cycle; encountering a fully processed vertex does not. A topological order exists only for a DAG. Ordinary BFS without dependency bookkeeping does not provide this test.

worked.title: Topological Sorting: An Empty Queue Can Reveal a Cycle
worked.scenario: Dependencies are A→C, B→C, C→D and D→E; F has none. An edge means its source must finish before its destination.
steps: Compute indegrees. A, B and F have indegree 0 and enter the queue. Removing A and B decreases C’s indegree; enqueue C only when it reaches 0.
C then releases D, and D releases E. F must also appear in the output despite being isolated.
Adding E→C leaves the queue empty after processing A, B and F, while C, D and E remain unprocessed in a directed cycle.
worked.result: Without the cycle, one topological order contains all 6 nodes. With it, only 3 nodes are processed, proving no topological order covers the whole graph. Time O(V+E).
worked.pitfall: Topological orders are usually not unique. Processing some nodes does not establish that the entire dependency graph is executable.
worked.question: Is checking only the subgraph reachable from one starting node enough?
worked.answer: No. Another component may contain a cycle. Count processed nodes across all V nodes.

depth.boundary: If the in-degree algorithm cannot process every vertex, a directed cycle exists. Encountering a previously visited vertex alone is insufficient evidence.

introduction.definition: Training and evaluation modes control the behavior of layers such as Dropout and BatchNorm. Disabling gradient recording controls whether the information needed for backpropagation is recorded. These are separate: switching to evaluation mode does not disable every gradient, and disabling gradients does not change Dropout’s training behavior. Set both correctly during evaluation or deployment for stable behavior and efficient resource use.
introduction.example: 例子：验证时设 eval 会关闭通常的 dropout 随机屏蔽，但并不自动关闭梯度记录；再使用 no_grad 才省去反传图。相反，train 配合 no_grad 仍可能更新 BatchNorm 运行统计。两组开关职责独立。

introduction.definition: A transaction treats several data operations as one logical unit. ACID names four classic properties: atomicity, consistency, isolation, and durability. A bank transfer is a familiar example: the debit and credit should succeed or fail together. Transactional consistency here should not be casually conflated with consistency models in distributed systems.
introduction.example:
Account A holds 100 and B holds 20. Transfer 30, expecting A=70 and B=50.
Atomicity makes grouped operations succeed or fail together. Isolation handles concurrent interleavings. Durability relies on commit and recovery mechanisms.

exercise.question: The database committed, but the client received no response. Is an immediate retry always safe?
exercise.answer: No. It may repeat the transfer. Use a business idempotency key or queryable operation status.

blocks.text: OLTP, online transaction processing, emphasizes many short read/write transactions, such as orders and transfers. OLAP, online analytical processing, emphasizes aggregation, statistics, and complex analysis, such as business reports. Data warehouses favor structured analytics; data lakes hold varied raw data; lakehouses try to combine their advantages. Row stores suit operations on individual records, while column stores often suit scanning a few columns for large-scale statistics.

worked.title: Transactions: What If a Transfer Fails Halfway?
worked.scenario: Account A holds 100 and B holds 20. Transfer 30, expecting A=70 and B=50.
steps: If A is debited before B is credited and the process crashes between them, unprotected writes may leave only the debit.
Place both updates in one transaction. Failure before commit should roll them back; a successful commit includes both updates.
Use conditional updates or appropriate concurrency control to check balances, preventing two transfers from both being approved against stale balances.
worked.result: Atomicity makes grouped operations succeed or fail together. Isolation handles concurrent interleavings. Durability relies on commit and recovery mechanisms.
worked.pitfall: Placing two statements next to each other does not create a transaction. Cross-database or external-payment operations also need suitable protocols and idempotency.
worked.question: The database committed, but the client received no response. Is an immediate retry always safe?
worked.answer: No. It may repeat the transfer. Use a business idempotency key or queryable operation status.

depth.boundary: Different isolation levels have different observable behaviors during concurrency.

introduction.definition: Two pointers maintain two positions in a sequence and move them according to a task-specific invariant. The technique is useful when movements eliminate possibilities without requiring a restart.
introduction.example: For sorted [1,2,4,7] and target 6, endpoints sum to 8, so move the right pointer to 4. The sum becomes 5, so advance left to 2 and find 2+4=6. The same elimination is not valid on an unsorted array.

exercise.question: 用自己的话解释：上面的情景为什么是“Two Pointers”的例子？请指出定义中的关键条件在情景里如何体现，而不是只复述最后的数值。
exercise.definition: Two pointers maintain two positions in a sequence and move them according to a task-specific invariant. The technique is useful when movements eliminate possibilities without requiring a restart.
exercise.evidence: For sorted [1,2,4,7] and target 6, endpoints sum to 8, so move the right pointer to 4. The sum becomes 5, so advance left to 2 and find 2+4=6. The same elimination is not valid on an unsorted array.

blocks.text: For target-sum search in a sorted array, use left and right endpoints. If their sum is too small, advance left; if too large, decrease right. Sorting supplies the monotonicity needed to discard pairs. Each pointer moves at most n times.

depth.boundary: Two indices are not a proof; justify moves using ordering, bounds, or another elimination argument.

introduction.definition: A VAE maps observations through an encoder to a probability distribution over latent variables, then reconstructs or generates samples with a decoder. Training combines reconstruction with constraints on the latent distribution, making sampling from a simple prior useful. The distinguishing feature is probabilistic latent-variable modeling, not merely dimensionality reduction. Latent variables can be ignored in some settings, so check what information the model actually uses.
introduction.example: 例子：生成一张图时，VAE 可先抽潜变量再解码，GAN 用生成器把噪声映射为图像，扩散模型从噪声开始多步去噪。三者即使输出同尺寸图像，训练目标与采样步骤也不同，不能把扩散的去噪步数解释成 VAE 的网络层数。

introduction.definition: Embodied AI studies how agents with bodies or action interfaces perceive, decide and act. Robot learning develops control abilities from data. VLA, or vision–language–action modeling, is an important research direction. Typical inputs include camera observations, language tasks and sometimes the robot’s internal state; outputs are executable action representations.
introduction.example: 例子：输入相机图像和“把红杯放到托盘上”的指令，VLA 输出一段动作表示。将动作转换为机械臂命令前，还需校准坐标、检查执行范围与碰撞。语言上描述正确的动作不等于真实机器人已经安全完成。

exercise.question: 用自己的话解释：上面的情景为什么是“VLA — Vision-Language-Action Model”的例子？请指出定义中的关键条件在情景里如何体现，而不是只复述最后的数值。
exercise.definition: Embodied AI studies how agents with bodies or action interfaces perceive, decide and act. Robot learning develops control abilities from data. VLA, or vision–language–action modeling, is an important research direction. Typical inputs include camera observations, language tasks and sometimes the robot’s internal state; outputs are executable action representations.
exercise.evidence: 例子：输入相机图像和“把红杯放到托盘上”的指令，VLA 输出一段动作表示。将动作转换为机械臂命令前，还需校准坐标、检查执行范围与碰撞。语言上描述正确的动作不等于真实机器人已经安全完成。

blocks.text: Compare the roles of LLMs, VLMs and VLAs. An LLM primarily processes language and related symbol sequences. A VLM combines visual inputs with language. A VLA must go beyond describing a cup on a table to outputting actions that move an arm to pick it up. It must decide what to do as well as interpret what it sees.

Action chunking predicts a short sequence of future actions at once, rather than one control instant. This can reduce generation frequency and short-term jitter, but still requires timely adjustments from new observations. Diffusion Policy generates action sequences with diffusion methods. ACT, Action Chunking with Transformers, is a representative imitation learning method using action chunks. Some VLA systems also use flow matching for continuous action generation.

VLA systems face costly demonstration collection, demanding action precision, varied robot platforms, latency, collisions and safety constraints. Correct visual or language answers do not establish reliable physical execution. Describe the process as perception, instruction understanding, action generation and feedback control.

depth.boundary: A policy using vision alone is not necessarily a vision-language-action model.

introduction.definition: Warmup first uses a smaller learning rate at the beginning of training, and then gradually increases it to the target level. Its purpose is to get training off to a smoother start, rather than letting the GPU heat up first. Then other scheduling methods are usually added. Not all models must use warmup; warmup that is too long can also eat up the effective training budget. Warmup is different from warm start: the latter usually refers to continuing from an existing model or state, rather than starting over from random initialization.
introduction.example: 例子：目标学习率为 0.001，线性 warmup 五次更新，可依次用 0.0002、0.0004、0.0006、0.0008、0.001。warm start 则从既有参数继续训练；恢复优化器、调度器与随机状态是否同时恢复，需要另行说明。

introduction.definition: Weight decay discourages excessively large weights. AdamW decouples it from Adam’s adaptive gradient scaling instead of treating it as an ordinary gradient term. For basic SGD, L2 regularization and weight decay can be equivalent under common conditions; that equivalence does not carry over directly to adaptive optimizers. In an interview, explain that the W in AdamW refers to decoupled weight decay, rather than describing it simply as faster Adam.
introduction.example:
Use the simplified decoupled update θ_next=(1-ηλ)θ-ηg for shrinkage and gradient updates, with θ=2, η=0.1, λ=0.01 and g=0.4.
Weight decay shrinks parameters during an update; learning-rate decay describes how η changes over time. Their numerical effects interact because shrinkage contains ηλ.

exercise.question: If g=0, can weight decay still update the parameter?
exercise.answer: Yes. If ηλ is nonzero and decay applies to that parameter, the equation still performs θ←(1-ηλ)θ.

worked.title: Weight Decay and Learning-Rate Decay: Different Controls
worked.scenario: Use the simplified decoupled update θ_next=(1-ηλ)θ-ηg for shrinkage and gradient updates, with θ=2, η=0.1, λ=0.01 and g=0.4.
steps: The shrinkage factor is 0.999, giving the shrunk parameter 1.998.
The gradient term is 0.04, giving 1.958 after the update. With λ=0, the same step gives 1.96.
Reducing the next step’s learning rate to 0.01 changes the schedule for η. λ still sets parameter shrinkage strength.
worked.result: Weight decay shrinks parameters during an update; learning-rate decay describes how η changes over time. Their numerical effects interact because shrinkage contains ηλ.
worked.pitfall: Here g denotes the update direction. Actual AdamW adjusts gradients using momentum and second-moment statistics, so this direction is not simply the raw gradient.
worked.question: If g=0, can weight decay still update the parameter?
worked.answer: Yes. If ηλ is nonzero and decay applies to that parameter, the equation still performs θ←(1-ηλ)θ.

depth.boundary: Weight decay differs from learning-rate decay; equivalence to an L2 penalty depends on the optimizer.

introduction.definition: A world model learns a model of the environment: its current state and how that state may change after actions. It need not generate high-resolution images or be a natural language model. It can predict future scenes at pixel level, or predict compressed internal states or representations.
introduction.example:
One-dimensional position x starts at 0 and targets 5. The real system follows x_next=x+u+wind, while the predictor ignores wind. Actions are restricted to [-1,1].
Closed-loop feedback changes accumulated error, but a proportional policy without wind compensation cannot eliminate every offset. The demo shows predicted and actual next positions together.

exercise.question: With zero wind, what happens after the feedback policy reaches 5?
exercise.answer: Its action becomes 0 and position remains 5. The fixed-action policy keeps moving by 1 each step.

blocks.text: Imagine a football agent observing player positions, ball velocity and defensive formations. A policy directly chooses whether to pass or shoot. A system with a world model can also predict how the defense might change over the next two seconds after a pass to a teammate on the left. It can compare predicted outcomes before choosing an action.

A physics simulator, such as a rigid-body dynamics engine, explicitly implements physical rules. A learned world model infers environmental dynamics from data. Simulators often make their rules clearer but can be costly to model or run; learned models are flexible but need not be physically accurate. Hybrid models combine known physics with learned components.

Causal modeling asks whether changing an action causes a particular outcome. A counterfactual asks what would have happened had a different action been taken. Predictive uncertainty matters: when a world model lacks relevant experience, the system should recognize that its predictions may be unreliable. Compounding error is central to long-horizon prediction. Partial observability means that sensors often reveal only part of the true state.

In an interview, distinguish a VLA from a world model by its role. A VLA maps observations and goals to actions; a world model predicts environmental change. A VLA system may have no explicit world model, or may use one to support planning, check predicted action consequences or generate training data.

There is no general-purpose world model that reliably simulates every real scenario. World modeling encompasses active research in video prediction, abstract representations, self-supervised learning, interactive environments, control and planning. Understanding these limits supports more precise discussion than listing model names alone.

worked.title: World Models: Prediction Error and Feedback Correction
worked.scenario: One-dimensional position x starts at 0 and targets 5. The real system follows x_next=x+u+wind, while the predictor ignores wind. Actions are restricted to [-1,1].
steps: A fixed-action policy always uses u=1. With wind=-0.3, each real movement is only 0.7, so predictions and observations diverge.
A feedback policy observes again each step and uses u=clip(5-x,-1,1). Its action shrinks as it approaches the target.
With wind=-0.3, feedback settles near 4.7, retaining a steady-state offset. Fixed actions continue past the target.
worked.result: Closed-loop feedback changes accumulated error, but a proportional policy without wind compensation cannot eliminate every offset. The demo shows predicted and actual next positions together.
worked.pitfall: This is not full MPC: it neither optimizes a multistep action sequence nor trains a world model. The simplified dynamics illustrate prediction, observation and feedback.
worked.question: With zero wind, what happens after the feedback policy reaches 5?
worked.answer: Its action becomes 0 and position remains 5. The fixed-action policy keeps moving by 1 each step.

depth.boundary: Realistic video does not automatically provide reliable action-conditioned prediction or control.

introduction.definition: 清空梯度是重置已累积的参数梯度；detach 是切断某条计算路径的梯度传播。它们操作的对象和目的不同。
introduction.example: 可以把累积梯度想成记账本：清空梯度是翻到新的一页；detach 像规定某条支路的结果只供读取，不沿这条支路追溯责任。

exercise.question: 对一个中间张量 detach，就等于清空整个模型已有的梯度吗？
exercise.answer: 不是。detach 影响该计算路径的传播，不会自动把参数上已经累积的梯度清掉，也不代表冻结整个模型。

blocks.text: Some frameworks accumulate new gradients onto existing ones by default, so clear gradients at the appropriate update boundaries. Failing to clear them can count old gradients again; clearing them too early defeats intended accumulation. Detach and stop-gradient operations block gradient propagation along a path, for example in target networks, teacher branches or unnecessary computation graphs. Detaching does not necessarily copy the underlying data and does not freeze the entire model.

depth.boundary: detach does not automatically copy storage or freeze the entire model.

introduction.definition: An array stores elements in sequential, indexable positions, enabling fast access by position. A dynamic array can grow; Python lists broadly belong to this category. A linked list connects nodes through pointers and supports insertion and deletion at certain positions, but is poor at random access. A stack is last-in, first-out, like a stack of plates; it commonly supports function calls and undo operations. A queue is first-in, first-out, like a line of people taking numbers; it commonly supports task scheduling. A deque, or double-ended queue, allows insertion and removal at both ends.
introduction.example: 例子：栈先压入 A 再压入 B，下一次 pop 返回 B，体现后进先出。用它检查括号“([])”时先遇到左括号就压入，右括号必须与栈顶匹配；单纯记录左右括号数量相等不足以判断顺序合法。

exercise.definition: An array stores elements in sequential, indexable positions, enabling fast access by position. A dynamic array can grow; Python lists broadly belong to this category. A linked list connects nodes through pointers and supports insertion and deletion at certain positions, but is poor at random access. A stack is last-in, first-out, like a stack of plates; it commonly supports function calls and undo operations. A queue is first-in, first-out, like a line of people taking numbers; it commonly supports task scheduling. A deque, or double-ended queue, allows insertion and removal at both ends.
exercise.evidence: 例子：栈先压入 A 再压入 B，下一次 pop 返回 B，体现后进先出。用它检查括号“([])”时先遇到左括号就压入，右括号必须与栈顶匹配；单纯记录左右括号数量相等不足以判断顺序合法。

introduction.definition: 贪心算法每一步根据当前规则作出一个选择，并希望这些局部选择能组成全局解。是否正确需要证明，不能只凭“这一步看起来最好”。
introduction.example: 面额只有 1 元和 3 元时，凑 6 元可连续选两枚 3 元。但换成 1、3、4 元，先选 4 元会用三枚硬币，而两枚 3 元更少。

exercise.question: “每次选最大面额”在一套硬币上成功，能否保证它对所有面额都正确？
exercise.answer: 不能。1、3、4 元凑 6 元就是反例。正确性依赖问题结构，需要交换论证或其他证明。

blocks.text: Divide and conquer splits a large problem into smaller ones, solves them separately, and combines their results; merge sort is a classic example. Dynamic programming handles overlapping subproblems by recording intermediate results to avoid recomputation. A greedy algorithm makes the locally best choice at each step and guarantees a global optimum only when the problem has the required properties. Backtracking systematically tries alternatives and undoes earlier choices when they fail, as in Sudoku and combinatorial search. Branch and bound uses upper and lower bounds to discard branches that cannot improve the current solution.

worked.title: Binary Search on the Answer: Test a Candidate Limit
worked.scenario: Keep nonnegative tasks [7,2,5,10,8] in order. Split them into at most 2 nonempty contiguous groups, minimizing the largest group sum.
steps: The answer is at least the largest item, 10, and at most the total, 32.
Limit 17 permits [7,2,5] with sum 14, then [10], but the final 8 requires a third group. It is infeasible.
Limit 18 permits [7,2,5] and [10,8]. Binary search finds the smallest feasible limit, 18.
worked.result: The optimal largest group sum is 18, splitting between 5 and 10. Each check costs O(n); integer search takes about O(n log U).
worked.pitfall: The greedy check requires nonnegative values. With negatives, a later item can reduce a temporarily excessive sum, so the same check is invalid.
worked.question: What is the answer if at most one group is allowed?
worked.answer: 32. All tasks must remain together.

worked.title: A Greedy Counterexample: Most Jobs Versus Greatest Reward
worked.scenario: Use A=(1,3,5), B=(2,5,100), C=(3,6,5), D=(6,7,4). Touching endpoints do not conflict.
steps: For maximum job count, earliest-finish selection chooses A,C,D: 3 jobs.
For maximum reward, that selection earns only 14, while B,D earn 104.
Changing only the objective requires a new proof that a choice is safe. Weighted interval DP can solve the reward version.
worked.result: A familiar rule does not automatically apply to every superficially similar scheduling problem.
worked.pitfall: Do not automatically sort intervals by start or finish and apply greedy selection. Clarify the objective, compatibility conditions and resource limits first.
worked.question: If every reward is 1, do the objectives still conflict?
worked.answer: No. Maximizing reward becomes maximizing count, recovering the unweighted conclusion.

depth.boundary: A locally attractive choice need not be globally correct; justify it through elimination or exchange.

introduction.definition: 复杂度描述输入规模增加时，算法消耗的时间或存储如何增长。它关心增长趋势，而不是某次运行恰好用了几毫秒。
introduction.example: 查名单时，逐个找可能需要检查整张名单；按位置直接取第十项则不必从头找。名单变长后，两种工作的增长方式不同。

exercise.question: 一段 O(n) 程序在一次测试中比 O(n²) 慢，能否据此否定复杂度分析？
exercise.answer: 不能。常数、实现和输入规模都影响实际用时。复杂度比较的是在所声明模型下随规模增长的趋势。

blocks.text: An algorithm is a sequence of clear steps for solving a problem. Time complexity describes how computational cost grows with input size; space complexity describes how memory requirements grow. Big O notation primarily concerns growth rates, rather than the actual number of seconds on a particular computer. Better theoretical complexity does not guarantee faster execution on every small input.

worked.title: Dynamic Arrays: Amortizing Expensive Growth
worked.scenario: Initial capacity is 1 and doubles when full. Append 8 elements, ignoring allocator overhead.
steps: Growing to capacities 2,4,8 copies 1,2,4 existing elements respectively: 7 copies in total.
Eight writes plus seven copies give 15 units of work. One append can be expensive, but total work is still proportional to 8.
A ninth append grows capacity to 16 and copies 8 elements. Total copies become 15 and total work 24, still below 3×9.
worked.result: With geometric capacity growth, a geometric series bounds n appends by O(n) total work, giving O(1) amortized cost per append.
worked.pitfall: Amortized O(1) does not mean worst-case O(1) for every append. Growing by one slot each time instead copies 1+2+…+(n-1) elements.
worked.question: Can old storage be ignored immediately during growth?
worked.answer: No. Old and new arrays can coexist during copying. Analyze peak memory and reclamation separately.

depth.boundary: Loop nesting alone does not determine complexity; include data-structure operations and output size.

introduction.definition: 递归是把一个问题交给同样的方法处理更小的子问题，再把子问题的结果接回来。必须有能直接回答的终止情形，而且每次调用都要向它靠近。
introduction.example: 计算 3! 时，先等 2! 的结果；计算 2! 时，先等 1!；约定 $0! = 1$ 后，逐层返回得到 1、1、2、6。每一层都要记住返回后还要乘的数。
introduction.story: 一队人排好队，每个人只看得见后一个人。队首问“从我开始有几个人？”每个人都问后一个人，再把答案加一。队尾直接回答“一人”，答案沿队伍传回来。队尾对应终止条件，每个人记住“还要加一”对应调用栈；如果没有人能认出队尾，这个问法就无法结束。

exercise.question: 函数调用了自己，就一定是正确的递归吗？
exercise.answer: 不一定。还要有终止条件，并保证子问题在合法输入下能到达它。例如计算 F(n) 时仍调用 F(n)，问题没有缩小，会持续调用而不能得到结果。

blocks.text: Recursion is a procedure solving a problem by calling itself on smaller or simpler instances. It requires a base case and progress toward that case. The call stack stores the suspended work of each invocation.

For factorial, F(0)=1 and F(n)=nF(n-1) for nonnegative integers n. The base case stops the calls. This implementation takes O(n) multiplications and O(n) stack depth without a transformation that removes those frames.
F(3) calls F(2), then F(1), then F(0); returning upward gives 1, 1, 2, 6. A missing base case or calling F(n) again instead of a smaller instance does not make progress and can exhaust the stack.

depth.boundary: Tree return values, search-path state, and backtracking undo have different semantics.

introduction.definition: A data structure organizes values and their relationships so operations have defined costs. Arrays store indexed sequences, linked lists connect nodes, hash tables support key lookup, and trees or graphs represent structured relationships.
introduction.example: If a task repeatedly reads the i-th measurement, an array is a natural fit. If it repeatedly asks whether an identifier has been seen, a hash set avoids scanning the whole sequence for each query. Neither choice is universally faster for every workload.

exercise.question: 用自己的话解释：上面的情景为什么是“Data Structures”的例子？请指出定义中的关键条件在情景里如何体现，而不是只复述最后的数值。
exercise.definition: A data structure organizes values and their relationships so operations have defined costs. Arrays store indexed sequences, linked lists connect nodes, hash tables support key lookup, and trees or graphs represent structured relationships.
exercise.evidence: If a task repeatedly reads the i-th measurement, an array is a natural fit. If it repeatedly asks whether an identifier has been seen, a hash set avoids scanning the whole sequence for each query. Neither choice is universally faster for every workload.

blocks.text: Choose by operations, not only by element count n. Array indexing is O(1); inserting into its middle can require O(n) moves. Hash-table lookup is expected O(1) under suitable hashing and load assumptions, while worst cases and resizing differ.

depth.boundary: A data structure supplies operations rather than determining the entire task’s algorithm.

introduction.definition: A tree is a hierarchical structure. Each node in a binary tree has at most two children. A binary search tree uses ordering to support search. AVL trees and red-black trees are balanced binary search trees that avoid excessive depth. A heap is another tree-based structure: rather than sorting all elements completely, it makes the minimum or maximum easy to retrieve. A priority queue, often implemented with a heap, schedules the most urgent task.
introduction.example:
Find the two largest values in [9,1,7,3,8]. First clarify whether output must be ordered, input may be modified, and data arrives continuously.
A heap suits streaming updates: time O(n log k), auxiliary space O(k). Quickselect suits mutable static data. The constraints determine the choice.

exercise.question: Data keeps arriving and Top K must be available at any time. What should be considered first?
exercise.answer: A fixed-size heap is usually convenient for incremental maintenance. Also discuss costs when k is close to n and the overhead of returning sorted results.

worked.title: Top K: Let Requirements Determine the Algorithm
worked.scenario: Find the two largest values in [9,1,7,3,8]. First clarify whether output must be ordered, input may be modified, and data arrives continuously.
steps: Keep a min-heap of size 2, whose root is the current second-largest value. Reading 9 and 1 gives {1,9}; 7 replaces 1, 3 is ignored, and 8 replaces 7.
The retained values are {8,9}. Descending output still requires sorting those two results.
A static array can instead use quickselect to find the boundary in average O(n) time. It rearranges the array, leaves the selected region unsorted, and its worst case depends on pivot selection.
worked.result: A heap suits streaming updates: time O(n log k), auxiliary space O(k). Quickselect suits mutable static data. The constraints determine the choice.
worked.pitfall: “Quickselect is faster than sorting” is incomplete without average versus worst-case cost, output ordering and input mutation requirements.
worked.question: Data keeps arriving and Top K must be available at any time. What should be considered first?
worked.answer: A fixed-size heap is usually convenient for incremental maintenance. Also discuss costs when k is close to n and the overhead of returning sorted results.

worked.title: Dijkstra: Why Old Distances Remain in the Queue
worked.scenario: Directed edges are A→B=5, A→C=1, C→B=1, B→D=2 and C→D=7. Start from A.
steps: After A, candidates are B=5 and C=1. Processing C first improves B to 2 and D to 8.
Processing the new B=2 improves D to 4. Old entries B=5 and D=8 may still be queued.
Next process D=4. When B=5 is popped, skip it because it differs from current dist[B]=2. Likewise skip D=8.
worked.result: Distances are A=0, C=1, B=2, D=4. The shortest route to D is A-C-B-D.
worked.pitfall: The demo sorts a small list to display candidates; it is not an efficient heap implementation. Heap complexity bounds do not describe that display container.
worked.question: If C→B=-4 is allowed, does the same nonnegative-weight proof apply?
worked.answer: No. Negative edges may lower a finalized distance. Choose another method according to the constraints.

depth.boundary: A heap is not totally ordered; its underlying array is not a sorted result.

introduction.definition: Rabin–Karp computes rolling hashes for sliding text windows, quickly filters candidate positions, and verifies the actual characters to guard against collisions. Aho–Corasick organizes many keywords into a trie and adds failure links, finding many patterns in a single scan. It suits dictionary matching and log-rule detection. One uses compact summaries to reduce comparisons; the other shares structure across patterns. Both reuse existing information.
introduction.example:
Patterns he, she and hers; text ushers, with zero-based indices 0…5.
Matches include she, he and hers. Producing every match costs time, so complexity must include output count.

exercise.question: If only the existence of any match matters, must all positions be stored?
exercise.answer: No. Return after the first match. This changes output cost, but the structure’s semantics must remain correct.

blocks.text: Rabin–Karp computes rolling hashes for sliding text windows, quickly filters candidate positions, and verifies the actual characters to guard against collisions. Aho–Corasick organizes many keywords into a trie and adds failure links, finding many patterns in a single scan. It suits dictionary matching and log-rule detection. One uses compact summaries to reduce comparisons; the other shares structure across patterns. Both reuse existing information.

worked.title: Multiple Patterns: Several Words Can End at One Position
worked.scenario: Patterns he, she and hers; text ushers, with zero-based indices 0…5.
steps: At index 3, character e completes she over [1,3].
The same position also completes suffix he over [2,3]. Failure links and output relationships must retain this match.
Reading r and s completes hers over [2,5]. Matches may overlap; finding one long word does not permit skipping all its characters.
worked.result: Matches include she, he and hers. Producing every match costs time, so complexity must include output count.
worked.pitfall: Checking only the current trie node’s terminal marker can miss shorter patterns on its failure chain.
worked.question: If only the existence of any match matters, must all positions be stored?
worked.answer: No. Return after the first match. This changes output cost, but the structure’s semantics must remain correct.

depth.boundary: Storage depends on created nodes and child representations. Merely stating linear operation time is incomplete.

introduction.definition: A graph consists of vertices and edges. Graph algorithms solve tasks such as reachability, traversal, shortest paths and dependency ordering. Directed edges distinguish source and destination; weighted edges attach a cost.
introduction.example: For edges A→B, A→C and B→D, BFS from A reaches B and C after one edge and D after two. Replacing edge counts by arbitrary travel costs does not preserve this BFS distance result.

exercise.question: 用自己的话解释：上面的情景为什么是“Graph Algorithms”的例子？请指出定义中的关键条件在情景里如何体现，而不是只复述最后的数值。
exercise.definition: A graph consists of vertices and edges. Graph algorithms solve tasks such as reachability, traversal, shortest paths and dependency ordering. Directed edges distinguish source and destination; weighted edges attach a cost.
exercise.evidence: For edges A→B, A→C and B→D, BFS from A reaches B and C after one edge and D after two. Replacing edge counts by arbitrary travel costs does not preserve this BFS distance result.

blocks.text: For V vertices and E edges in an adjacency-list representation, BFS and DFS take O(V+E). BFS gives shortest edge counts in an unweighted graph. Weighted shortest paths require an algorithm whose weight assumptions match the data.

depth.boundary: Whether the graph is directed, whether the edge weights are non-negative, and whether the weights are equal will change the applicable algorithm.

applications.title: Motion Planning · 图搜索在机器人路径中的应用
applications.reason: 复用节点、边和路径成本的定义，机器人页面补充构型、碰撞与轨迹可行性。

introduction.definition: 操作系统是管理处理器、内存和设备，并为程序提供受控使用方式的软件。进程是程序运行时的资源与隔离边界，线程是其中的执行单元。
introduction.example: 电脑同时播放音乐和编辑文档，操作系统安排它们获得处理器时间和内存。就像管理员安排多个住户使用公共设施，而不是让每个住户直接改动整栋楼的管线。

exercise.question: 两个程序都使用地址 0x1000，是否一定在读写同一块物理内存？
exercise.answer: 不是。进程通常有各自的虚拟地址空间，相同虚拟地址可以映射到不同物理内存；共享内存需要另外建立安排。

blocks.text: 操作系统管理进程、线程、内存与设备，并向应用提供受控接口。进程提供资源与隔离边界，线程是进程内部的执行单元；锁和死锁属于并发机制，不能代替操作系统本身的定义。
虚拟地址由进程地址空间映射，系统调用进入内核完成受保护的操作。调度器分配执行机会，文件描述符等句柄引用系统资源。并发表示任务时间区间重叠，是否同时在不同核心执行还取决于硬件与调度。
两个进程各自使用虚拟地址 0x1000，可以映射到不同物理内存。一个进程的两个线程通常共享地址空间，同时更新共享计数可能发生竞争；需要按并发契约同步，不能因地址相同就把跨进程和进程内共享混为一谈。

depth.boundary: Concurrency and parallelism describe task progress and execution; blocking and asynchrony describe waiting and control flow.

introduction.definition: Networks enable data transfer between devices. An IP address identifies a communication endpoint. A packet is a unit of network-transmitted data. Routers forward packets toward their destinations. DNS, the Domain Name System, resolves human-readable domain names to relevant network addresses.
introduction.example: 例子：浏览器查询服务名得到地址，再建立传输连接并发送 HTTP 请求。一次应用请求可分成多个网络包；某包重传与用户重试完整业务请求不是同一件事。业务重试仍需用操作身份防止重复处理。

exercise.question: 用自己的话解释：上面的情景为什么是“Network”的例子？请指出定义中的关键条件在情景里如何体现，而不是只复述最后的数值。
exercise.definition: Networks enable data transfer between devices. An IP address identifies a communication endpoint. A packet is a unit of network-transmitted data. Routers forward packets toward their destinations. DNS, the Domain Name System, resolves human-readable domain names to relevant network addresses.
exercise.evidence: 例子：浏览器查询服务名得到地址，再建立传输连接并发送 HTTP 请求。一次应用请求可分成多个网络包；某包重传与用户重试完整业务请求不是同一件事。业务重试仍需用操作身份防止重复处理。

blocks.text: A simplified page request proceeds as follows. The user enters a URL; the device resolves an address through DNS, establishes the necessary network connection and secure session, and sends an HTTP request. The server processes it, perhaps accesses a database, and returns HTML, JSON, or other resources. The browser then loads styles, scripts, and images and renders the page.

Latency measures round-trip waiting or response time; bandwidth is a link's data-carrying capacity; throughput is the data transfer actually achieved. A CDN, or content delivery network, caches content closer to users. A load balancer distributes requests across service instances. A reverse proxy receives and forwards requests on a server's behalf. A firewall restricts network traffic according to rules.

A retry repeats a request after a failure; a timeout prevents indefinite waiting. Exponential backoff increases the wait after successive failures. Adding random jitter helps prevent clients from retrying simultaneously. Idempotency means that repeating an operation has the same final effect as performing it once. Payment services often require idempotency request IDs because clients may retry after network timeouts, but must not charge repeatedly.

depth.boundary: Latency and throughput are different indicators, and service reliability also involves retries and idempotence.

introduction.definition: Consensus protocols let nodes agree on particular state updates; Raft is one common algorithm. Leader election decides who coordinates certain operations. Distributed locks coordinate shared resources across machines but can introduce difficult failure boundaries. Exactly-once processing is often an end-to-end effect built using transactions, idempotency, and deduplication, not a network that never retransmits.
introduction.example: 例子：五个投票节点的多数为 3。某条日志只有两个节点确认时，不能仅因其中一个是 leader 就当作已提交。协议还需处理任期与日志规则；多数算术本身并不是一份完整的共识实现。

introduction.definition: Round robin distributes requests among instances in turn with little overhead. Least connections sends new work to instances with fewer connections, which can help when request durations vary, although connection count is not a perfect load measure. Consistent hashing maps objects and nodes into a stable assignment structure, reducing key movement when nodes join or leave; it commonly supports sharding and cache placement. All allocate work or data, but consistent hashing specifically preserves mapping stability under membership changes.
introduction.example:
Cache capacity is 2. Display most recently used entries on the left. Execute put(1), put(2), get(1), put(3), get(2).
Accessing 1 changes the later eviction choice. A hash table plus doubly linked list gives typical operations expected O(1) time and uses O(capacity) space.

exercise.question: At capacity 3, would get(2) still miss?
exercise.answer: No. Inserting 3 would not exceed capacity, so 2 would remain cached.

blocks.text: LRU evicts the least recently accessed data, exploiting temporal locality. LFU evicts less frequently accessed data and can suit stable long-term popularity, but may retain formerly popular items too long. When a hot cache entry expires, many requests may hit the database simultaneously. Request coalescing, mutually exclusive rebuilding, early refresh, and expiration jitter address different bursts. Caching policy includes both what to evict and how to recover after expiration or failure.
Scenario and inputs: Cache capacity is 2. Display most recently used entries on the left. Execute put(1), put(2), get(1), put(3), get(2).

worked.title: LRU: One Access Changes the Eviction Choice
worked.scenario: Cache capacity is 2. Display most recently used entries on the left. Execute put(1), put(2), get(1), put(3), get(2).
steps: The first two writes give [2,1]. get(1) hits and moves 1 to the front, giving [1,2].
put(3) exceeds capacity, evicts least recently used 2, and leaves [3,1].
get(2) misses, leaving [3,1]. A hash table locates nodes; a doubly linked list moves them to the front and removes the tail.
worked.result: Accessing 1 changes the later eviction choice. A hash table plus doubly linked list gives typical operations expected O(1) time and uses O(capacity) space.
worked.pitfall: The demo displays order with a short array; that array implementation is not O(1). LRU does not evict by insertion time or guarantee the optimal hit rate.
worked.question: At capacity 3, would get(2) still miss?
worked.answer: No. Inserting 3 would not exceed capacity, so 2 would remain cached.

depth.boundary: LRU decides which entry to evict; a KV cache reuses attention keys and values. They operate on different data and constraints.

introduction.definition: Feature engineering turns raw observations into inputs suitable for a prediction task. It includes defining units, aggregations, missing-value behavior and transformations. A feature must be available at the prediction time.
introduction.example: Training values 1 and 3 have mean 2 and population standard deviation 1. A future value 5 transforms to 3. Refitting the mean using that future value changes the training procedure using information held out for evaluation.

exercise.question: 用自己的话解释：上面的情景为什么是“Feature Engineering”的例子？请指出定义中的关键条件在情景里如何体现，而不是只复述最后的数值。
exercise.definition: Feature engineering turns raw observations into inputs suitable for a prediction task. It includes defining units, aggregations, missing-value behavior and transformations. A feature must be available at the prediction time.
exercise.evidence: Training values 1 and 3 have mean 2 and population standard deviation 1. A future value 5 transforms to 3. Refitting the mean using that future value changes the training procedure using information held out for evaluation.

blocks.text: A fitted transformation learns state from training data. For standardization, z=(x-μ_train)/σ_train, where μ_train and σ_train are the training mean and scale. Apply those same values to validation and test inputs; define how zero scale is handled.

blocks.text: The prediction is y_hat=β_0+Σ_j β_j x_j. Ordinary least squares chooses coefficients minimizing the sum of squared prediction errors. β_0 is the intercept; β_j measures the contribution per unit of feature x_j in the model. Correlated inputs can make coefficients unstable.

For y_hat=2+3x, input x=4 gives prediction 14. If x is measured in meters, changing it to centimeters requires changing the coefficient accordingly. A fitted relationship predicts association and does not by itself establish causality.

introduction.definition: A decision tree groups samples through successive conditions. A node is a decision location; a split divides data; a leaf is a terminal node. To predict order cancellation, a tree may split by price, then delivery time, and output a cancellation rate at each leaf. Classification trees predict classes or probabilities; regression trees predict continuous values. Training chooses features and thresholds from the objective rather than merely reproducing rules written beforehand.
introduction.example:
Five classification trees vote [1,1,0,1,0] on one email. Positive means spam.
An ensemble requires useful individual predictors and is also affected by error correlation. Real random forest classifiers may average leaf probabilities, unlike this hard-voting example.

exercise.question: Every tree predicts 0 when the truth is 1. Would adding 100 identical trees help?
exercise.answer: No. Duplicating the same error adds no information.
