worked.title: Random Forests: Error Correlation Limits Voting Gains
worked.scenario: Five classification trees vote [1,1,0,1,0] on one email. Positive means spam.
steps: Hard voting gives 3 to 2, producing class 1. Trees using identical data and features may make highly correlated errors.
For each tree, draw a bootstrap sample of training observations with replacement. Randomly selecting candidate features at each split introduces further variation among trees.
If all five trees make the same error on a type of email, adding votes does not automatically correct that systematic bias.
worked.result: An ensemble requires useful individual predictors and is also affected by error correlation. Real random forest classifiers may average leaf probabilities, unlike this hard-voting example.
worked.pitfall: 3/5 is not automatically a calibrated real-world probability. Out-of-bag evaluation does not replace independent testing for every task.
worked.question: Every tree predicts 0 when the truth is 1. Would adding 100 identical trees help?
worked.answer: No. Duplicating the same error adds no information.

depth.boundary: Deep trees can be unstable. Complexity control and ensemble methods address this in different ways.

introduction.definition: 聚类按规定的相似性，把没有预先类别标签的对象分组。分组含义取决于特征、距离和算法。
introduction.example: 把水果按重量和颜色摆成几堆，算法只看到这些特征，不知道“苹果”“梨”这些名字。不同特征和距离可能分出不同的堆。

exercise.question: 算法分出的每一堆，是否必然就是现实中的一种水果？
exercise.answer: 不是。聚类反映所用特征和规则下的相似性，不自动等于真实类别，也不自动给出因果解释。

blocks.text: 聚类在没有类别标签时，依据指定距离或相似性把样本分组。K-means 用中心代表簇；层次聚类反复合并或拆分簇，形成一棵分组树。分组是否有用取决于特征、尺度与任务。
K-means 最小化 $\sum_i\|x_i-\mu_{c_i}\|^2$，cᵢ 为样本簇编号、μ 为中心。层次聚类还需指定簇间距离规则，如单连接、全连接或平均连接。资产 HRP 使用相关距离及聚类树分配资本，是聚类基础之上的应用。
一维数据 (0,1,9,10) 取 K=2，可分成 (0,1) 与 (9,10)，中心为 0.5、9.5，平方误差和为 1。把全部点放在中心 5 的同一簇，误差和为 82。改变距离或特征缩放，可能改变分组。

worked.title: K-Means: Assignment and Mean Updates
worked.scenario: The six 2D points are (0,0), (0,2), (2,0), (7,7), (7,9), (9,7). Set K=2 with initial centers (0,0) and (2,0).
steps: Assign each point to its nearest center by Euclidean distance, breaking ties by the smaller center index. Both initial centers are in the lower-left group, so do not cover both groups.
Replace each center with the mean of its assigned points, then reassign using the new centers. Repeat, checking within-cluster squared error, SSE, at each step.
The final clusters have centers (2/3,2/3) and (23/3,23/3), with SSE=32/3.
worked.result: Lloyd’s alternating steps find the obvious grouping here. Neither assignment nor mean updates increase this objective, but a global optimum is not guaranteed.
worked.pitfall: K is specified in advance. The demo retains the old center for an empty cluster as an explicit teaching convention; libraries may differ. Feature scale affects Euclidean distance.
worked.question: If every second coordinate is multiplied by 100, do distances retain the same meaning?
worked.answer: No. The second coordinate will dominate. Decide whether to standardize and how to handle units based on the task.

depth.boundary: Clusters need not match real-world categories. Distance scales, density assumptions, and cluster shapes affect the grouping.

introduction.definition: Anomaly detection identifies observations unusual under a specified reference model or normal-data baseline. Unusual does not necessarily mean erroneous, malicious or important; that interpretation requires context.
introduction.example: If normal latency has reference mean 100 ms and scale 10 ms, 150 ms has z=5. A threshold of 3 flags it for investigation. A sustained workload change can make the old baseline inappropriate rather than proving each new request is faulty.

exercise.definition: Anomaly detection identifies observations unusual under a specified reference model or normal-data baseline. Unusual does not necessarily mean erroneous, malicious or important; that interpretation requires context.
exercise.evidence: If normal latency has reference mean 100 ms and scale 10 ms, 150 ms has z=5. A threshold of 3 flags it for investigation. A sustained workload change can make the old baseline inappropriate rather than proving each new request is faulty.

blocks.text: A simple score is z=(x-μ)/σ for a scalar baseline with positive scale σ. A rule may flag |z|>k. μ and σ are estimated from reference data, k is a chosen threshold, and a normal-distribution interpretation requires additional assumptions.

depth.boundary: The anomaly score does not automatically equal the calibrated anomaly probability.

introduction.definition: Neural architectures encode different design preferences for different data structures. A CNN, or convolutional neural network, uses local convolution kernels to process grid-structured data such as images. It reuses local patterns and has long been important for image recognition, object detection and many other vision tasks. ResNet uses residual connections to make deep networks easier to train.
introduction.example:
Input is the 3×3 matrix [[1,2,3],[4,5,6],[7,8,9]], kernel [[1,0],[0,1]], stride 1, no padding and bias 0.
Output is [[6,8],[12,14]]. This uses the cross-correlation convention common in deep learning libraries, without flipping the kernel.

exercise.question: What changes with kernel [[1,-1],[1,-1]]?
exercise.answer: All four outputs are -2: each window computes its left-column sum minus its right-column sum.

blocks.text: At this point, you can already explain why "deep learning" is not just one model. CNN utilizes spatial locality; RNN emphasizes sequential states; Transformer emphasizes dynamic information association; GNN utilizes graph structure; different designs reflect the inductive bias of different tasks.

worked.title: Convolution Windows: Which Pixels Produce One Output?
worked.scenario: Input is the 3×3 matrix [[1,2,3],[4,5,6],[7,8,9]], kernel [[1,0],[0,1]], stride 1, no padding and bias 0.
steps: Multiply the upper-left window [[1,2],[4,5]] elementwise by the kernel and sum: 1×1+2×0+4×0+5×1=6.
Move one position right to obtain 2+6=8. The two windows in the next row give 4+8=12 and 5+9=14.
Output spatial size is (3-2)/1+1=2, giving a 2×2 output. The same sliding kernel shares weights across positions.
worked.result: Output is [[6,8],[12,14]]. This uses the cross-correlation convention common in deep learning libraries, without flipping the kernel.
worked.pitfall: Mathematical convolution often flips the kernel; state the convention rather than mixing them. Channels, padding, dilation and multiple kernels are omitted here.
worked.question: What changes with kernel [[1,-1],[1,-1]]?
worked.answer: All four outputs are -2: each window computes its left-column sum minus its right-column sum.

depth.boundary: Local connectivity and weight sharing are inductive biases. They do not guarantee invariance to transformations or better performance on every task.

introduction.definition: Word2Vec learns vectors from word–context co-occurrence. GloVe uses global co-occurrence statistics, while FastText adds subword information to handle word forms and unseen words. Their typical word representations are context independent. Contextual embeddings instead give a word different vectors in different sentences, such as apple as a fruit versus Apple as a company. Nearby vectors reflect a learned relationship, not necessarily exact synonymy.
introduction.example:
Use image vector [1,0] and text vectors [2,0] and [1,1] to illustrate vector comparison only.
Shared representations turn cross-modal retrieval into a nearest-vector problem. These artificial vectors neither train nor validate a real image–text model.

exercise.question: What is the cosine for text vector [-1,0]?
exercise.answer: -1, indicating opposite direction. Semantic interpretation still depends on the learned space.

blocks.text: SimCLR treats different augmented views of the same image as positive pairs and learns a stable visual representation. CLIP brings the matched image and text closer and distinguishes them from other pairs to obtain a cross-modal space. It can use text category descriptions for zero-shot classification or image and text retrieval, but it is not a chat model that is inherently capable of generating long answers. The quality of the training image-text pairs, negative samples, and augmentation design all affect the learned associations.

BYOL, DINO and related self-distillation approaches train one branch to match a teacher branch’s representation, with teacher updates and mechanisms to prevent collapse. They do not always require explicit negative examples. Masked autoencoders hide much of an input and learn to reconstruct it, emphasizing structural completion. Learning useful representations does not by itself produce an instruction-following agent; downstream interfaces still need training.

Vision–language models connect a visual encoder to language capabilities. A projector maps visual features into representations accepted by a language model; cross-attention offers another interaction mechanism. Image resolution, visual-token count and cropping affect recognition of small text and fine details. OCR recognizes text; broader visual understanding also includes positions, relationships and scenes. They are not interchangeable.

ASR converts speech to text using approaches such as CTC, encoder–decoder models or transducers. Transducers commonly support streaming recognition with different input and output lengths. TTS converts text to speech; a vocoder converts acoustic representations to waveforms. A mel spectrogram is a common time–frequency representation; codec tokens encode audio as discrete units. Word error rate, or WER, measures transcription errors, not tone, timbre or speech naturalness.

sections.title: Video Token, Temporal Consistency, Optical Flow [Overview]

blocks.text: Video requires modeling change over time, not merely processing more images. Temporal consistency concerns whether objects maintain their identity, appearance and plausible motion. Optical flow estimates local visual motion and supports tracking and video analysis, though camera movement and occlusion complicate interpretation. Coherent-looking generated video can still violate contact mechanics, gravity or action–outcome relationships. Distinguish visual quality from physical prediction.

Point clouds represent scenes with 3D points and additional attributes. NeRF learns a spatially and view-dependent radiance field to render novel views. 3D Gaussian splatting represents and renders scenes efficiently with optimizable spatial Gaussian primitives. These solve 3D representation and view synthesis, rather than necessarily learning how forces move objects. Static reconstruction, interactive world modeling and robot control are distinct levels.

worked.title: Cross-Modal Representation: Cosine Similarity Is Not Fact-Checking
worked.scenario: Use image vector [1,0] and text vectors [2,0] and [1,1] to illustrate vector comparison only.
steps: The image’s cosine similarity with the first text is 2/(1×2)=1; with the second it is 1/√2≈0.707.
After normalization, the first text vector is [1,0] and the second is approximately [.707,.707]. Their dot products with the image vector equal cosine similarities.
Scaling the first text vector to [20,0] still gives cosine 1, showing invariance to positive rescaling of vector magnitude.
worked.result: Shared representations turn cross-modal retrieval into a nearest-vector problem. These artificial vectors neither train nor validate a real image–text model.
worked.pitfall: Similarity is not correctness or probability. Cosine for a zero vector is undefined. Models can still misread negation, quantities and detailed spatial relationships.
worked.question: What is the cosine for text vector [-1,0]?
worked.answer: -1, indicating opposite direction. Semantic interpretation still depends on the learned space.

depth.boundary: Embedding similarity, cross-modal understanding, and reliable action are distinct evaluation goals.

blocks.text: 固定策略 π 下，$V^\pi(s)=E_\pi[r_{t+1}+\gamma V^\pi(s_{t+1})\mid s_t=s]$。最优动作价值为 $Q^*(s,a)=E[r_{t+1}+\gamma\max_{a'}Q^*(s_{t+1},a')\mid s_t=s,a_t=a]$。γ 为折扣，s、a 为状态和行动；真正终止后未来价值为零，时间截断不必等于终止。
一个行动立即得到奖励 2，随后确定进入价值 5 的非终止状态，γ=0.9，则该次 Bellman 目标为 2+0.9×5=6.5。若这一步已经真正终止，目标只有 2。交易奖励如何纳入费用和库存风险，见金融应用。

worked.title: Q-Learning: No Bootstrapping at True Termination
worked.scenario: Current Q(s,a)=2, reward r=1, maximum next-state Q=4, discount γ=0.9 and learning rate α=0.5.
steps: For a nonterminal transition, the target is r+γ max Q=1+0.9×4=4.6.
The TD error is 4.6-2=2.6. Update Q=2+0.5×2.6=3.3.
At a true terminal state, the target is only r=1, giving 2+0.5×(1-2)=1.5.
worked.result: The same observed reward produces different learning targets depending on termination. One tabular Q-learning update does not establish a fully learned policy.
worked.pitfall: Distinguish true termination from time-limit truncation. Bootstrapping depends on the task and interface semantics. Q-learning uses the maximum next-state value; SARSA uses the actual next action’s value.
worked.question: With α=1, what is the updated value for the nonterminal transition?
worked.answer: It becomes the current target, 4.6. This does not mean the target estimate is noise-free.

depth.boundary: Value depends on the policy, discount, and task; single-step rewards alone are insufficient for comparison.

introduction.definition: A policy-gradient method adjusts parameters of an action policy to improve expected return. A stochastic policy π_θ(a|s) gives the probability of taking action a in state s.
introduction.example: If an action has higher estimated advantage than the baseline, a small ascent update tends to increase its sampled log probability. One fortunate reward is not enough to identify a reliable advantage; exploration and estimation affect the update.

blocks.text: A score-function gradient has the form E[∇_θ log π_θ(a|s) A(s,a)], under the sampling and return convention of the algorithm. A is an advantage estimate comparing the action with a baseline; an inaccurate estimate can increase variance or bias.

depth.boundary: Constraints in a policy objective differ from gradient clipping.

introduction.definition: Imitation learning trains a policy using expert demonstrations. Behavior cloning is its supervised form: predict the demonstrated action from the recorded observation. Other imitation methods can query an expert or match broader behavior.
introduction.example: A driving policy trained only on centered-lane images may drift slightly at deployment and encounter images absent from training. Collecting expert corrections on learner-visited states targets this coverage gap; simply lowering training loss on the original images may not.

blocks.text: For demonstrations (s_i,a_i), behavior cloning minimizes an action loss Σ_i L(π_θ(s_i),a_i). The dataset covers expert-visited states, which may differ from states reached after the learner makes mistakes; this is distribution shift.

depth.boundary: Behavior cloning may fit demonstrations without keeping its own rollout states within the demonstration distribution.

concepts.title: Motion Planning · 图搜索在机器人路径中的应用

introduction.definition: 运动规划是在机器人构型空间中寻找从起点到目标的无碰撞路径。构型可以是一组关节角；离散化后，可把可行构型作为节点、允许的局部运动作为边，再使用图搜索。图上有路径并不自动代表真实机器人能按任意速度执行。
introduction.example: 机械臂的起止关节角都安全，中间直线插值仍可能扫过桌边。规划器可以经一个绕行构型连接起终点，但要检查整条边上的碰撞，而不只是节点。之后再给路径分配执行时间；这一步与预测模型、实时反馈控制有不同职责。

exercise.evidence: 机械臂的起止关节角都安全，中间直线插值仍可能扫过桌边。规划器可以经一个绕行构型连接起终点，但要检查整条边上的碰撞，而不只是节点。之后再给路径分配执行时间；这一步与预测模型、实时反馈控制有不同职责。

blocks.text: 设构型为 q，路径为 q(s)，s∈[0,1]，要求路径位于无碰撞集合。离散路径成本可写 \(C=\sum_{(u,v)\in\text{path}}c(u,v)\)。只有声明边权非负等适用条件后，才能选择相应最短路算法。路径加上时间参数后，还需检查速度、加速度与执行器限制。

depth.boundary: Geometric paths, dynamic constraints, state estimation, and feedback control address different parts of robot motion.

introduction.definition: Disjoint-set union (DSU) maintains disjoint sets. find returns a set representative, and union merges two sets. Two nodes are connected exactly when their representatives match. Representatives may change after unions, so do not treat a root’s label as a permanent application ID.
introduction.example:
Six nodes 0…5 receive undirected connections (0,1), (2,3), (1,2), (0,3), (4,5), in that order.
The final partition is {0,1,2,3} and {4,5}. Representatives depend on the union strategy, but membership does not.

exercise.question: Remove (1,2) but still add (0,3). How many final sets remain?
exercise.answer: Still 2. Connection (0,3) merges the previously separate {0,1} and {2,3}.

blocks.text: Ordinary disjoint-set union is good at online queries that only add connections, and cannot directly reverse a union to process arbitrary deletions. Offline dynamic connectivity, rollback structures, etc. require additional design; when rolling back, it is usually avoided to directly use path compression that is difficult to recover.

worked.title: Union-Find: Repeated Connections Do Not Reduce Set Count
worked.scenario: Six nodes 0…5 receive undirected connections (0,1), (2,3), (1,2), (0,3), (4,5), in that order.
steps: Start with 6 sets. The first two connections each merge a pair, leaving 4 sets.
After merging (1,2), nodes 0,1,2,3 share one set. The count becomes 3.
For (0,3), both roots already match, so no merge occurs. Finally (4,5) reduces the count to 2.
worked.result: The final partition is {0,1,2,3} and {4,5}. Representatives depend on the union strategy, but membership does not.
worked.pitfall: Do not subtract one for every edge. Repeated edges or edges closing a cycle may cause no new union.
worked.question: Remove (1,2) but still add (0,3). How many final sets remain?
worked.answer: Still 2. Connection (0,3) merges the previously separate {0,1} and {2,3}.

depth.boundary: Ordinary DSU mainly handles added connections. Path compression changes tree shape without changing set membership.

introduction.definition: 0–1 BFS finds shortest paths when every edge weight is either zero or one. It uses a deque to process zero-cost relaxations before cost-one relaxations.
introduction.example: If A→B costs 1, A→C costs 0 and C→B costs 0, the shortest distance to B is 0 through C. Plain unweighted BFS would prefer the one-edge path, while the deque respects actual zero-one cost.

exercise.question: 用自己的话解释：上面的情景为什么是“0-1 BFS”的例子？请指出定义中的关键条件在情景里如何体现，而不是只复述最后的数值。
exercise.definition: 0–1 BFS finds shortest paths when every edge weight is either zero or one. It uses a deque to process zero-cost relaxations before cost-one relaxations.
exercise.evidence: If A→B costs 1, A→C costs 0 and C→B costs 0, the shortest distance to B is 0 through C. Plain unweighted BFS would prefer the one-edge path, while the deque respects actual zero-one cost.

blocks.text: When improving dist[v] through an edge from u, push v to the front for weight 0 and to the back for weight 1. With a proper adjacency-list implementation, complexity is O(V+E). Other weights require a different algorithm or transformation.

depth.boundary: Relax whenever distance improves; first enqueueing does not make a distance final.

introduction.definition: Bellman–Ford computes single-source shortest-path distances with possibly negative edge weights and can detect a reachable negative cycle. A reachable negative cycle can make some minimum path costs unbounded below.
introduction.example: For A→B cost 4, A→C cost 5 and B→C cost -2, the best cost to C is 2 via B. Negative weights invalidate Dijkstra’s usual nonnegative-weight assumption, but are allowed by Bellman–Ford.

exercise.question: 用自己的话解释：上面的情景为什么是“Bellman-Ford”的例子？请指出定义中的关键条件在情景里如何体现，而不是只复述最后的数值。
exercise.definition: Bellman–Ford computes single-source shortest-path distances with possibly negative edge weights and can detect a reachable negative cycle. A reachable negative cycle can make some minimum path costs unbounded below.
exercise.evidence: For A→B cost 4, A→C cost 5 and B→C cost -2, the best cost to C is 2 via B. Negative weights invalidate Dijkstra’s usual nonnegative-weight assumption, but are allowed by Bellman–Ford.

blocks.text: Relax an edge u→v of weight w using dist[v]=min(dist[v],dist[u]+w). After at most V-1 full passes, shortest simple paths are covered. An additional reachable improvement signals a reachable negative cycle. The usual complexity is O(VE).

depth.boundary: A negative cycle unreachable from the source does not invalidate all that source’s results.

introduction.definition: In a one-based Fenwick tree, tree[i] stores the sum of an interval of length lowbit(i). In the appropriate integer representation, lowbit(i)=i & (-i) extracts the least significant set bit.
introduction.example:
Use the one-based array a=[2,1,3,4,2]. The tree stores interval sums, initially tree[1…5]=[2,3,3,10,2].
A Fenwick update touches only binary interval blocks containing the position. Each query or update path takes at most O(log n) steps.

exercise.question: If the increment at position 3 were -2 instead, what would the sum of the first five elements be?
exercise.answer: 10: original total 12 minus 2. The structure supports negative increments too.

blocks.text: In a one-based Fenwick tree, tree[i] stores the sum of an interval of length lowbit(i). In the appropriate integer representation, lowbit(i)=i & (-i) extracts the least significant set bit.

worked.title: Fenwick Trees: Queries and Updates Move Differently
worked.scenario: Use the one-based array a=[2,1,3,4,2]. The tree stores interval sums, initially tree[1…5]=[2,3,3,10,2].
steps: For the first 5 elements, read tree[5]=2, subtract lowbit(5)=1 to reach index 4, then read tree[4]=10. The total is 12.
Add 2 at position 3: tree[3] changes from 3 to 5, then tree[4] from 10 to 12. The next index 8 exceeds n, so stop.
The new total is 14. The sum over positions 2…4 is prefix(4)-prefix(1)=12-2=10.
worked.result: A Fenwick update touches only binary interval blocks containing the position. Each query or update path takes at most O(log n) steps.
worked.pitfall: Index 0 is unsuitable as a starting point for this one-based update interface because lowbit(0)=0.
worked.question: If the increment at position 3 were -2 instead, what would the sum of the first five elements be?
worked.answer: 10: original total 12 minus 2. The structure supports negative increments too.

depth.boundary: The one-based update interface excludes index 0; obtain range sums by subtracting prefixes.

introduction.definition: The segment tree recursively splits the interval in half, with the parent node holding a mergeable summary of both sides, such as sum, min, max, or count. The query interval is divided into a small number of completely covered nodes, and then the answers are merged; point modification only recalculates a path from the root to the leaf.
introduction.example:
For [2,1,3,4,2,6], query the maximum in the zero-based half-open interval [1,5).
The query determines what each node stores. Sums, maxima and more complex summaries have different merge rules.

exercise.question: If every value is negative, is 0 a valid initial merge value?
exercise.answer: No. It may exceed every real value. Use a suitable identity or handle empty results explicitly.

The query interval is divided into a small number of completely covered nodes, and then the answers are merged; point modification only recalculates a path from the root to the leaf.

worked.title: Segment Trees: Range Maxima Cannot Be Subtracted
worked.scenario: For [2,1,3,4,2,6], query the maximum in the zero-based half-open interval [1,5).
steps: The selected values are [1,3,4,2], with maximum 4. Index 5 containing 6 is excluded.
Decompose the range into segment-tree nodes and merge their summaries with max. Negative infinity can serve as the merge identity.
Changing index 2 from 3 to 9 updates only the relevant leaf and ancestors. Querying [1,5) now returns 9.
worked.result: The query determines what each node stores. Sums, maxima and more complex summaries have different merge rules.
worked.pitfall: prefixMax(5)-prefixMax(1) does not give the range maximum. Define the result for an empty interval explicitly.
worked.question: If every value is negative, is 0 a valid initial merge value?
worked.answer: No. It may exceed every real value. Use a suitable identity or handle empty results explicitly.

depth.boundary: Lazy-tag composition order and summary updates must match the operation.

introduction.definition: A difference array may use zero-based or one-based indices, but reserve the position after the right endpoint. To add x over a closed range [l,r], add x to d[l] and subtract x from d[r+1]. Prefix accumulation then reconstructs the updated array.
introduction.example:
Start with a zero-based, length-5 array of zeros. Add 2 to inclusive [1,3], then add -1 to [2,4], reconstructing the array afterward.
The final array is [0,2,1,1,-1]. Each range update changes two endpoints; final reconstruction takes O(n).

exercise.question: For a half-open range [l,r), where is the cancellation?
exercise.answer: At d[r], because r is already outside the updated range.

blocks.text: Step 1: Allocate a length-6 difference array. The first update adds 2 to d[1] and subtracts 2 from d[4].

worked.title: Difference Arrays: Undo the Increment After the Range
worked.scenario: Start with a zero-based, length-5 array of zeros. Add 2 to inclusive [1,3], then add -1 to [2,4], reconstructing the array afterward.
steps: Allocate a length-6 difference array. The first update adds 2 to d[1] and subtracts 2 from d[4].
The second subtracts 1 from d[2] and adds 1 to d[5]. Position d[5] is a sentinel canceling the update after the array ends.
Prefix-sum the first five differences to obtain values 0,2,1,1,-1 at positions 0…4.
worked.result: The final array is [0,2,1,1,-1]. Each range update changes two endpoints; final reconstruction takes O(n).
worked.pitfall: For an inclusive range, cancel at r+1 rather than r. Allocate the sentinel but do not return it as a sixth array value.
worked.question: For a half-open range [l,r), where is the cancellation?
worked.answer: At d[r], because r is already outside the updated range.

depth.boundary: Basic difference arrays suit offline reconstruction; online queries usually require another structure.

introduction.definition: KMP searches for one pattern using a prefix function that records how much already matched text can be reused after a mismatch. A proper prefix excludes the whole string.
introduction.example: For pattern abab, the prefix-function array is [0,0,1,2]. In text ababab, matches overlap: after a full match, the suffix ab can serve as the matched prefix for the next candidate, without rescanning those letters.

exercise.question: 用自己的话解释：上面的情景为什么是“KMP Prefix Function”的例子？请指出定义中的关键条件在情景里如何体现，而不是只复述最后的数值。
exercise.definition: KMP searches for one pattern using a prefix function that records how much already matched text can be reused after a mismatch. A proper prefix excludes the whole string.
exercise.evidence: For pattern abab, the prefix-function array is [0,0,1,2]. In text ababab, matches overlap: after a full match, the suffix ab can serve as the matched prefix for the next candidate, without rescanning those letters.

blocks.text: For pattern position i, π[i] is the length of the longest proper prefix equal to a suffix of the prefix ending at i. After mismatch, fall back through π rather than restarting the text scan. Standard matching takes O(n+m) for text length n and pattern length m.

depth.boundary: Prefix-function values are lengths. Specify overlap handling after matches and the empty-pattern convention.

introduction.definition: Aho–Corasick searches many patterns together using a trie, failure links and output information. Trie prefixes share work; failure links represent a useful suffix when the next transition is missing.
introduction.example: For patterns he, she and hers, the trie shares the prefix he between he and hers. Reading she can report both she and its suffix he through output/failure information. This differs from KMP’s single-pattern prefix table.

exercise.question: 用自己的话解释：上面的情景为什么是“Aho-Corasick”的例子？请指出定义中的关键条件在情景里如何体现，而不是只复述最后的数值。

exercise.evidence: For patterns he, she and hers, the trie shares the prefix he between he and hers. Reading she can report both she and its suffix he through output/failure information. This differs from KMP’s single-pattern prefix table.

blocks.text: Build the trie for total pattern length M and failure links in breadth-first order. Scan text through transitions and failure links, reporting outputs at reached states. With an appropriate transition representation, scan cost is O(n+z), where z is the number of reported matches.

depth.boundary: State the transition implementation and include the actual number of reported matches in complexity.

introduction.definition: The tails method finds the length of a longest strictly increasing subsequence. tails[k] is the smallest achievable ending value of an increasing subsequence of length k+1 among processed inputs.
introduction.example: Processing [3,1,2] changes tails from [3] to [1] to [1,2], so the length is 2. The strict version uses the first value ≥x; choosing the first value >x instead addresses a nondecreasing variant.

exercise.question: 用自己的话解释：上面的情景为什么是“LIS Tails”的例子？请指出定义中的关键条件在情景里如何体现，而不是只复述最后的数值。
exercise.definition: The tails method finds the length of a longest strictly increasing subsequence. tails[k] is the smallest achievable ending value of an increasing subsequence of length k+1 among processed inputs.
exercise.evidence: Processing [3,1,2] changes tails from [3] to [1] to [1,2], so the length is 2. The strict version uses the first value ≥x; choosing the first value >x instead addresses a nondecreasing variant.

blocks.text: For each x, replace the first tails value greater than or equal to x, or append if none exists. Binary search gives O(n log n). tails is a summary of best endpoints, not necessarily one actual subsequence; reconstruction needs predecessor information.

depth.boundary: tails need not itself be a subsequence of the input. Reconstruction requires additional predecessor information.

introduction.definition: Weighted interval scheduling selects nonoverlapping intervals to maximize total weight. Sorting by finish time makes the final selected interval support a useful recurrence.
introduction.example: Suppose A=[0,2] has weight 4, B=[2,4] weight 5 and C=[0,4] weight 8, allowing touching endpoints. A+B earns 9 and beats C. Choosing the highest individual weight first would miss this result.

exercise.question: 用自己的话解释：上面的情景为什么是“Weighted Interval Scheduling”的例子？请指出定义中的关键条件在情景里如何体现，而不是只复述最后的数值。

blocks.text: Let p(i) be the last earlier interval compatible with interval i, and w_i its weight. Then DP[i]=max(DP[i-1],w_i+DP[p(i)]), with DP[0]=0. Define endpoint compatibility explicitly; binary search can compute predecessor indices.

depth.boundary: Maximizing task count differs from maximizing reward; earliest-finish greedy does not apply unconditionally.

introduction.definition: Interval dynamic programming stores an answer for a contiguous range and builds larger ranges from smaller ones. The state must specify exactly which endpoints belong to the interval.
introduction.example: For matrices 10×30, 30×5 and 5×60, multiplying the first two first costs 1,500+3,000=4,500. Multiplying the last two first costs 9,000+18,000=27,000. The interval state compares both parenthesizations.

blocks.text: In matrix-chain multiplication, DP[l,r] is the minimum scalar multiplication count for matrices l through r. Its recurrence is \(DP[l,r]=\min_{l\le k<r}(DP[l,k]+DP[k+1,r]+d_{l-1}d_kd_r)\). Matrix i has dimensions \(d_{i-1}\times d_i\); a single matrix needs zero multiplications.

depth.boundary: The task determines the merge cost; one interval template does not fit every problem.

Four nodes 0…3 have directed distance matrix [[0,2,9,10],[1,0,6,4],[15,7,0,8],[6,3,12,0]]. Start at 0, visit every other node once, then return to 0.

worked.title: Bitmask DP: Remember the Last Node Too
worked.scenario: Four nodes 0…3 have directed distance matrix [[0,2,9,10],[1,0,6,4],[15,7,0,8],[6,3,12,0]]. Start at 0, visit every other node once, then return to 0.
steps: A state needs both the visited set and the last node: the next edge’s cost depends on the endpoint, even for the same visited set.
For example, 0→2→3 costs 9+8=17. Continuing to 1 and then 0 adds 3+1.
The full tour 0→2→3→1→0 costs 21. Checking the other five visitation orders confirms none is cheaper.
worked.result: The optimal tour costs 21. Bitmask DP shares subproblems in O(n²2ⁿ) time; it does not make the problem polynomial in size.
worked.pitfall: Omitting the return edge solves a different path problem. With asymmetric distances, reversing a tour need not give an equivalent route.
worked.question: Is one minimum value per visited set sufficient, without its endpoint?
worked.answer: No. Different endpoints have different continuation costs. A locally cheaper state may not yield the globally optimal tour.

depth.boundary: Bitmasks do not remove the exponential state count, and language integer widths are limited.

introduction.definition: An exchange argument shows that some optimal solution can be transformed into an equally good one beginning with the greedy choice. To maximize the number of compatible unweighted intervals, choose an interval with the earliest finish. Replacing an optimal solution’s first interval with this one leaves at least as much room for later intervals.
introduction.example: suppose you can test whether any solution satisfies it, and feasibility changes monotonically with B. Then search for the boundary between infeasible and feasible candidates.

sections.title: Exchange Arguments: Show How to Replace an Optimal Solution’s First Choice

blocks.text: Once tasks have different benefits, machines have multiple resource constraints, or preemption methods are allowed to change, the original proof may no longer hold. Giving counterexamples during the interview can better demonstrate your understanding of the goals and constraints than just memorizing a "common greedy rule".

sections.title: Binary Search on the Answer: Feasibility Is Monotonic

blocks.text: Binary search applies beyond sorted arrays. Given a candidate bound B, suppose you can test whether any solution satisfies it, and feasibility changes monotonically with B. Then search for the boundary between infeasible and feasible candidates.

For example, split nonnegative tasks into at most k groups in their original order to minimize the maximum group sum. The lower bound is the largest individual value and the upper bound is the total sum. A larger B relaxes the constraint. Maintain explicit search boundaries rather than returning the first feasible candidate encountered.

sections.title: Feasibility check: Applicable prerequisites for grouped greedy

blocks.text: Given the upper limit, try to put the next item into the current group from left to right, and only open a new group if it cannot be placed. Non-negative numbers make "adding later does not reduce the current group sum" true, so this check can calculate the minimum number of groups required.

If negative numbers are allowed, the current overrun may be offset by subsequent negative terms, and the argument for early group cutting becomes invalid. If exactly k non-empty groups are required, non-negative and k does not exceed n, the larger group can be continued to be split without increasing the maximum sum; other constraints need to be re-argued.

sections.title: Numerical Search and Expression of Complexity

blocks.text: For an integer search interval of width U, O(n) work per feasibility check gives O(n log(U+1)) time and potentially O(1) auxiliary space. Here the logarithmic parameter is the answer range, not the number of input elements.

Floating-point answers require error or iteration number conventions; midpoint calculations must consider overflow, and termination conditions must be consistent with interval conventions. Don't write a fixed-precision decimal search directly as left=mid+1, and don't ignore the integer precision determined by the input range.

worked.title: Binary Search on the Answer: Test a Candidate Limit
worked.scenario: Keep nonnegative tasks [7,2,5,10,8] in order. Split them into at most 2 nonempty contiguous groups, minimizing the largest group sum.
steps: The answer is at least the largest item, 10, and at most the total, 32.
Limit 17 permits [7,2,5] with sum 14, then [10], but the final 8 requires a third group. It is infeasible.
Limit 18 permits [7,2,5] and [10,8]. Binary search finds the smallest feasible limit, 18.
worked.result: The optimal largest group sum is 18, splitting between 5 and 10. Each check costs O(n); integer search takes about O(n log U).
worked.pitfall: The greedy check requires nonnegative values. With negatives, a later item can reduce a temporarily excessive sum, so the same check is invalid.
worked.question: What is the answer if at most one group is allowed?
worked.answer: 32. All tasks must remain together.

depth.boundary: Prove any greedy feasibility test independently; constraints such as negative values can change the argument.

introduction.definition: 蓄水池抽样在不知道最终数据流长度时，用固定容量保留一个均匀随机子样本。它解决抽样问题；Bloom filter 解决近似成员查询，定义不再从后者页面重复搬来。
introduction.example: 容量 k=1，先保存 A；B 到来时以 1/2 概率替换，C 到来时以 1/3 概率替换。最终 A 的保留概率为 (1/2)×(2/3)=1/3，B 也为 1/3，C 为 1/3。不能总用 1/2 替换，否则近期记录被过度保留。

exercise.question: 用自己的话解释：上面的情景为什么是“Reservoir Sampling”的例子？请指出定义中的关键条件在情景里如何体现，而不是只复述最后的数值。

blocks.text: 容量为 k，先保存前 k 个观测。第 t>k 个观测到来时，从 1 到 t 等概率抽整数 j；若 j≤k，就替换池中第 j 个，否则保持。处理到 t 时，每个原观测被保留的概率都是 k/t，空间为 O(k)。

worked.title: Reservoir Sampling: Every Position Ends with Probability One Third
worked.scenario: A,B,C arrive in a stream. Keep one sample, applying a position-dependent replacement probability.
steps: Keep A initially. B replaces it with probability 1/2.
C replaces the current sample with probability 1/3. A’s final retention probability is 1×1/2×2/3=1/3.
B’s final probability is 1/2×2/3=1/3. C’s final probability is 1/3.
worked.result: All three positions are equally likely to remain, without knowing the stream’s final length in advance.
worked.pitfall: Replacing with probability 1/2 every time favors later elements. Incorrect endpoints in uniform integer sampling also change probabilities.
worked.question: For records A,A,B, what is the probability that the retained value is A?
worked.answer: 2/3. Sampling is uniform over record positions. The two A records are distinct positions; values are not deduplicated first.

depth.boundary: Correct probabilities depend on uniform-index bounds and the definition of a sampling unit.

introduction.definition: Bloom filter records bits with multiple hash positions. If the query finds that any bit is 0, it can be determined that it has not been inserted; if all are 1, it can only be said that it may exist, because different elements may set these bits together.

worked.title: Bloom Filters: Two Inserted Items Combine into a False Positive
worked.scenario: Start with 8 zero bits and two hash positions per item. A maps to [1,4], B to [4,6], and uninserted C to [1,6].
steps: Insert A by setting bits 1 and 4. Insert B by setting bits 4 and 6.
Both C positions are now 1, returning “possibly present,” although C was never inserted. This is a false positive.
Clearing shared bit 4 to delete A would make B encounter 0 and incorrectly appear absent.
worked.result: Shared bits provide compact storage, but cause false positives and prevent ordinary deletion. An exact record lookup can confirm membership.
worked.pitfall: This fixed, tiny bitmap illustrates the mechanism. It cannot establish a production system’s false-positive rate.
worked.question: If D maps to [0,6], what can be concluded?
worked.answer: Bit 0 remains 0. Under standard insertion-only operation with consistent hashes, D was definitely not inserted.

depth.boundary: Standard insert-only use has no false negatives. Directly clearing shared bits is not safe deletion.

introduction.definition: Worst-case analysis focuses on the most expensive case among allowed inputs; expectation analysis must explain whether the randomness comes from the algorithm or the input model; amortized analysis allocates the total cost of a series of operations to each operation and does not require random inputs.
introduction.example:
Initial capacity is 1 and doubles when full. Append 8 elements, ignoring allocator overhead.
With geometric capacity growth, a geometric series bounds n appends by O(n) total work, giving O(1) amortized cost per append.

exercise.question: Can old storage be ignored immediately during growth?
exercise.answer: No. Old and new arrays can coexist during copying. Analyze peak memory and reclamation separately.

blocks.text: Worst-case analysis focuses on the most expensive case among allowed inputs; expectation analysis must explain whether the randomness comes from the algorithm or the input model; amortized analysis allocates the total cost of a series of operations to each operation and does not require random inputs.

worked.title: Dynamic Arrays: Amortizing Expensive Growth
worked.scenario: Initial capacity is 1 and doubles when full. Append 8 elements, ignoring allocator overhead.
steps: Growing to capacities 2,4,8 copies 1,2,4 existing elements respectively: 7 copies in total.
Eight writes plus seven copies give 15 units of work. One append can be expensive, but total work is still proportional to 8.
A ninth append grows capacity to 16 and copies 8 elements. Total copies become 15 and total work 24, still below 3×9.
worked.result: With geometric capacity growth, a geometric series bounds n appends by O(n) total work, giving O(1) amortized cost per append.
worked.pitfall: Amortized O(1) does not mean worst-case O(1) for every append. Growing by one slot each time instead copies 1+2+…+(n-1) elements.
worked.question: Can old storage be ignored immediately during growth?
worked.answer: No. Old and new arrays can coexist during copying. Analyze peak memory and reclamation separately.

depth.boundary: Amortized analysis is not expected analysis over random inputs and does not make every operation cheap.

introduction.definition: Represent a value as m/10^s. To increase the scale, multiply m by a power of ten. To reduce it without rounding, require the discarded digits to be zero. Decimal-string operations can implement this conversion without a binary floating-point intermediate.
introduction.example: 例子：12.30 可表示为整数 1230 与 scale=2。与 0.45 相加，先统一精度得到 1275/100=12.75；若改为 scale=1，1230/100 只能在相应整除条件下精确改写。金额取整必须明确规则，不能靠显示两位小数代替。

exercise.question: 用自己的话解释：上面的情景为什么是“Exact Decimal Arithmetic / Minor Units”的例子？请指出定义中的关键条件在情景里如何体现，而不是只复述最后的数值。

blocks.text: Keep the representation scale separate from the allowed amount quantum. Stripe represents ISK with two decimal places but permits only whole-ISK charges; HUF and TWD manual payouts similarly require minor-unit integers divisible by 100.

depth.boundary: Representation scale and allowed increments can differ by operation. Input grammar, precision, and divisibility need separate checks. Integer storage must be wide enough; arbitrary-precision arithmetic does not have constant cost for unbounded digit counts.

introduction.definition: Dropbox content_hash first hashes each 4,194,304-byte block with SHA-256, then hashes the concatenation of the raw 32-byte block digests. Only the final digest is encoded as hexadecimal. Transport chunk boundaries do not change the fixed block boundaries.
introduction.example: 例子：文件分成两个块，各自 SHA-256 得到 32 字节摘要 A、B。组合散列应对 64 个原始摘要字节求哈希；把 A、B 各转成 64 字符十六进制后再拼接，会变成另一组输入，不能得到同一个分块内容散列。

exercise.question: 用自己的话解释：上面的情景为什么是“Cryptographic Hashes / Streaming Digests”的例子？请指出定义中的关键条件在情景里如何体现，而不是只复述最后的数值。
exercise.definition: Dropbox content_hash first hashes each 4,194,304-byte block with SHA-256, then hashes the concatenation of the raw 32-byte block digests. Only the final digest is encoded as hexadecimal. Transport chunk boundaries do not change the fixed block boundaries.
exercise.evidence: 例子：文件分成两个块，各自 SHA-256 得到 32 字节摘要 A、B。组合散列应对 64 个原始摘要字节求哈希；把 A、B 各转成 64 字符十六进制后再拼接，会变成另一组输入，不能得到同一个分块内容散列。

blocks.text: Keep one inner hash context, one outer context, and a block-byte counter. Finalize every full block and any remaining nonempty block. An empty file contributes no inner block; an exact block multiple must not append an empty block.

depth.boundary: Dropbox content_hash differs from SHA-256 applied directly to the file. Hash-table indexing, content identification, and authentication have different requirements. Digest equality is subject to collision assumptions and does not by itself authenticate a sender.

introduction.definition: The decomposed string e followed by a combining acute accent contains two Unicode scalars but one grapheme cluster and three UTF-8 bytes. A multi-scalar emoji can also form one Character.
introduction.example: 例子：“é”可由一个码点表示，也可由 e 加组合重音组成；后者有两个 Unicode 标量，但用户通常把它视为一个字形簇。按 UTF-8 字节截断还可能破坏编码；限制“10 个可见字符”需先明确计数单位。

exercise.question: 用自己的话解释：上面的情景为什么是“Unicode Grapheme Clusters / UTF-8”的例子？请指出定义中的关键条件在情景里如何体现，而不是只复述最后的数值。
exercise.definition: The decomposed string e followed by a combining acute accent contains two Unicode scalars but one grapheme cluster and three UTF-8 bytes. A multi-scalar emoji can also form one Character.
exercise.evidence: 例子：“é”可由一个码点表示，也可由 e 加组合重音组成；后者有两个 Unicode 标量，但用户通常把它视为一个字形簇。按 UTF-8 字节截断还可能破坏编码；限制“10 个可见字符”需先明确计数单位。

blocks.text: For a byte-limited prefix that preserves characters, visit whole grapheme clusters in order and accumulate each cluster's UTF-8 length. Stop before the next cluster would exceed the budget. Segmentation should use a Unicode-aware library rather than byte slicing.

depth.boundary: Counting characters does not give a byte length. Canonically equivalent text can have different byte sequences. The segmentation version and normalization policy are part of an interoperable text-processing contract.

introduction.definition: With finite demand, each delivered element consumes one credit. Explicit requests and the additional demand returned by receive add credits; returning none adds zero and does not cancel existing demand.
introduction.example: 例子：订阅者先请求 3 个元素，生产者依次交付后，需求余额为 2、1、0。在余额为零时继续交付，违反这份需求契约；缓冲、暂停上游或拒绝请求属于另行明确的处理策略。

exercise.question: 用自己的话解释：上面的情景为什么是“Backpressure / Subscriber Demand”的例子？请指出定义中的关键条件在情景里如何体现，而不是只复述最后的数值。

blocks.text: A PassthroughSubject does not buffer values for later demand. With one subscriber and zero demand, a sent value is dropped for that subscriber. Other publishers and buffering operators can have different policies.

depth.boundary: Demand limits deliveries rather than elapsed-time request rate. Unlimited demand, cancellation, reentrant sends, multiple subscribers, and completion require their own protocol rules.

applications.title: Adaptive Concurrency · 服务并发上限的反馈控制
applications.reason: 复用背压的供需关系，单独解释服务如何根据延迟反馈调整在途请求上限。

applications.title: Backpressure · 行情与交易消息的拥塞控制
applications.reason: 将一般背压用于行情新鲜度、交易回报完整性和拥塞时的风险降级。

introduction.definition: 最大最小公平分配优先改善最小且尚未满足的分配额。需求已满足的对象退出继续均分，让其余对象分享剩余资源。
introduction.example: 有 10 份资源，三人的需求分别为 2、6、8。先每人分到 2 份，用掉 6 份；第一人已满足，余下 4 份由另外两人平分，结果为 2、4、4。

exercise.question: 为什么不让第一人也继续参与剩余资源的均分？
exercise.answer: 他的需求上限是 2，继续分配超过了需求。需求封顶后退出，剩余资源应给尚未满足的对象。

blocks.text: For capacity C >= 0 and demands d_i >= 0, allocate x_i = min(d_i, lambda), choosing a common water level so the total is min(C, sum d_i). A demand-capped consumer leaves the sharing set when its cap is reached.

Sort demands, satisfy the smallest cap when it is no greater than the remaining equal share, then divide the remaining capacity equally among active consumers. Sorting costs O(n log(n + 1)) time; the subsequent scan is linear.

depth.boundary: This formula assumes equal weights and one divisible resource, without reservations, placement constraints, or indivisible jobs. Peloton's hierarchical, weighted, multi-resource scheduler has additional policies.

distinctions.title: Risk Parity · 风险平价
distinctions.reason: 最大最小公平分配保护较小的未满足分配；风险平价约束组合风险贡献。目标、单位与约束不同。

concepts.title: Adaptive Concurrency · 服务并发上限的反馈控制

introduction.definition: 自适应并发限制器根据已经观察到的服务延迟、利用率或丢弃等反馈，调整同时在途的请求数。它把背压落到请求入口，目的是控制排队；并发上限是请求数，不能当作每秒请求速率。
introduction.example: 若 R₀ 失真，估计也会失真；处理时间较长与排队较多需要额外观测来区分。

exercise.question: 用自己的话解释：上面的情景为什么是“Adaptive Concurrency · 服务并发上限的反馈控制”的例子？请指出定义中的关键条件在情景里如何体现，而不是只复述最后的数值。
exercise.definition: 自适应并发限制器根据已经观察到的服务延迟、利用率或丢弃等反馈，调整同时在途的请求数。它把背压落到请求入口，目的是控制排队；并发上限是请求数，不能当作每秒请求速率。

blocks.text: 在本页讨论的固定基线教学口径中，上限为 L、无排队基线延迟为 R₀、当前延迟为 R，且 R≥R₀>0，排队量估计为 \(\widehat q=\lceil L(1-R_0/R)\rceil\)。这只是反馈信号，不能单凭它推断真实队列。实际更新还要声明阈值、平滑、上下界和基线探测规则，不能凭公式臆造完整控制策略。
L=20、R₀=10 毫秒、R=20 毫秒时，估计排队量为 10。控制器可以按事先设定的策略降低后续准入，但已经进入系统的请求不会因此消失。若 R₀ 失真，估计也会失真；处理时间较长与排队较多需要额外观测来区分。

depth.boundary: The queue estimate is a model, not a measured count of waiting requests. A concurrency cap is distinct from a request-rate quota. This pinned open-source implementation does not establish Netflix's current production configuration.

distinctions.title: Token Bucket / Rate Limiting
distinctions.reason: 令牌桶控制准入速率与突发额度；并发限制控制同时在途数量。相同请求速率可对应不同并发。

introduction.definition: COUNT(*) counts rows, COUNT(expression) ignores NULL values, and COUNT(DISTINCT expression) counts distinct nonnull values. A left join creates a NULL-filled row for an unmatched parent; a one-to-many join can repeat each parent's values.
introduction.example: 例子：左表两个用户，右表只有用户 A 的两条订单。LEFT JOIN 后有三行，COUNT(*)=3，而 COUNT(order_id)=2。若业务要求用户数，应按用户标识计数；不能把联接后的行数直接解释成用户数。

exercise.question: 用自己的话解释：上面的情景为什么是“SQL Aggregation / Join Cardinality”的例子？请指出定义中的关键条件在情景里如何体现，而不是只复述最后的数值。

blocks.text: Group by stable identifiers when different entities can share a name. To return every maximum, compare each result with the maximum aggregate rather than selecting one arbitrary row. Compute percentages with the intended denominator and real-valued division; use ORDER BY when output order matters.

depth.boundary: SQL does not promise row order without ORDER BY. Empty groups, NULL, duplicate join matches, and tied maxima need explicit contracts. Logical query semantics do not determine whether an engine uses hashing, sorting, or an index.

introduction.definition: For a mean, retain (sum, count), combine pairs componentwise, and divide once at the end. An unweighted average of worker means fails when partition sizes differ.
introduction.example: 例子：分片一为 (0,10)，均值 5；分片二只有 (100)，均值 100。直接平均两个均值得 52.5，但正确整体均值为 110/3≈36.67。保存并合并 (sum,count) 可处理不同分片大小。

blocks.text: A combiner must preserve results when applied to different groupings, including when it is skipped. Associativity and commutativity are useful requirements for unordered aggregation; floating-point rounding still depends on evaluation order.

depth.boundary: Aggregation algebra does not by itself guarantee exactly-once side effects, deterministic floating-point results, or balanced partitions.

concepts.title: Mergeable Variance · 流式方差与分片合并

introduction.definition: 可合并方差摘要是在流式计算或分布式分片中，保存样本数、均值和离均差平方和，再由这些摘要计算整体方差的方法。应用问题是数据怎样分批到达、摘要如何合并；总体方差和样本方差的定义仍使用共同的统计基础。
introduction.example: 分片 A 为 1、3，摘要是 (2,2,2)；B 为 5，摘要是 (1,5,0)。合并得均值 3、M₂=8，总体方差为 8/3，样本方差为 4。直接平均两片的方差会漏掉分片均值之间的差异。摘要只需固定大小存储，但浮点合并次序仍可能带来微小舍入差。

exercise.definition: 可合并方差摘要是在流式计算或分布式分片中，保存样本数、均值和离均差平方和，再由这些摘要计算整体方差的方法。应用问题是数据怎样分批到达、摘要如何合并；总体方差和样本方差的定义仍使用共同的统计基础。
exercise.evidence: 分片 A 为 1、3，摘要是 (2,2,2)；B 为 5，摘要是 (1,5,0)。合并得均值 3、M₂=8，总体方差为 8/3，样本方差为 4。直接平均两片的方差会漏掉分片均值之间的差异。摘要只需固定大小存储，但浮点合并次序仍可能带来微小舍入差。

blocks.text: 摘要为 (n, μ, M₂)，M₂ 是各观测与均值之差的平方和。合并非空摘要 A、B，令 \(n=n_A+n_B\)、\(\Delta=\mu_B-\mu_A\)，则 \(\mu=\mu_A+\Delta n_B/n\)，\(M_2=M_{2,A}+M_{2,B}+\Delta^2n_An_B/n\)。总体方差为 M₂/n；无偏样本方差为 M₂/(n−1)，要求 n>1。空摘要须先单独处理，不能除零。

depth.boundary: Population variance and sample variance use different denominators. Empty input needs an explicit convention. Floating-point overflow and rounding remain possible, and different merge orders can produce slightly different results.

introduction.definition: Serializability requires equivalence to a serial transaction order. External consistency adds the order that clients can observe between non-overlapping transactions.
introduction.example: 例子：客户端已收到事务 T1 提交成功，随后才发起 T2，则外部一致的序列必须把 T1 放在 T2 前。两事务若实际重叠，未必有由客户端先后强制的顺序；不能把“可串行化”自动解释成遵守所有墙钟印象。

exercise.definition: Serializability requires equivalence to a serial transaction order. External consistency adds the order that clients can observe between non-overlapping transactions.

blocks.text: If T1 commits before T2 begins, a consistent snapshot cannot include T2's effects while omitting T1's. Strong reads started after both commits must reflect both; an explicitly historical snapshot can precede them.

depth.boundary: Two independent reads are not automatically one snapshot. Clock timestamps alone do not establish a transaction consistency guarantee.

introduction.definition: For N > 0 eligible requests, B bad requests, and success target S, observed success is 1 − B/N and the allowed bad-event count is N(1 − S). Budget consumption is B/[N(1 − S)] when the denominator is positive.
introduction.example: 例子：窗口有 10000 个合格请求，成功目标 99.9%，允许坏事件数为 10。实际失败 6 次，预算消费 60%。若把超时请求从分母中删掉会改变指标契约，不能只为了让结果达标而排除它们。

exercise.question: 用自己的话解释：上面的情景为什么是“SLI / SLO / Error Budget”的例子？请指出定义中的关键条件在情景里如何体现，而不是只复述最后的数值。

exercise.evidence: 例子：窗口有 10000 个合格请求，成功目标 99.9%，允许坏事件数为 10。实际失败 6 次，预算消费 60%。若把超时请求从分母中删掉会改变指标契约，不能只为了让结果达标而排除它们。

blocks.text: Define eligible events, observation window, and measurement location before calculating the ratio. A request-based budget and a time-based availability budget have different denominators.

depth.boundary: A request error fraction cannot be converted directly into outage duration. An SLO target alone is not an SLA with contractual consequences.

distinctions.title: Latency Budget · 延迟预算
distinctions.reason: 错误预算是目标窗口内允许的失败额度；延迟预算分配一次链路的耗时，不能混用预算单位。

introduction.definition: For capacity C, rate r, elapsed time Δt, and previous credit b, refill to min(C, b + rΔt). Admit a unit-cost request only when this balance is at least one, then subtract one.
introduction.example: 例子：容量 5、补充速率每秒 2、当前余额 1，经过 2 秒后补到 min(5,1+4)=5。连续六个单位成本请求中可立即放行五个，第六个应按规则等待或拒绝；这不是对同时在途请求数的限制。

exercise.question: 用自己的话解释：上面的情景为什么是“Token Bucket / Rate Limiting”的例子？请指出定义中的关键条件在情景里如何体现，而不是只复述最后的数值。
exercise.definition: For capacity C, rate r, elapsed time Δt, and previous credit b, refill to min(C, b + rΔt). Admit a unit-cost request only when this balance is at least one, then subtract one.
exercise.evidence: 例子：容量 5、补充速率每秒 2、当前余额 1，经过 2 秒后补到 min(5,1+4)=5。连续六个单位成本请求中可立即放行五个，第六个应按规则等待或拒绝；这不是对同时在途请求数的限制。

blocks.text: Retain fractional credit and update the timestamp on each refill. Shared buckets need atomic refill-and-consume decisions; independent replica buckets do not enforce one global quota.

depth.boundary: Rate, concurrent in-flight work, and queue size are different limits. A token bucket is not a guarantee of uniform spacing between requests.

distinctions.title: Adaptive Concurrency · 服务并发上限的反馈控制
distinctions.reason: 令牌桶控制准入速率与突发额度；并发限制控制同时在途数量。相同请求速率可对应不同并发。

introduction.definition: Closed allows calls and records outcomes. Open rejects locally until the recovery policy permits a transition. Half-open allows limited trial calls before restoring normal traffic or reopening.
introduction.example: 例子：约定连续 3 次失败后打开熔断，之后本地拒绝调用；过 10 秒允许一个 half-open 探测。探测成功才按约定恢复流量，失败则回到 open。探测规则应固定，不能让所有请求同时变成试探而压垮恢复中的服务。

exercise.question: 用自己的话解释：上面的情景为什么是“Circuit Breaker”的例子？请指出定义中的关键条件在情景里如何体现，而不是只复述最后的数值。
exercise.definition: Closed allows calls and records outcomes. Open rejects locally until the recovery policy permits a transition. Half-open allows limited trial calls before restoring normal traffic or reopening.

blocks.text: Choose explicit failure thresholds, observation windows, timeout behavior, and recovery criteria. Concurrent callers must coordinate probe admission to avoid releasing a new burst into a failing service.

depth.boundary: A circuit breaker does not make retries safe, replace a timeout, or enforce a request-rate quota. Local rejections are not downstream failures.

introduction.definition: A version check such as If-Match rejects a stale replacement. After a conflict, reread the current state and recompute the intended change before retrying.
introduction.example: 例子：两个客户端都读到余额版本 7，A 更新后版本变为 8，B 使用 If-Match:7 的覆盖请求应冲突。B 需读取最新状态并重新判断业务条件，而不是把旧值盲目重试到成功。

exercise.question: 用自己的话解释：上面的情景为什么是“Optimistic Concurrency / Conditional Writes”的例子？请指出定义中的关键条件在情景里如何体现，而不是只复述最后的数值。

blocks.text: A state predicate can enforce a local invariant directly, such as stock >= requested quantity before subtracting stock in the same atomic operation.

depth.boundary: A separate read and write do not provide an atomic condition. Conditional mutation alone does not deduplicate repeated business requests or establish a multi-item transaction.

introduction.definition: A lost response leaves the caller uncertain whether an operation committed. Retrying a decrement can apply the change twice even if every individual decrement is atomic.
introduction.example: 例子：操作 K 要扣减 10，服务器已扣但响应丢失。客户端用同一 K 和相同内容重试，应返回同一次操作结果，不能再扣 10；若复用 K 却把金额改为 20，应报告冲突，而不是静默当作同一请求。

exercise.question: 用自己的话解释：上面的情景为什么是“Idempotency / Safe Retries”的例子？请指出定义中的关键条件在情景里如何体现，而不是只复述最后的数值。
exercise.definition: A lost response leaves the caller uncertain whether an operation committed. Retrying a decrement can apply the change twice even if every individual decrement is atomic.

blocks.text: Bind an idempotency key to the request intent. Coordinate recording that key, applying the mutation, and retaining its result so duplicate submissions return the earlier outcome. Define key scope, retention, and behavior for the same key with different parameters.

depth.boundary: A timeout does not prove failure. A stock predicate, transport retry, FIFO delivery, or expiring cache entry alone does not guarantee one business effect.

applications.title: Idempotent Processing · 成交与订单的幂等处理
applications.reason: 把安全重试应用于重复执行回报，协调成交身份、现金持仓更新、持久化和崩溃恢复。

introduction.definition: If A1 precedes A2 and B1 precedes B2, six complete interleavings respect these two constraints: choose the two A positions from four slots.
introduction.example: 例子：A 组顺序 A1→A2，B 组顺序 B1→B2，则 A1、B1、B2、A2 是合法交错，A2、A1、B1、B2 则违反 A 组顺序。每组 FIFO 没有定义跨组的唯一全局次序，去重又是独立要求。

exercise.question: 用自己的话解释：上面的情景为什么是“Message Ordering / FIFO Groups”的例子？请指出定义中的关键条件在情景里如何体现，而不是只复述最后的数值。
exercise.definition: If A1 precedes A2 and B1 precedes B2, six complete interleavings respect these two constraints: choose the two A positions from four slots.
exercise.evidence: 例子：A 组顺序 A1→A2，B 组顺序 B1→B2，则 A1、B1、B2、A2 是合法交错，A2、A1、B1、B2 则违反 A 组顺序。每组 FIFO 没有定义跨组的唯一全局次序，去重又是独立要求。

blocks.text: Choose grouping keys that match the business invariant, then process effects in group order. Delivery, handler completion, visibility timeouts, and duplicate effects require separate reasoning.

depth.boundary: FIFO delivery does not serialize arbitrary asynchronous side effects. A mathematical set of valid schedules does not promise that a queue implements every schedule.

introduction.definition: In a clockwise ring, a key belongs to the first token at or after its hash, with wraparound. A sorted token array supports this lookup with binary search.
introduction.example: 例子：环上的节点令牌为 20、60、90，键哈希 50 归到顺时针首个令牌 60。加入令牌 40 后，哈希 30 的键从 60 转到 40，哈希 50 仍归 60。迁移范围由环区间决定，并非所有键重新分配。

exercise.question: 用自己的话解释：上面的情景为什么是“Consistent Hashing”的例子？请指出定义中的关键条件在情景里如何体现，而不是只复述最后的数值。

blocks.text: Inserting a token transfers the interval from the previous token, exclusive, to the new token, inclusive. Virtual tokens can improve balance; replication must select distinct physical owners when required.

depth.boundary: Limited remapping does not imply equal load, automatic data migration, or consistency during reconfiguration. One hot key can remain a bottleneck.

introduction.definition: Coalescing groups neighboring lane accesses into memory transactions. Under the stated 32-byte segment model, 32 aligned four-byte contiguous loads touch four segments; a one-word shift touches five.
introduction.example: 例子：32 个线程读取连续、对齐的四字节元素，共 128 字节，在简化的 32 字节段模型下触及 4 段。整体错开四字节可能触及 5 段；真实硬件还需核对事务与缓存规则，不能把这个教学段数当所有 GPU 的固定性能倍数。

exercise.question: 用自己的话解释：上面的情景为什么是“GPU Coalescing / Scan / Reduction”的例子？请指出定义中的关键条件在情景里如何体现，而不是只复述最后的数值。

blocks.text: A work-efficient exclusive scan has O(n) work and O(log n) dependency depth. A reduction combines inputs into a total. Participation masks and synchronization are part of correctness; floating-point results can change with the reduction tree.

depth.boundary: Operation count and dependency depth do not predict GPU wall time. Transaction rules depend on architecture, and warp masks do not supply values for absent lanes.

introduction.definition: In cache-aside, a reader can miss, read an old database value, pause, and refill after a writer commits and deletes the cache entry. Deleting after the database write does not eliminate that interleaving.
introduction.example: 例子：读者从数据库拿到旧值 1 后暂停；写者提交新值 2 并删除缓存；随后读者恢复，把旧值 1 填回缓存。仅仅“先写库再删缓存”仍可能产生这个交错，需要按版本、租约或明确失效协议处理。

exercise.definition: In cache-aside, a reader can miss, read an old database value, pause, and refill after a writer commits and deletes the cache entry. Deleting after the database write does not eliminate that interleaving.
exercise.evidence: 例子：读者从数据库拿到旧值 1 后暂停；写者提交新值 2 并删除缓存；随后读者恢复，把旧值 1 填回缓存。仅仅“先写库再删缓存”仍可能产生这个交错，需要按版本、租约或明确失效协议处理。

blocks.text: Grant a per-key fill token and invalidate it on deletion. Check the token atomically when accepting a fill. A delayed reader with an invalid token cannot repopulate that entry with its old value.

depth.boundary: This lease protects the illustrated stale-fill race. It is not a CPU cache-coherence protocol, a normal TTL, or a proof of globally serializable database and cache reads.

introduction.definition: Initialize d[i][i] = 0, direct edges to their minimum weight, and missing edges to infinity. For each intermediate vertex k, update d[i][j] = min(d[i][j], d[i][k] + d[k][j]) for every i and j.
introduction.example: 例子：有 A→B=3、B→C=4、A→C=10。当中间点为 B 时，A 到 C 更新为 min(10,3+4)=7。初始化对角线为 0，缺边为无穷；发现可达负环时，不能把受影响路径当作有限最短路。

exercise.question: 用自己的话解释：上面的情景为什么是“Floyd–Warshall / All-pairs Shortest Paths”的例子？请指出定义中的关键条件在情景里如何体现，而不是只复述最后的数值。
exercise.definition: Initialize d[i][i] = 0, direct edges to their minimum weight, and missing edges to infinity. For each intermediate vertex k, update d[i][j] = min(d[i][j], d[i][k] + d[k][j]) for every i and j.
exercise.evidence: 例子：有 A→B=3、B→C=4、A→C=10。当中间点为 B 时，A 到 C 更新为 min(10,3+4)=7。初始化对角线为 0，缺边为无穷；发现可达负环时，不能把受影响路径当作有限最短路。

blocks.text: Keep k as the outer loop so each stage has a complete intermediate-vertex meaning. The algorithm uses O(V³) time and O(V²) storage for V vertices. A small alphabet of directed character conversions is a natural application.

depth.boundary: Unreachable pairs remain infinite and must not be treated as free conversions. Negative cycles can make finite shortest-path costs undefined for affected pairs.

introduction.definition: Initialize degrees and enqueue every vertex below the threshold. Removing a vertex reduces each surviving neighbor's degree; enqueue a neighbor when it becomes ineligible. Queue processing with adjacency lists takes O(V + E) time and O(V + E) total storage.
introduction.example: 例子：三角形 A、B、C 加一条 B→D 的无向尾边，求 2-core 时先删除度为 1 的 D，留下三角形。阈值升到 3 时，删除 A、C 后会连锁使 B 也不合格；必须递归更新剩余度数。

exercise.question: 用自己的话解释：上面的情景为什么是“Graph Core / Degree Peeling”的例子？请指出定义中的关键条件在情景里如何体现，而不是只复述最后的数值。
exercise.definition: Initialize degrees and enqueue every vertex below the threshold. Removing a vertex reduces each surviving neighbor's degree; enqueue a neighbor when it becomes ineligible. Queue processing with adjacency lists takes O(V + E) time and O(V + E) total storage.
exercise.evidence: 例子：三角形 A、B、C 加一条 B→D 的无向尾边，求 2-core 时先删除度为 1 的 D，留下三角形。阈值升到 3 时，删除 A、C 后会连锁使 B 也不合格；必须递归更新剩余度数。

blocks.text: Any feasible induced subgraph with minimum degree at least k survives every removal: a vertex currently below k cannot belong to such a subgraph. This invariant proves both the pruning rule and the maximality of the remainder. A required vertex removed during peeling makes a constrained planting problem impossible.

depth.boundary: Use current degrees after removals. Core membership differs from connected-component membership; even a 2-core can contain a bridge joining two cyclic regions.

introduction.definition: For n points (x_i, y_i), retain Sx = Σx_i, Sy = Σy_i, and Q = Σ(x_i² + y_i²). At query (a, b), the total squared distance is n(a² + b²) − 2aSx − 2bSy + Q.
introduction.example: 例子：两点为 (0,0)、(2,0)，有 n=2、Sx=2、Sy=0、Q=4。查询 (1,1)，平方距离总和为 2×2−2×1×2+4=4，和逐点算出的 2+2 一致。若改问普通距离，不能再套用这个平方展开。

exercise.question: 用自己的话解释：上面的情景为什么是“Squared-distance Sums / Coordinate Moments”的例子？请指出定义中的关键条件在情景里如何体现，而不是只复述最后的数值。
exercise.definition: For n points (x_i, y_i), retain Sx = Σx_i, Sy = Σy_i, and Q = Σ(x_i² + y_i²). At query (a, b), the total squared distance is n(a² + b²) − 2aSx − 2bSy + Q.
exercise.evidence: 例子：两点为 (0,0)、(2,0)，有 n=2、Sx=2、Sy=0、Q=4。查询 (1,1)，平方距离总和为 2×2−2×1×2+4=4，和逐点算出的 2+2 一致。若改问普通距离，不能再套用这个平方展开。

blocks.text: Build these moments in O(n) time and evaluate q two-dimensional queries in O(q) time, using O(1) aggregate state. With modular output, reduce the expanded expression consistently and use arithmetic wide enough for every product.

depth.boundary: The expansion is for squared distances. It does not give the sum of ordinary Euclidean distances. Coordinates and aggregate products can exceed safe integer ranges even when each coordinate fits individually.
